parks.name: Fort George Canyon Park
parks.location:
There is no access to the park from Red Rock Road East. Only access the Park from Hwy 16 West via Blackwater Road.
A 4.8 km trail provides access to the west side of the river. The trailhead is located off West Lake Road, 24.5 km from Prince George via Highway 16 west and Blackwater Road. The trailhead and first part of the trail remain under Ministry of Forests jurisdiction. From the edge of the plateau down to the river, the trail is in the park. The park is not road or trail accessible from the east side.
Directions from Prince George: take Highway 16 west to the Blackwater Road. Turn left onto the Blackwater Road and follow it for 11.3 km and turn left onto the West Lake Road. Follow the West Lake Road for 9.7 km and turn left onto an unnamed road. Follow this road for approximately 3 km to a parking lot. The hiking trail is approximately 4.8 km to Fort George Canyon.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area located at the trailhead parking lot.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets located at the trailhead parking lot. There are no flush toilets.

parks.name: Fort Nelson River Ecological Reserve
parks.location: On the west bank of Fort Nelson River, 20km north east of Fort Nelson.

parks.name: Fossli Park
parks.location:
Fossli Park is situated on the south side of Stirling Arm on Sproat Lake, west of Port Alberni on Vancouver Island. Access is by boat or an approximately 30 minute walk from the Stirling Arm Mainline, a private logging road.
Travel through Port Alberni on the way to Tofino and turn left on the first McCoy Lake Road access. Travel approximately 6.5 km and then turn left on Stirling Arm Drive for about 3 km. Turn left onto Ash Main gravel road for 0.9 km. At the Stirling Arm Mainline intersection turn right and travel 4 km. Just before the bridge you’ll find a pullout where you can park. An old logging road from the parking lot leads to the trail that will take you to Sproat Lake. The closest community is Port Alberni.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: A picnic table and pit toilet are located at the lake. A beautiful 30 minute trail leads through second-growth forest to an old homestead site on Sproat Lake. Here visitors can relax on the level grassy area or pebble beach and enjoy the lovely views of Sproat Lake.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: A pit toilet is located at the lake, approximately 30 minutes from the parking area.

parks.name: Foster Arm Protected Area
parks.location: Located on the north side of Foster Creek, and on the west side of Kinbasket Lake. This is a very remote area. The closest community is Valemount.

parks.name: Francis Point Park
parks.location: Located approximately 35km northwest of Sechelt in Pender Harbour on the Sunshine Coast.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are pit toilets available in the day-use area.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: The park offers a day-use and picnicking area.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Francois Lake Park
parks.location:
Located at the east end of Francois Lake, Francois Lake Park is approximately 12 km from Highway 16, southwest of Fraser Lake.
From Fraser Lake, head west on Hwy 16 for 3.3 km and turn left onto the Francois Lake Road. Follow this for 7.2 km and turn left onto the Nithi Road. Follow this for 1.8 km and turn right onto Dahlgren Road. Follow this road for 4.4 km around the east end of Francois Lake to the campsite.
From Burns Lake, drive east along Hwy 16 to Endako. On the east side of Endako, head south on the Endako Mine Road to the Francois Lake Road. Turn left on this road, follow it through Glennanan, over the Stellako River, and 2.75 km further to the Nithi Road. See the directions above for Fraser Lake for the rest.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Day-use/picnic areas are available at Sawmill Point and Black Point.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit toilets are provided in the campground. There are no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: A gravel boat launch is available at Sawmill Point. Public boat launches are available at each of the public ferry landings outside the park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are permitted in fire rings. Please bring your own firewood. You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small. Be prepared to bring a portable stove for cooking.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Fraser River Breaks Park
parks.location: The park is located approximately 12 kilometres north of Williams Lake.

parks.name: Fraser River Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 6km west of Chilliwack.

parks.name: Fraser River Park
parks.location: The park is located on the west bank of the Fraser River, on Highway 97 south, approximately 35 km from Prince George.

parks.name: Fred Antoine Park
parks.location: This park is located approximately 25 km northwest of Lillooet.

parks.name: French Bar Creek Park
parks.location: The park is located approximately 60 kilometres north of Lillooet.

parks.name: French Beach Park
parks.location:
French Beach Park is on the west coast of southern Vancouver Island. The park can be accessed via Highway 14, 20km west of Sooke. Directional signs are posted. The park is located approximately 11km from Jordan River.
The nearest communities are Sooke, Jordan River, Port Renfrew, and Victoria.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
There is a sani-station is available at this park, subject to freezing conditions. Facilities are located alongside Highway 14, west of the park entrance.
The sani-dump is closed during the winter season, due to freezing temperatures.
Sani-station use fee: $5 per discharge

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. Campfire rings are provided at each campsite, as well as communal rings in the day-use area. Firewood can be purchased from the park operator.
Fires are not permitted on the beach.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act ). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a large, grassy day-use and picnic area with picnic tables, fire rings, fresh water taps, and pit toilets. The day-use area is located next to the sand and gravel beach.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit toilets are located throughout French Beach Park. There are no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: There is a playground available at this park.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
Cold-water taps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season.
Drinking Water System Report: French Beach [PDF]

parks.name: Gabriola Sands Park
parks.location: Gabriola Sands Park is located on the northwest side of Gabriola Island on an isthmus dividing Taylor Bay and Pilot Bay. Access to Gabriola Island is via BC Ferries from Nanaimo on southern Vancouver Island, a 20 minute ferry ride. From the ferry terminal on Gabriola, turn left on Taylor Bay Road and follow until you see signs for Gabriola Sands Park, located on Decourcy Drive. The park is also accessible by boat. Boaters can reference marine chart #3458 for more information on this area.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Gabriola Sands Park has a day-use and picnic area with picnic tables, pit toilets, two sandy beaches, a parking lot and a playing field. There is also a cold-water hand pump (water must be boiled, filtered or treated prior to consumption).

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has two pit toilets. One on Taylor Bay beach and the other on Pilot Bay beach.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Galiano Island Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 2km south east of the settlement of North Galiano in the Gulf Islands.

parks.name: Gamble Creek Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Found 23km south east of Prince Rupert.

parks.name: Garden Bay Marine Park
parks.location: The park is located 30 km from Sechelt, on the Sechelt Peninsula. Follow Highway 101 north past Madeira Park; turn left on Garden Bay Road. At Garden Bay Lake keep left and drive approximately 2 km to Claydon Road. Pender Harbour includes the following communities: Garden Bay, Medeira Park, Irvines Landing.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: There is a water tap in the day-use area. Boil water advisory.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for the day-use area.

parks.name: Garibaldi Park
parks.location:
There are five park access points along Highway 99 (the Sea to Sky Highway) between Squamish and Pemberton. We recommend taking a vehicle to these access points as the trailheads are between 2 km and 16 km off Highway 99.
Park access points (south to north):
Diamond Head
Black Tusk/Garibaldi Lake (Rubble Creek)
Cheakamus Lake
Singing Pass
Wedgemount Lake
Nearby communities include Whistler and Brackendale.
Transportation to the park is provided by Parkbus.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
All picnic areas in the park are accessible by hiking in, and they have pit toilets. Day-use cooking shelters are available at Red Heather, Garibaldi Lake, and Taylor Meadows. Camping is not allowed in the shelters.
Diamond Head
Red Heather day-use shelter offers two picnic tables, counters with a wash sink, two propane burners, a wood stove (winter only), and pit toilet facilities. Elfin Lakes offers two outdoor picnic tables, a day-use shelter with two picnic tables, counters with two wash sinks, and pit toilet facilities.
Learn more
Black Tusk/Garibaldi Lake
Garibaldi Lake offers four day-use shelters with two picnic tables each, counters, wash sinks, and pit toilet facilities. Taylor Meadows offers two day-use shelters, each with two picnic tables, counters, a wash sink, and pit toilet facilities.
Learn more
Cheakamus Lake
You can use various scenic spots around the lake to picnic in a natural setting. Pit toilet facilities are provided. There are no picnic tables.
Learn more
Singing Pass
This area offers plenty of room to picnic in a beautiful alpine setting. Pit toilet facilities are provided. There are no picnic tables.
Learn more
Wedgemount Lake
There is a small shelter at Wedgemount Lake with limited seating. Although this shelter is not recommended for picnicking, there is plenty of room outside to picnic in a beautiful alpine setting. Pit toilet facilities are provided. There are no picnic tables.
Learn more

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Water is available in lakes and streams. All drinking water must be filtered, boiled, or otherwise treated before drinking. Wash all dishes and conduct personal hygiene at least 30 m from the water source. Dispose of wastewater in a shelter sink or in campground pit toilets.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail:
Pit toilets are located at all designated camping areas, day-use sites, and trailheads. Please bring your own toilet paper.
Do not place garbage in the toilets. There are no garbage facilities, so please pack out what you pack in.

parks.name: Gibson Marine Park
parks.location: Gibson Marine Park is located in the central portion of Clayoquot Sound, north of Tofino on the west coast of Vancouver Island. The park is located on the south side of Flores Island and is accessible only by boat from Tofino. Boaters can reference marine chart #3674 and #3673 for more information on this area. Water taxis from Tofino and Ahousaht offer access to the park via the Village of Ahousaht. Nearby communities include: Tofino, Ahousaht, Hotsprings Village.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: A pit toilet is located at the most easterly beach in the park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While small fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you do have a fire use small pieces of wood that will burn completely. Build your fires below the high tide mark. and do not burn live wood, burn drift wood instead. Never build fires next to or near beach logs, this could lead to a forest fire. Never leave your fire unattended and practice “
Leave No Trace” camping ethics.

parks.name: Gilnockie Creek Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 34km south by south east of Moyie, East Kootenay District.

parks.name: Gilnockie Park
parks.location: The park is located 5 km north of the US border, between Moyie Lake and Elko Park access is by seasonal logging roads from Highway 3 at Moyie Lake via Teepee Creek, Yahk River and Ward Creek (approximately 35 km). The park can also be accessed from Lake Koocanusa at Kikomun Creek Park via Plumbob Creek, Gold Creek and Caven Creek (approximately 35 km) or via Gold Creek, Bloom Creek and Ward Creek (approximately 40 km). The closest community is Cranbrook.

parks.name: Gilpin Grasslands Park
parks.location: Located 9 km east of the municipality of Grand Forks, and encompasses the grassland hills on the north side, and the Kettle River on the south side of Highway 3.

parks.name: Gingietl Creek Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Found 35km upstream from mouth of Nass River, 85km north by north west of Terrace.

parks.name: Giscome Portage Trail Protected Area
parks.location: Giscome Portage Trail is located 40 km North of Prince George and 6 km off Highway 97 North on Mitchell Road. There is also another access point where the trail comes out at Barney Creek Road (close to Summit Lake), which is 48 km North of Prince George on Highway 97. The closest communities are Prince George and Bear Lake.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are pit toilets at the Huble Homestead Regional Park Site.

parks.name: Gitnadoiks River Park
parks.location: The park is located approximately 50 km west of Terrace on the south side of the Skeena River. The closest boat launch is located at Exchamsiks River Park. The closest communities are Terrace (50 km east of the park), Port Edward (80 km west of the park) and Prince Rupert (90 km west of the park).

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: No firewood or fire rings are available. If you have to make a fire, keep it minimal, make sure it is extinguished, please spread ashes and rocks about. Use only dead and down wood for fires.

parks.name: Gitnadoiks River Protected Area
parks.location: The protected area is located approximately 50km west of Terrace on the south side of the Skeena River. The closest boat launch is located at Exchamsiks River Park. The closest communities are Terrace (50km east of the protected area), Port Edward (80km west of the protected area) and Prince Rupert (90km west of the protected area).

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: No firewood or fire rings are available. If you have to make a fire, keep it minimal, make sure it is extinguished, please spread ashes and rocks about.

parks.name: Gitxaała Nii Łuutiksm/Kitkatla Conservancy
parks.location:
The conservancy is located adjacent to Kitkatla/Gitxaała and 55 km southwest of Prince Rupert. The communities of Oona River and Hunts Inlet, located on Porcher Island, are also nearby. Access to the conservancy is primarily by boat and there are a number of sheltered inlets suitable for anchoring. For information on ferry and float plane schedules contact the Gitxaała Nation at 250-848-2214.
Reference: Marine Charts #3987
Prince Rupert Visitor Centre
100 First Avenue West
Prince Rupert, British Columbia V8J 1A8
Phone: 250-624-5637
Fax: 250-627-8009
Toll-free: 1-800-667-1994
visitprincerupert.com
prinfo@citytel.net

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood and campfire rings are not provided. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of campfires and using campstoves instead.
If you must have a fire, please have it in the intertidal area, burn only dead and down wood, be sure to fully extinguish the fire when done and spread out the ashes and rocks. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Gladstone Park
parks.location:
Gladstone Park is located approximately 20 km northeast of Grand Forks on Hwy 3 at the north end of Christina Lake in the Monashee Mountains. The most common accesses to the park are via the Texas Creek campground and by boat from Christina Lake.
The campground is 5 km east of Christina Lake on Hwy 3; turn onto East Lake Drive and follow 4 km to the 63 site campground at the end of the road.
There is rough 4WD access to Xenia Lake, 22 km up the North Fork Rd from Grand Forks to Miller Creek Rd. Turn right and go about 4 km. Look for a small road on the left marked with a white deactivated road sign that leads to the lake.
There is also access to the Mt. Gladstone trailhead from Hwy 3 and the abandoned CPR railway at Paulson, the Mt. Faith trailhead from the Burrell Forest Service Road, and Peter Lake from Dog Creek Road.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Visitors can use Christina Lake day-use area, located 10 km from the park.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park offers nine flush toilets and five pit toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps are located throughout the Texas Creek campground. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail:
There is a paved boat launch available at Texas Creek. It is open year-round though ice will limit use. It is located on Litchy Road between pieces of private property, 500 m before the campground. There is a wide paved road with a single lane turn-around running off one side. The road slopes down to a double wide concrete ramp with two docks made of interlocking plastic blocks.
There is a payphone and an information shelter beside the dock. Parking is across East Lake Road in two large gravel parking lots. There is one pit toilet by the parking lots.
Please note: There is no long term trailer storage permitted at the Texas Creek boat launch. Any trailers left in the parking lot for more than 14 days per calendar year are subject to removal and fines.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: Hot showers are available in the campground. There is no additional fee for their use. Shower facilities are for campground visitors only.

parks.operating_note: Day-use area, boat launch, and trails are accessible year-round, though snow may affect access.

parks.name: Gladys Lake Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located at Eaglenest Range, 65km east by south east of Iskut.

parks.name: Goat Cove Conservancy
parks.location: The conservancy is located approximately 25 kilometres northeast of Klemtu and 85 kilometres north of Bella Bella.

parks.name: Goat Range Park
parks.location: This park is situated in the Selkirk Mountains, between Slocan and Kootenay lakes at the south end, and between Arrow Lakes and Duncan Lake at the north end.

parks.name: God's Pocket Marine Park
parks.location: God’s Pocket Marine Park is located on the north side of Goletas Channel approximately 10 km northwest of Port Hardy on northern Vancouver Island. The park can be accessed by boat or float plane (to a lodge nearby) from Port Hardy. Boaters can reference marine chart #3549 (Queen Charlotte Strait western section) for more information on this area.

parks.name: Goguka Creek Protected Area
parks.location: Goguka Creek Protected Area is located in the Jackfish Creek/Prophet River area alongside the Alaska Highway at km 441, (mile post 274). The closest communities are Fort Nelson and Prophet River.

parks.name: Gold Muchalat Park
parks.location: The park is located on the Gold and Muchalat Rivers, approximately 15 km northeast of the town of Gold River on north-central Vancouver Island. Access is via the road to Woss Lake from Gold River. Other logging roads run through the park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you must use a campfire, please practice “Leave No Trace” camping ethics. Please be responsible with your fire and be aware of fire closures.

parks.name: Golden Ears Park
parks.location:
Golden Ears Park lies in the Coast Mountains, 11 km north of Maple Ridge on the north side of the Fraser River. Access to the park is by vehicle via Dewdney Trunk Road through Maple Ridge.
If heading west, turn right onto 232nd Street. Or, if heading east, turn left onto 232nd Street. Then turn right onto Fern Crescent at the traffic circle and follow the road into the park. The campgrounds are approximately 11 km north of the park entrance.
The campground gatehouse is at 17801 Golden Ears Park Campground. The communities, towns, and cities closest to this park are Maple Ridge, Mission, and Pitt Meadows.
Parkbus
This park is serviced by Parkbus, an environmentally friendly and affordable transportation service from downtown Vancouver to select BC Parks. To find out more about Parkbus, and see routes and schedules, check the Parkbus website.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Golden Ears Park features a trail specifically designed for wheelchair accessibility. The Spirea Universal Access Trail.
Wheelchair-accessible toilets are available at all campgrounds and in the Alouette (South Beach) day-use area. There are wheelchair-accessible showers at Gold Creek and Alouette campgrounds.
Four campsites at the Gold Creek campground are paved. Wheelchair access to the beach is also available from parking lot two at the Alouette (South Beach) day-use area.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail:
Golden Ears Park features a four-lane, cement-surface boat launch at the south end of Alouette Lake. The park also offers boat-accessible camping along the lake. For information, see marine-accessible camping.
Vehicles and trailers can be parked overnight at the boat launch parking lot. There is no nearby marina to moor boats overnight. We do not recommend leaving your boat in the water overnight due to the risk of theft.
Outside peak season, the water level in Alouette Lake can vary considerably due to water management by BC Hydro. Be especially careful when the water is low. Watch for submerged stumps and other obstacles.
Day-use passes
You may need a day-use vehicle pass to access Alouette Lake boat launch during peak season. If you have a valid reservation for overnight camping, you do not need a day-use pass. For details, please visit the day-use passes page.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are not allowed in the backcountry and marine sites of Golden Ears Park. Please use a portable fuel stove for cooking.
Campfires are only allowed in fire rings at:
Alouette, Gold Creek, and North Beach campgrounds
Alouette, Golden Ears, and Woodlands group campsites
Do not gather firewood from anywhere else in the park. This is an offence under the Park Act. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals, and it adds valuable organic matter to the soil.
You can buy firewood in the park from the park operator. If you bring your own firewood, please buy it locally, to avoid introducing invasive species. To learn more, visit Buy Local, Burn Local.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
Cold-water taps are available in Alouette Campground, Gold Creek Campground and at the West Canyon Trailhead. Taps are shut off in the winter. Unfortunately, there is no water available at North Beach Campground.
Drinking water from taps is tested on a regular basis. For water testing information, please contact the park operator (see the contact section below for how to get in touch). You can download recent reports below:
Annual Drinking Water System Report 2025: Park headquarters Water System [PDF]
Annual Drinking Water System Report 2025: Gold Creek/Aloutette Water System [PDF]
Annual Drinking Water System Report 2025: South Beach Water System [PDF]
Annual Drinking Water System Report 2025: Rolley Lake Water System [PDF]
All backcountry drinking water should be filtered, boiled, or otherwise treated before use. Wash all dishes and conduct personal hygiene at least 30 m from any water source.
There is no permanent source of water past Alder Flats. Depending on the conditions, water can be melted from the snowfield in the northern shadow of the peak.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
There are four day-use beach areas on the shoreline of Alouette Lake in Golden Ears Park. All four are ideal for picnicking.
Day-use passes
You may need a day-use vehicle pass to access Golden Ears Park during peak season. If you have a valid reservation for overnight camping, you do not need a day-use pass. For details, please visit the day-use passes page.
Alouette (South Beach)
This vehicle-accessible area is at kilometre seven on the main parkway. It is open in summer with full services (flush toilets, drinking water taps, change house). In winter, it is open with minimal services (pit toilets only).
We provide picnic tables in this area. Some of these picnic tables come with barbeque attachments. Please bring your own briquettes and barbeques as fires are not allowed.
There is a sand-and-gravel beach with a seasonal roped-off swimming area. No lifeguards are on duty at this beach (or anywhere in BC Parks). Canoe, kayak, and pedalboat rentals are available.
A special area for leashed dogs is between the boat launch and the canoe rental shop. Unfortunately, dogs are not allowed in the main part of the South Beach day-use area.
Campers Beach
This walk-in area is next to Alouette and Gold Creek campgrounds. Day-use visitors can park in the visitor parking lot beside the ticket booth. Dogs are not allowed in this area.
There is a sand-and-gravel beach, which has a roped-off swimming area during peak season. No lifeguards are on duty. A water tap is available during the summer. Pit toilets are available.
North Beach
This sand-and-gravel beach is next to North Beach Campground. It is accessible on foot from the East Canyon parking lot via the North Beach Trail. There are no lifeguards. Dogs are allowed but must stay on leash. Pit toilets are provided.
Alouette (East Beach)
This area is directly across from South Beach and only accessible by boat. Pit toilets are provided. These are a short distance from the beach at both the north and south ends.
Fires and overnight camping are not allowed at day-use areas in this park. There is no garbage removal at Campers Beach, North Beach, and East Beach. Please bring a garbage bag and pack out your trash.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail:
Pit and flush toilets are available at Alouette and Gold Creek campgrounds and the day-use areas of this park. Only pit toilets are available at North Beach Campground. All flush toilets are closed during the winter. All designated backcountry camping areas and marine campsites have pit toilets.
Toilet paper is not provided in backcountry pit toilets. Never put garbage in the toilets.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: There is a playground near the shower building at the north end of Alouette Campground.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
Golden Ears Park offers a sani-station. You can find this just off the main parkway, close to the campgrounds. It is usually closed from October 16 to March 31.
Fees (per use)
Sani-station$5 (must be paid at the ticket booth)

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: Hot showers are available for no extra cost at the Alouette and Gold Creek campgrounds. There are no showers at North Beach Campground. All shower buildings are closed during the winter.

gate.note: Park gate open April to mid-October, 7 am to 11 pm, and mid-October to March, 7 am to 7 pm. In winter, the access road may be closed due to snow and ice.

parks.operating_note: April to mid-October, 7 am to 11 pm, and mid-October to March, 7 am to 7 pm. In winter, the access road may be closed due to snow and ice.

parks.name: Goldpan Park
parks.location: This park is located on the east bank of the Thompson River adjacent to Hwy 1, 10 km south of Spences Bridge.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: No campfires allowed in the day-use area. Ensure that barbeques or campstoves are used on the ground, not set on picnic tables.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Day-use facilities are located at the entrance to the park adjacent to the highway. There are seven picnic tables. This day-use site overlooks the Thompson River. There is no shade provided at this site.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are four pit toilets located within the campground, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: There is a potable water handpump located next to the information shelter. Water used from the river should be treated or boiled before being consumed.

parks.name: Goldstream Park
parks.location:
Goldstream Provincial Park is located 16km northwest of Victoria on southern Vancouver Island on the Trans Canada Hwy (Hwy #1). There are separate entrances for the main campground, group campsite, and day-use area:
Visitors coming to the campground now must use Amy Road via Westshore Parkway to get to the campground. The Westshore Parkway intersection is just south of the old (now closed) Sooke Lake Road intersection and the first traffic signal after the Spencer Road intersection on Trans Canada Hwy #1.
The entrance to the day-use area is at the junction of Trans Canada Hwy #1 and Finlayson Arm Road.
The entrance to the group campsite is off the Trans Canada Hwy #1 opposite the now closed Sooke Lake Road intersection.
Nearby communities include: Victoria, Langford, Duncan, Colwood, Metchosin, Sooke.

facilities.name: Bike park
facilities.detail:
A children’s bicycle pump track is available for the use and enjoyment of visitors staying in the campground. The pump track is located near the amphitheatre, and near campsites 103-108 and 132-138.
The new bicycle pump track with 240 metres of beginner and intermediate skills trails complete with small obstacles. This new facility provides a safe and controlled environment for kids to get exercise, hone their bike handling skills and have fun.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail:
The playground and children’s bike park are located near the amphitheatre. This area is near campsites #103-108 and #132-138.
Bicycle pump track and skills trails
Goldstream has a new bicycle pump track with 240 metres of beginner and intermediate skills trails complete with small obstacles. This new facility provides a safe and controlled environment for kids to get exercise, hone their bike handling skills and have fun.
Bicycle helmets are mandatory in British Columbia and must be worn by all kids and adults using the pump track and skills trails. Eye protection, gloves and knee and elbow protection are also recommended.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: Hot showers are available at Goldstream Park. They are located in the main campground area.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station/dump is available during the main camping season. The facility is located in the main campground. In the event of freezing temperatures, the sani-dump may be shut down temporarily.
The sani-station use fee is $5 per discharge.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Campground
Goldstream picnic site
Prospector and Goldminer group sites
Visitor centre

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. Campfire rings are provided at each campsite, as well as communal rings in the day use area.
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil. You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit toilets are located throughout the park. Flush toilet buildings are located in the day-use area and main campground.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a large day-use and picnic area with a picnic shelter, wood stove, flush toilets, fire rings, and numerous picnic tables. Nature walks and trails of varying lengths starting at the day-use area offer the opportunity to see some of the park’s more notable features. The Freeman King Visitor Centre can be reached by a short trail from the day-use area parking lot. The centre is open daily, year-round. This is not a reservable facility.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
Cold water taps are located throughout the park in the campground and day-use area. Taps are shut off during the off-season.
Drinking Water System Report 2025 [PDF]

parks.name: Goose Bay Conservancy
parks.location: This conservancy is located approximately 100 kilometres south of Bella Bella, 50 kilometres southwest of Wuikinuxv Village and 485 kilometres north of Vancouver.

parks.name: Goosegrass Creek Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located on the west side of Kinbasket Lake (Mica Reservoir), 20km east of Mica Creek.

parks.name: Gordon Bay Park
parks.location: Gordon Bay Park is located 35km northwest of Duncan on southern Vancouver Island. The park, situated on the shores of Cowichan Lake, is accessed via Hwy #18 off Hwy #1. Travel 26km west on Hwy #18 to Lake Cowichan, then 14km on South Shore Road. Nearby communities include: Honeymoon Bay, Cowichan Lake, Youbou, Duncan, Victoria.

facilities.name: Bike park
facilities.detail: A children’s bike pump track is available for the use and enjoyment of visitors staying in the campground.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a large day-use and picnic area with picnic tables, parking lot, adventure playground, amphitheatre, and flush toilets. The day-use area is a popular spot for local residents, who come to the park to swim and picnic.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit toilets are located throughout the park. Flush toilets are located in the campground and day-use area and are open from April 1 to October 31.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: There are two separate hot shower facilities in this park, located within the campground.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
Cold water taps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season.
Drinking water system reports 2024
Drinking water report: Gordon Bay campground [PDF]
Drinking water report: group site [PDF]
Drinking water report: day-use area [PDF]

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: A number of facilities at this park are wheelchair-accessible, including picnic tables, the main campsites and group campsite, and the shower and flush toilet buildings.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: There is an adventure playground available at the day-use area of this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: A boat launch is located northeast of the day-use parking lot.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfire rings are provided at each campsite but be prepared to bring a portable stove for cooking.
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Gowlland Tod Park
parks.location:
The park is located on the east side of Saanich Inlet on southern Vancouver Island. There are three park accesses:
Tod Inlet access is located near Brentwood Bay, off Wallace Drive.
Mackenzie Bight access is located off Rossdurrance Road, off Willis Point Road.
Caleb Pike access is on Caleb Pike Road, off Millstream Road near Langford. Gowlland Tod Park can also be accessed by boat via Tod Inlet.
The nearby communities are Brentwood Bay, Saanich, Sidney, Langford, Colwood, Victoria.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has three day-use accesses: Tod Inlet, Mackenzie Bight and Caleb Pike. All three areas have pit toilets. Only Tod Inlet and Caleb Pike have picnic tables. Parking lots are available at Mackenzie Bight and Caleb Pike.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has pit toilets located at the Tod Inlet, Mackenzie Bight and Caleb Pike trailheads.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Graham-Laurier Park
parks.location: Graham-Laurier Park lies north of the Peace Arm of Williston Reach and west of the Continental Divide. It is approximately 145 km northwest of Fort St. John. Graham-Laurier is a remote wilderness area. The Halfway/Graham Forest Service road provides the only motorized access to within 10 km of the southeast corner of the park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Keep backcountry fires small.

parks.name: Granby Park
parks.location:
Within the Kootenay-Okanagan Boundary area, this park is located approximately 135 km east of Vernon or 65 km north of Grand Forks. The closest communities are Grand Forks, Lumby, Nakusp and Christina Lake.
Access to the north end of the park is by road off of Highway 6 between Cherryville and Needles. Park visitors should turn south off Highway 6 onto the Mount Scaia Road, 10 km west of Needles. The gravel surfaced Mount Scaia Road is approximately 23 km long and terminates within Granby Park.
Access to the south end of the park is by road off of Highway 3 in Grandforks. Visitors should turn north on North Fork Road. There is 20 km of pavement and 65 km of gravel with the road ending 4 km from Granby Park Boundary. The Bluejoint Lookout road provides access to a trail that leads up to Bluejoint Mountain at the edge of the park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Grayling River Hot Springs Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 67km north east of Muncho Lake.

parks.name: Graystokes Park
parks.location: This park is located 45km northeast of Kelowna. From Highway 97 in Kelowna follow Highway 33 for 23.5km toward Big White Ski Area. Turn left, then take Three Forks Road and cross Mission Creek at 7km. Continue north for 0.5km and turn right onto Greystokes Forest Service Road. Follow this rough road to the park for approximately 10km.

parks.name: Great Glacier Park
parks.location: Great Glacier Park is approximately 120 km southwest of Telegraph Creek. The park’s southwestern end borders Alaska. The only way to access this park is by boat on the Stikine River. The most popular boat launch for accessing Great Glacier Park is in Glenora.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: A pit toilet is available at the Great Glacier Park campground. There are no flush toilets or other pit toilets anywhere in the park. Please bring your own toilet paper, as it is not provided at the campground.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed at the campground, but only in the two fire rings provided. We encourage you to minimize the use of fire and bring a camping stove for cooking. Fires are not allowed anywhere else in the park.
We recommend gathering dead wood from the riverbank just outside the park. Dry wood is very limited near the campground. Also, gathering wood within a BC Park is an offence under the Park Act.

parks.name: Green Inlet Marine Park
parks.location: Green Inlet Marine Park is on the east side of Tolmie Channel across from Princess Royal Island, just west of Fiordland Recreation Area. 196 km south of Prince Rupert. It is accessible by boat only. Refer to Canadian Hydrographic Chart 3738. Supplies are available at Klemtu or Bella Bella.

parks.name: Green Lake Park
parks.location: Access is approximately 16 km northeast of 70 Mile House off Hwy #97 along North Bonaparte Road or approximately 18 km south of Hwy #24 at Lone Butte and follow the signs along Watch Lake Road. The closest communities are 70 Mile House, Lone Butte and 100 Mile House.

facilities.name: Picnic shelters
facilities.detail:
Sunset View and Emerald Bay feature picnic shelters. Sunset View has a locked gate between 10 pm and 8 am. Group picnicking is open in the summer and reservations are available for the Sunset View picnic shelter.
You can make a reservation online at camping.bcparks.ca or by calling 1-800-689-9025 (1-519-858-6161 internationally). For detailed information, see the picnic shelters page.
Group picnicking fee: $35 per group
A $20 fee is added for anyone who is not a B.C. resident. For more information, visit the non-resident fee section of the camping fees page.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Arrowhead
Blue Spring
Emerald Bay
Little Arrowhead
Service Centre
Sunset View

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps and handpumps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season. There are no hose hook-ups for campers and trailers.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator in some parks or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.
You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small. Be prepared to bring a portable stove for cooking.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets located throughout the campgrounds and day-use areas. A flush toilet building is located at the sani-station building.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: Two paved, single-boat launches are located in the park. One is on the southside at Sunset View campground and the other is on the north side at Little Arrowhead picnic site. There is a parking area for vehicles and boat trailers at both places.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail:
Big Toy playground equipment is located at
Sunset View
and
Emerald Bay
campgrounds. Horseshoe pits are available in all three campgrounds. Please bring your own horseshoes.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station and dump is available during the collecting season. The sani-station facilities are located at the junction of North Green Lake Road and North Bonaparte Road, 12 km west of Sunset View campground and 18 km southwest of Emerald Bay.
Sani-station use fee: $5 per discharge

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
Picnic and day-use areas are located at Blue Spring, Little Arrowhead, Emerald Bay, and Sunset View.
Day-use areas at Sunset View and Emerald Bay also feature picnic shelters. Blue Spring, Little Arrowhead, and Sunset View have a locked gate between 10 pm and 8 am.

parks.name: Greenbush Lake Protected Area
parks.location:
Greenbush Lake is located 124 km north of Vernon. Take Hwy 97 to Vernon, then go east on Hwy 6 from for 47 km, through Lumby to Cherryville. At Cherryville, turn north onto Sugar Lake Road. Follow until the paved road ends becoming the gravel Sugar Lake Forest Service Road. Follow past Sugar Lake and along the Shuswap River for 53 km to the protected area. The Forest Service Recreation Site on the northwest side of Greenbush lake is just outside the protected area which surrounds it on the north, east and south sides. The recreation site provides the main access into the protected area.
The closest communities are Cherryville, Lumby and Vernon.
In the winter, backcountry skiers fly by helicopter to Blanket Glacier Chalet, located just east of the Protected Area. The Chalet commissions these flights from Revelstoke. As well, heli-skiing trips in the Protected Area are provided by CMH Revelstoke.

parks.name: Greenstone Mountain Park
parks.location: The park is located approximately 20 km southwest of Kamloops. Access is off Highway # 1 near Cherry Cr. via Greenstone Mountain Forest Service Road, or off of the Logan Lake (Meadow Creek) Road via the Dominic Forest Service Rd., then a service road for the communications tower.

parks.name: Grohman Narrows Park
parks.location: This park is 5 km from the City of Nelson.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Gunboat Harbour Conservancy
parks.location: Gunboat Harbour Conservancy is located approximately 25 kilometres south of Prince Rupert.

parks.name: Gwillim Lake Park
parks.location: This park is located 56 km southeast of Chetwynd. Take Highway 29 south off Highway 97 (paved access).

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: A hand pump is located in the park. The hand pump may be removed during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: An adventure playground is situated in the middle of the campground.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a boat launch complete with turnaround and a large parking area for vehicles with trailers.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Gwyneth Lake Park
parks.location: Located approximately 70 kilometres west of Lillooet and 60 kilometres north of Pemberton, accessed from the Hurley Forest Service Road.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
If visitors require a campfire, keeping the campfire small can conserve firewood and air quality. Do not leave your campfire unattended. Please ensure the campfire is completely extinguished before leaving the area. Be prepared by bringing a portable stove for cooking.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, it is prohibited to gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There is one user maintained pit toilet. Visitors need to bring their own toilet paper.

parks.name: Hai Lake – Mount Herman Park
parks.location:
Hai Lake – Mount Herman park is located about 15 km south of Terrace on the west side of Beam Station Road. Terrace is the closest community to this park and access into this park is by roads and trails. Use NTS Map Sheet #103 I/7 (Lakelse Lake). The Hai Lake trail is accessed via the South Thunderbird Forest Service Road and Herman Lake is accessed via Beam Station Road. For more detailed directions to Hai Lake and Herman Lake, see the Hiking section.
Visitor Information Centre
Terrace Visitor Info Centre
4511 Keith Avenue
Terrace, BC V8G 1K1
Ph. 250-635-4944
Toll Free: 1-877-635-4944
E-Mail: info@visitterrace.com
Website: hellobc.com

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has one pit toilet which is located at Hai Lake.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: The 82 m boardwalk trail and viewing platform (3 m x 3 m) at Herman Lake are wheelchair-accessible.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Please conserve firewood.
While campfires are allowed, there is no firewood available. We encourage visitors to use camp stoves and only have a campfire in emergency situations.

parks.name: Hakai Lúxvbálís Conservancy
parks.location:
Hakai Lúxvbálís Conservancy is located along the B.C. coast, approximately 130 km north of Port Hardy and 115 km southwest of Bella Coola.
Access is via sea or air: chartered boats and chartered or scheduled air services are available from Vancouver, Port Hardy, Bella Bella (Waglisla) and Bella Coola. It is also possible to take the “Discovery Coast Passage” service offered by BC Ferries, which travels between Port Hardy and Bella Coola; the ferries make a stop at Bella Bella (Waglisla), 45 km north of Hakai. The nearest settlement is Namu on the mainland coast, 10 km across Fitz Hugh Sound.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Campfires are allowed but firewood is not provided. Be prepared to bring a portable stove for cooking. If you must have a fire, please burn only dead and down wood, and be sure to extinguish the fire fully. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil so please use it conservatively, if at all. You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small.

parks.name: Haley Lake Ecological Reserve
parks.location: On Vancouver Island, approximately 32km south west of Nanaimo.

parks.name: Halkett Bay Marine Park
parks.location: Halkett Bay Park is located on the southeastern shore of Gambier Island, 15km from Horseshoe Bay. Located 40km from marinas in Vancouver and 10km from Lions Bay, it is well within day-use range of most boaters.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has pit toilets, no flush toilets. There is one pit toilet available near the information kiosk.

parks.name: Hamber Park
parks.location: The park is located 22 km from the trail head parking lot at Sunwapta Falls (Jasper National Park) to the campground at the east of Fortress Lake. The closest communities are Valemount and Jasper, Alberta.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Campfires are permitted in the park, but lightweight stoves are recommended for cooking. Please be extremely careful with fires and only use down and dead wood.

parks.name: Hanna-Tintina Conservancy
parks.location:
Hanna-Tintina Conservancy is located in the vicinity of Meziadin Junction and can be accessed by Highway 37 and 37A.
Stewart: 62.5 kilometres on Highway 37A and 37
Kitwanga Junction: 143 kilometres on Highway 37
Dease Lake: 312 kilometres on Highway 37.
Kitwanga and Stewart are the closest communities.

parks.name: Harbour-Dudgeon Lakes Park
parks.location: Located 175 km northeast of Kamloops, accessed via 44 km of logging roads from the north end of Adams Lake. The closest communities are Kamloops, Clearwater, Vavenby and Chase.

parks.name: Hardy Island Marine Park
parks.location: This park consists of Musket Island and Hardy Island and is strategically situated, being midway from Vancouver, Princess Louisa and Desolation Sound. This park can be approached from either Malaspina Strait or Jervis Inlet via Telescope Passage.

parks.name: Harmony Islands Marine Park
parks.location: This park is situated on the east side of Hotham Island, north of Granville Bay and consists of the southernmost island. The other islands are privately owned and are not a part of the park. Please respect these areas and do not trespass on private property. The closest community is Powell River.

parks.name: Harry Lake Aspen Park
parks.location: This park is situated 40 km west of Cache Creek. To access the park, drive north from Cache Creek on Highway 97, west along Highway 99, south along Hat Creek Road, and then up logging roads along Medicine Creek. A backcountry road map will assist visitors in locating this park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfire should be used only for warming or drying. Be prepared by bringing a portable stove for cooking.
If visitors require a campfire, keeping the campfire small can conserve firewood and air quality. Do not leave your campfire unattended. Please ensure the campfire is completely extinguished before leaving the area.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, it is prohibited to gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Hay River Protected Area
parks.location: Hay River Protected Area is located 15 km from the Alberta border.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Boil or filter all water from streams and rivers.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Campfires are allowed in the park. To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil. Please bring a portable stove for cooking.

parks.name: Haynes' Lease Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Adjacent to the north end of Osoyoos Lake, 6km north by north west of Osoyoos.

parks.name: Heather Lake Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 23km north by north west of Mackenzie.

parks.name: Heather-Dina Lakes Park
parks.location: The Parsnip West Forest Service Road (PWFSR) can be reached from Highway 39 by heading north from the closest community of Mackenzie for approximately 10 km. There are two main entry points into the park, both of which are accessed from the PWFSR. The gravel road is suitable for most two-wheel drive vehicles during the summer, but four-wheel drive vehicles are recommended during wet weather. A sign near the 25 km marker of the PWFSR indicates the turnoff to Heather Lake and the site is located less than 1 km from the turnoff. The Dina Lake site is also marked with a sign and is located approximately 31 km on the PWFSR.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
Heather Lake day-use area
There is one picnic table and a fire-ring located close to the lake near the boat launch. Visitors may also use the camping area for day-use activities.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood is not available to be purchased in the park. You may bring your own wood.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail:
Heather Lake
A small gravel boat launch is available for launching small to medium car top-sized boats.
Dina Lake
A boat launch is available at Dina Lake for launching car-top boats.
A motor restriction is in place:
7.5 kw (10 horse power) or less on Dina Lake #1, and
electric motors only on nearby Dina Lake #2

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

parks.name: Height of the Rockies Park
parks.location:
Height of the Rockies park is adjacent to Banff National Park, Elk Lakes Park, and Peter Lougheed Park in Alberta. There are six major trailheads accessible by summer logging roads:
from Canal Flats on Hwy 93/95 via the Whiteswan and White River roads ( turn east 4.5 km south of Canal Flats)
from Sparwood on Hwy 3 turn north to Elkford, then follow the Elk River road
from Highway 93 from Kootenay National Park, access Settlers Road through to the Palliser and Albert River roads
The park is also accessible by trail routes from Banff National Park, Elk Lakes Park and Peter Lougheed Park.
The community of Elkford is the closest community when accessing Height of the Rockies from the southern portion of the park. Canal Flats and Radium Hot Springs are the closest communities when accessing the park from the west.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: The park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets. There is a pit toilet at Connor Lakes cabin and Queen Mary cabin. Bury human waste in soil at least 15 cm deep and 30 m from water if no toilet is provided.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Fires are allowed but be prepared by bringing a portable stove for cooking. Only have open fires when necessary, keeping them small to conserve firewood.
Fires are prohibited in the Limestone Lakes area and Beatty Lake area to mitigate impacts concerning conservational values.

parks.name: Helliwell Park
parks.location:
Helliwell Park is located on Hornby Island, two short ferry rides from Vancouver Island.
To reach Hornby Island take the Denman Island Ferry from Buckley Bay, off Hwy #19a. From Hwy #19, take the Buckley Bay exit #101. Once on the Denman Island, follow Denman Road to the Hornby Island Ferry terminal. Another 10 minute ferry ride will put you on Hornby Island. From there follow the main road to the Hornby Island CO-OP then turn left following Central Road to St. John’s Point Road to the park. Nearby communities include Hornby Island, Denman Island, Buckley Bay, Fanny Bay, Courtenay, Comox Valley.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are four pit toilets at this park. Three along the trail and one at the parking lot.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: There are no designated picnic facilities at this park. However, benches are located at various spots along the trail. Pit toilets are also located along the trail and at the parking lot. An information shelter and bike racks can be found at the parking lot.

parks.name: Hemer Park
parks.location: Hemer Park is located on Holden Lake, 12km south of Nanaimo on southern Vancouver Island. Take the Cedar Road turnoff from Hwy 1 and follow directional signs to the park, which is situated on Hemer Road. Nearby communities include Nanaimo, Yellow Point, Ladysmith.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This day-use only park has no designated picnic facilities. However, there are a number of park benches where visitors could enjoy a picnic. Other facilities consist of an extensive trail system and two pit toilets.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has two pit toilets, located approximately 50 metres from the parking lot on the main trail.

parks.name: Herald Park
parks.location: Herald Park is 14 km east of the Trans-Canada Highway at Tappen. It is on the west shore of the Salmon Arm of Shuswap Lake. The closest communities, towns, and cities are Tappen, Canoe, Sorrento, and Salmon Arm.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Herald Park offers a large day-use and picnicking area. This has a combination of grassy areas and over 1,000 m of mostly sandy beach. Pit toilets and cold-water taps are available. Camping is allowed in the day-use area when the campgrounds are closed.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit and flush toilets are available throughout the park. For a park map, see the maps and location section.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: Hot showers are available for campers in the Homestead and Reinecker campgrounds.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold-water taps are available throughout Herald Park. Taps are shut off outside the operating season. There are no hookups in this park. Water for filling holding tanks is available at the sani-station.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail:
A concrete boat launch is available in Herald Park’s day-use area. A large parking area is nearby, which can accommodate boat trailers. Overnight parking is not allowed. For a map with the boat launch location, see maps and location.
To use your boat in Herald Park, you must have:
A pleasure craft operator card
A pleasure craft licence
All safety equipment required by Transport Canada, on board
Park Ranger’s frequently inspect boats. For more information on boating regulations, see Transport Canada’s marine transportation page and check signs at the boat launch.
Houseboats are not allowed to park overnight in Herald Park. Please see the Shuswap Marine Park page for information about lake sites.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station is available for registered campers in Herald Park. For opening dates, contact the park operator.
Fees (per use)
Sani-station$5

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed in fire rings provided in the campgrounds. We encourage all campers to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire. Bring a camping stove for cooking.
Herald Park is a high-risk forest fire area. Keep your campfire below 50 cm high. Never leave your campfire unattended. To learn more about safe campfires, see the prevent wildfires section of our camping and day-use guide.
You can buy firewood in the park, or bring your own. If you bring your own firewood, buy it locally. Wood from other areas can spread invasive species. For firewood prices, contact the park operator.
Do not gather firewood in the park, as this is an offence under the Park Act. Dead wood is important habitat for plants and animals, and it adds valuable organic material to the soil.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: An adventure playground is available in the day-use area.

gate.note: May close earlier due to snow. Trails accessible year-round.

parks.operating_note: Gate may close earlier due to snow. Campground gate closes mid-October. Trails accessible year-round.

parks.name: Hesquiat Lake Park
parks.location: Hesquiat Lake Park is located in Clayoquot Sound on the west coast of Vancouver Island, north of Tofino. The park is situated on the east side of Hesquiat Lake, northeast of Hesquiat Harbour. This park is difficult to access and can only be reached by floatplane or by boat via Hesquiat Harbour. Nearby communities include Tofino, Hot Springs Village, Flores Island, Ahousat.

parks.name: Hesquiat Peninsula Park
parks.location: Hesquiat Peninsula is located in the northwestern part of Clayoquot Sound on the west coast of Vancouver Island. The park is situated between Nootka Sound and Hesquiat Harbour and is accessible by boat and float plane from Hot Springs Cove, Tofino, Tahsis and Gold River.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While small fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you do have a fire use small pieces of wood that will burn completely. Build your fires below the high tide mark.
Never build fires next to or near beach logs. Never leave your fire unattended and practice “Leave No Trace” camping ethics.

parks.name: High Lakes Basin Park
parks.location: Located 16 km west of Little Fort, and 2.5 km north of Caverhill Lake on the Nehalliston Plateau. Access is by foot or horseback.

parks.name: Hisnit River Watershed Protected Area
parks.location: This protected area is located approximately 35 kilometres from Kyuquot, adjacent to Brooks Peninsula Park (a.k.a. Mquqᵂin Park) and Ka:’yu:’k’t’h’/Che:k’tles7et’h’ First Nations Lands at the Power River Estuary (Hisnit).

parks.name: Hitchie Creek Park
parks.location: Hitchie Creek is situated to the north of Nitinat Lake and is adjacent to Pacific Rim National Park Reserve on the southwest coast of Vancouver Island. Access to the park is by hiking from Hitchie Lake within the national park, a rough route approximately 1 km long.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Water for human consumption can be found in the creek and lake. All surface water must be well boiled, filtered or treated prior to consumption.

parks.name: Hole-in-the-Wall Park
parks.location: Hole-in-the-Wall Park is located 50 km along the Sukunka Forest Service Road. The closest communities, towns and cities are Tumbler Ridge and Chetwynd.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Holliday Creek Arch Protected Area
parks.location: This small, 395-hectare protected area is located between the communities of Dunster and McBride, north of Highway 16. There is no road access.

parks.name: Homathko Estuary Park
parks.location: Homathko Estuary Park lies 220 km northwest of Vancouver, at the head of Bute Inlet. There is boat access via Bute Inlet to Waddington Harbour; however, moorage facilities do not exist at this park and moorage near the park may be difficult due to extensive mud flats and shallow water.

parks.name: Homathko River-Tatlayoko Protected Area
parks.location: The Protected Area is located approximately 175 km west of Williams Lake and 30 km south of Tatla Lake. The area can be accessed by gravel road off Highway 20 near Tatla Lake. For additional map information, please refer to topographical map numbers: 1:50,000 92N/6, 92N/7, 92N/8, 92N/9, 92N/11, and 92N/2.

parks.name: Honeymoon Bay Ecological Reserve
parks.location: On Sutton Creek, 9km west of Lake Cowichan town.

parks.name: Horne Lake Caves Park
parks.location: Horne Lake Caves Park is located 60 km north of Nanaimo and 26 km west of Qualicum on central Vancouver Island. The park can be accessed via the Horne Lake exit off Hwy 19 or Hwy 19a. Follow signs for 12 km to Horne Lake.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area with two picnic tables and pit toilets. The Horne Lake Regional Park is located adjacent to the provincial park. The regional park allows access to Horne Lake which provides recreation opportunities for camping, swimming, fishing and picnicking nearby.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has two pit toilets, located at the day-use area.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Horneline Creek Park
parks.location: Located near the Kechika River, about 130 km south of Lower Post and about 30 km north of Denetiah Park. Access is by river boat and foot. The Kechika River is the main access route to the park. Access to the Kechika River primarily occurs at Skooks Landing, near the community of Fireside, and involves a 250 km boat trip. The historic Davie Trail, which travels from Fort Ware to Lower Post, follows a portion of the Kechika River adjacent to the Rocky Mountain Trench.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Campfires are allowed in the park. To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil. Please bring a portable stove for cooking.

parks.name: Horsefly Lake Park
parks.location:
The park is located on Horsefly Lake, approximately 65km from 150 Mile House off Highway 97. 55km of the route is paved, and 10km is well-maintained gravel. The closest community is Horsefly, located 13km southwest of the park. Other communities are Likely and Williams Lake.
For map information, please refer to topographical map numbers: 1:50,000 92P/11.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area. It is a grassy area with a pebbly beach on the lake. There are two change houses, horseshoe pits, basketball net, feather ball, BBQ, and a dock for swimming. Firewood is available for purchase.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has only pit toilets which are located throughout the campground.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps are located throughout the park. One at the entrance and one at the boat launch area. Taps are shut off during the off-season. Water taps do not have hose hook-ups for campers and trailers.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: This park has a play area composed of a basketball hoop, feather ball and horseshoe pit. These are located in the day-use area.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a single-wide concrete boat launch at this park. It is located at the far end of the campground. There is parking available for vehicles and boat trailers, and they can be left overnight. Boats should not be left in the water or beached overnight.

parks.name: Hot Springs-No Name Creek Conservancy
parks.location: Hot Springs-No Name Creek Conservancy is located approximately 20 kilometres southwest of Bella Coola and 45 kilometres east of Bella Bella.

parks.name: Huchsduwachsdu Nuyem Jees/Kitlope Heritage Conservancy
parks.location:
The park is located at the end of the Gardner Canal, on British Columbia’s central coast, approximately 50km northwest of Bella Coola and 120km southeast of Kitimat. The area is accessed by boat to the end of the Gardener Canal. The area is accessed by boat and aircraft only. Visitors should be experienced in ocean navigation and wilderness survival. Visitors can use jet boats to access Kitlope Lake and Kitlope River systems.
Reference: Marine Charts #3743 (Douglas Channel) and #3745 (Gardner Canal).
Reference: 1:50,000 topographic map #93 E/4 (Kitlope Lake).

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: While campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Some back country pit toilets are available for public use at the Miskusa Indian Reserve (IR #16), BC Parks Cabin, and the two campsites at Kitlope Lake.

parks.name: Hudson Rocks Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Found 2.5km north of Newcastle Island, Nanaimo, B.C.

parks.name: Hunwadi/Ahnuhati – Bald Conservancy
parks.location: The conservancy is located on Knight Inlet, 100 km east of Port Hardy, 80 km north of Campbell River and 200 km northwest of Vancouver.

parks.name: Háthayim Marine Park [a.k.a. Von Donop Marine Park]
parks.location: Háthayim Marine Park is located at the northwest tip of Cortes Island, east of Campbell River on central Vancouver Island. Access to the park is by boat only, via Sutil Channel. Boaters can reference marine chart #3538 for more information on this area. Nearby communities include Cortes Island, Quadra Island, Squirrel Cove, Whaletown, Campbell River.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While small fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you do have a fire, please utilize previously constructed fire rings and use small pieces of wood that will burn completely. If you can’t find a previously used site, try to construct your fire rings below the high tide mark. Never leave your fire unattended and practice “
Leave No Trace” camping ethics.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: One pit toilet is located at the far end of the bay.

parks.name: Hǝnʎǝmdzi Mǝkola/Yorke Island Conservancy
parks.location: Hənʎəmdᶻi Məkola/Yorke Island Conservancy is located 68 km northwest of Campbell River, 75 km northwest of Cape Mudge and 248 km northwest of Vancouver.

parks.name: I7loqaw7/100 Lakes Plateau Conservancy
parks.location: I7loqaw7/100 Lakes Plateau Conservancy is located approximately 55 kilometres northwest of Pemberton.

parks.name: Ilgachuz Range Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Found 35 km north of Anahim Lake, Chilcotin district.

parks.name: Incomappleux Conservancy
parks.location: Southeast of Revelstoke, and approximately 70km north of Nakusp off Highway 31.

parks.name: Indian Lake – Hitchcock Creek/Át Chi'îni Shà Conservancy
Inkaneep Park
parks.location: This park is located 6km north of Oliver on Hwy 97. The closest communities are Okanagan Falls and Oliver.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has two pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: A hand pump is available in the park.
