parks.name: Malaspina Park
parks.location:
Malaspina Park is located approximately 30 km to the northwest of Powell River, on the eastern and northern shoreline of Malaspina Peninsula. The closest communities are the communities of Lund and Malaspina Inlet.
Nearby provincial parks include Desolation Sound, Okeover Arm, Copeland Islands, Roscoe Bay, Teakerne Arm and Walsh Cove.

parks.name: Mansons Landing Park
parks.location:
Located on the west side of Cortes Island, this park is accessible by boat and by car ferry from Campbell River via Quadra Island. Ferry service is offered by BC Ferries; sailing times are approximately 15 minutes from Campbell River to Quadra Island, and 45 minutes from Quadra to Cortes. The park can be reached via Seaford Road on Cortes Island.
The park can also be accessed by private boat, which can moor at the adjacent federal government wharf (space permitting).
Nearby communities include: Whaletown, Squirrel Cove, Cortes Bay and Smelt Bay.

facilities.name: Information
facilities.detail: An information shelter is located at Hague Lake.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has two day-use and picnic areas: one at Mansons Lagoon and one at Hague Lake. Facilities at Mansons Lagoon include picnic tables, one pit toilet, a sandy spit and a parking lot. This parking lot also accesses the federal wharf. Hague Lake has a pit toilet, information shelter, sandy beach and a small parking area. Both areas can be accessed from Seaford Road on Cortes Island. A rough trail, approximately 1 km long, links the two day-use areas.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for Manson's Landing Park as well as the Hague Lake area.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a natural boat launch (no facility) on the west side of the spit at Mansons Lagoon. Motorboats are not permitted on Hague Lake.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Hague Lake has two pit toilets, an information shelter, sandy beach and a small parking area. Both areas can be accessed from Seaford Road on Cortes Island. A rough trail, approximately 1 km long, links the two day-use areas.

parks.name: Manzanita Cove Conservancy
parks.location:
Manzanita Cove Conservancy is located along the northwest coast of British Columbia and is within the asserted traditional territories of the Coast Tsimshian 1 and the Kitsumkalum First Nation. It is also within the asserted traditional harvest area of the Kitselas First Nation. The conservancy is situated approximately 20 kilometres north of Lax Kw’alaams (Port Simpson), 45 kilometres north of Metlakatla and 50 kilometres north of Prince Rupert.
Manzanita Cove Conservancy: Overview [PDF]
Manzanita Cove Conservancy: Context [PDF]
1 The term “Coast Tsimshian” is used to refer to the people of both the Lax Kw’alaams First Nation and the Metlakatla First Nation.

parks.name: Mara Meadows Ecological Reserve
parks.location: In the Larch Hills, 17km north of Enderby.

parks.name: Mara Meadows Park
parks.location: The park is located 12 kilometres southeast of Salmon Arm on the southeastern edge of Larch Hills.

parks.name: Mara Park
parks.location: On the south-east side of Mara Lake, accessed via Hwy 97A. The park is 10km north of the junction of Hwys 97A and 97B. If traveling on Trans Canada Hwy #1, the park is 12km south of Sicamous.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area as well as a parking lot.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit and flush toilets are located throughout the park.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: A paved boat launch is provided.

gate.note: Dates may change depending on snow

parks.name: Marble Canyon Park
parks.location:
Marble Canyon Park is 40 km northwest of Cache Creek, a village in the Thompson region of B.C.’s southern interior. The nearest town is Lillooet. Most visitors access the park via the gated entrance to Crown Lake Campground.
From Cache Creek, head north on Cariboo HWY/BC-97 S for 11 km. Turn left onto BC-99 S, toward Lillooet and Whistler. Stay on HWY 99 for 27.5 km. The campground entrance is on your left.
In the winter, the campground gate is closed. A pull-out by the gate has parking space for around six vehicles. From here, it is a short walk to the campground. For information on when the gate is open, see the top of this page.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
Marble Canyon Park has a small day-use and picnic area beside Crown Lake Campground. When visiting this area, please park in a designated parking spot.
Do not park on the side of the road. Barbecues and camp stoves are not allowed on the picnic tables. There are no day-use facilities at Pavilion Lake.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Marble Canyon Park has pit toilets at the campground and day-use area on the shore of Crown Lake. There are no public toilets or other facilities at Pavilion Lake. If you are visiting Pavilion Lake, please use the facilities at Crown Lake.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Marble Canyon Park has one hand pump, which is at Crown Lake Campground. The water is safe for drinking and cooking.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed in the firepits provided at Crown Lake Campground. For more information, see the camping section. Fires are not allowed anywhere else in this park. It is especially dangerous to light fires on the ice of frozen lakes during the winter.
You can help protect the environment by keeping your campfire small and using a camping stove for cooking. Do not gather firewood in the park. Gathering wood is an offence under the Park Act. Dead wood is important habitat for plants and animals, and it adds valuable organic material to the soil.
If you bring your own firewood, please buy it locally. Wood brought in from other areas can introduce invasive species. To learn more, visit Buy Local, Burn Local. You can buy firewood from the park operator. Please pay in cash when you register for camping.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: If you must have a fire, please burn only dead and down wood, and be sure to extinguish the fire fully. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil so please use it conservatively, if at all. Be prepared to bring a portable stove for cooking.

parks.name: Marble River Park
parks.location: Marble River Park is located on northern Vancouver Island, at the juncture of Rupert Inlet, Holberg Inlet, Quatsino Sound and Neroutsos Inlet. The park is located approximately 15km north of Port Alice and 35km southwest of Port Hardy. The park can also be accessed by boat from Coal Harbour. Boaters can reference marine chart #3679 (Quatsino Sound) and the more detailed chart for Quatsino Narrows, #3681 (Plans Quatsino Sound).

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you must use a campfire, please practice “
Leave No Trace” camping ethics.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Marl Creek Park
parks.location: The park is located in the Southern Rocky Mountain Trench approximately 25 km north of Golden on the Trans-Canada Highway. There is no public access and the park is not developed for visitor use.

parks.name: Martha Creek Park
parks.location:
Martha Creek Park is 20 km north of Revelstoke, in the southern interior of B.C.
From Revelstoke, take Big Bend Hwy/Nakusp Mica Hwy/BC-23 N for about 17 km. Watch for parks signs. The park entrance will be on your left.

facilities.name: Picnic shelters
facilities.detail:
A picnic shelter is located off the day-use parking lot. The enclosed building does not have cooking facilities or services. A potable water tap and grey water disposal are nearby. Inside the shelter are four picnic tables, and nearby are five picnic tables. Reservations are available for the picnic shelter.
You can make a reservation online at camping.bcparks.ca or by calling 1-800-689-9025 (1-519-858-6161 internationally). For detailed information, see the picnic shelters page.
Group picnicking fee: $50 per group
A $20 fee is added for anyone who is not a B.C. resident. For more information, visit the non-resident fee section of the camping fees page.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold well water is available for cooking and drinking. Both campers and picnickers share eight water taps located at each group of campsites. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
This park has two recognized day-use areas. One is on the beach and one is closer to the day-use parking area. The one parking lot can accommodate 40 vehicles. Fire pits and barbeque stands are not available.
The beach day-use and picnic area located at the south end of the campground has six picnic tables, 20 m back from the shoreline. Nearby are an adventure playground, water tap and two pit toilets. The beach is coarse sand and pebbles, 300 m long and flat.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: There are hot showers in the flush washrooms, with an accessible parking lot located across the shower building. There is no extra charge for showers, however, they are for registered guests only.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
There is a sani-station available in this park. This is a full-service sani-station, suitable for dumping black and grey water, as well as a fresh water fill.
Sani-station use fee: $5 per discharge in coin or purchased token.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: A paved and concrete singlewide boat launch is located at the southern tip of the park, at the far end of the park entrance road. A large wharf accommodating up to four boats is available to dock your boat. Overnight parking is not permitted within the day-use parking lot. Overflow boat trailer parking is also available near site 41. See Campground Map [PDF] .

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: An adventure playground with swing set, monkey bars, and slide is located at the beach day-use area. The equipment is set in pea gravel.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: The park campground has twelve pit toilets conveniently located throughout the campsites and day-use areas. There is a large, flush washroom and shower facility located central to the campground. It has male and female sides, as well as a family room with flush toilet, sink and shower. This facility is disability and wheelchair-accessible.

parks.name: Maxhamish Lake Park
parks.location: 125 km north of Fort Nelson, 12 km off the Liard Hwy (77). There is no road access and the closest community is Fort Nelson.

parks.name: Maxhamish Lake Protected Area
parks.location: 125 km north of Fort Nelson, 12 km off the Liard Hwy (77). There is no road access and the closest community is Fort Nelson.

parks.name: Maxtaktsm'aa/Union Passage Conservancy
parks.location:
Maxtaktsm’aa/Union Passage Conservancy is only accessible by boat or float plane and is located approximately 15 km SW of Hartley Bay and 90 km SW of Kitimat. It is located between Grenville Channel and Squally Channel and also between Farrant Island and Pitt Island.
Reference: Marine Charts #3945 (Approaches to Douglas Channel) and #3742 (Otter Passage to McKay Reach).
Reference: 1:50,000 scale Topographic Map #103 H/6 (Hartley Bay).
Visitor Information Centre:

facilities.detail:
Firewood and campfire rings are not provided. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of campfires and using campstoves instead.
If you must have a fire, please burn only dead and down wood, and be sure to fully extinguish the fire when done and spread out the ashes and rocks. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil so please use it conservatively, if at all.

parks.name: McConnell Lake Park
parks.location: This park is located 35km south of Kamloops and 49km north of Merritt. To access this park, take the Lac le Jeune Exit off Hwy #5.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This is a very rustic day-use area. There is one picnic table near the boat launch.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has one pit toilet, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a small gravel surfaced boat launch suitable for small boats. This is a small, quiet fishing lake. High-speed operation of boats is discouraged.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: McDonald Creek Park
parks.location: This park is located in the southern interior of B.C. on the east and west shores of the Upper Arrow Lake, 10 km south of Nakusp on Highway 6. The park facilities are only in the eastern section of the park.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
One day-use and picnic area is located before the campground on a sandy, grassed bench. This area has six tables, one pit toilet and a water tap.
During high water the beach is sandy with the tables 50 metres from the waters edge. Although this area is recognized as the main day-use and picnic site, many visitors do picnic along its entire 800 metre shoreline.
This area has limited facilities and contains no change house or barbeque stands. A day-use parking area is nearby.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are over fifteen accessible pit toilets located throughout the campground and within the day-use area. One pit toilet is at the boat launch. There are flush toilets located in the shower building.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: The shower building is located near the entrance to the campground by the day-use parking lot. The shower building has three showers in each of the men’s and women’s washrooms in addition to a flush toilet. There is also a fully accessible washroom complete with a shower and toilet. There are no extra charges for showers and they are for registered guests only.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water is available for cooking and drinking. The park has chlorinated, treated water pumped from the reservoir. There are eleven drinking water taps located throughout the campground and day-use area. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: The playground is located adjacent to the day-use beach and is accessible from the day-use parking lot. The playground is suitable for ages five and older. Surrounding the playground are picnic tables, a potable water stand pipe, shared fire ring and toilet facilities.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: The boat launch is located at the south end of the park, accessed by turning turn left at the park entrance. This concrete plank, singlewide ramp is only useable during high water. A nearby 25 vehicle parking lot is available for overnight parking. There is no wharf but boats are beached during the day. Both car top and power boats can be seen on the lake.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
The park has a sani-station.
Sani-station use fee: $5 per discharge in coin or purchased token.

facilities.name: Electrical hook-ups
facilities.detail: Sites 1 to 18 have either 30amp or 50amp electrical service. An additional service charge of $7 per night, applies to these sites regardless of whether electrical service is used. Electrified campsites have fire rings.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Megin River Ecological Reserve
parks.location: At the mouth of the Megin River, Shelter Inlet, 21km north by north west of Tofino.

parks.name: Mehatl Creek Park
parks.location:
To reach Mehatl Creek Park, turn west at the main intersection in Boston Bar, where a big sign directs traffic off of Highway 1 to North Bend. Drive over the bridge to the west side of the Fraser River and follow the Nahatlatch Forest Service Road. Continue along the Forest Service Road for about 48 km to Mehatl Creek Park. To reach Mehatl Creek Park via this route you must pass through Nahatlatch Park.

parks.name: Memory Island Park
parks.location: Memory Island Park is located on Shawnigan Lake on southern Vancouver Island. The park can be reached from various points on Shawnigan Lake, including West Shawnigan Lake Park. To reach this park turn west off Hwy 1 at Shawnigan/Mill Bay Road in Mill Bay. Follow the road approximately 15 km to Shawnigan Lake, then turn right onto Shawnigan Lake Road. Follow this road until you reach the park. Nearby communities include: Shawnigan Lake, Cobble Hill, Mill Bay, Cowichan

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

parks.name: Meridian Road (Vanderhoof) Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 40km south of Vanderhoof.

parks.name: Meziadin Lake Park
parks.location: Located 155 km north of Kitwanga on Highway 37, just south of Meziadin Junction and 50 km east of Stewart.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Meziadin Lake Park is a scenic spot with beautiful views over Meziadin Lake. It has many facilities such as a large picnic shelter, picnic tables, fire rings, pit toilets, handicap access toilets, food cache and a drinking water hand pump.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are two pit toilets that are wheelchair-accessible.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: A hand water pump is available and it is located adjacent to the information shelter. There are no hose hookups for campers or trailers.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: Meziadin Lake Park is an excellent location for boating offering beautiful views of the surrounding landscape. A gravel, moderate grade boat launch is available to visitors. It is singlewide and trailers must be parked at their campsite. Boats can be tied to the dock but there is limited space.

facilities.name: Electrical hook-ups
facilities.detail: Electricity with 30 amp service is available to 18 sites. Please note campers occupying sites with electricity will pay an extra $5 per night whether the power is in use or not.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Milligan Hills Park
parks.location: Milligan Hills Park is located approximately 150 km northeast of Fort St. John near the B.C. and Alberta border. A gravel road (137 Road) provides access to within 3 km of the park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood is not available in the park. You may purchase firewood outside of the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
While campfires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Miracle Beach Park
parks.location: Miracle Beach Park is located 22km north of Courtenay and 22km south of Campbell River off Hwy 19a. From Hwy 19 take exit #144 (Hamm Road) to Hwy 19a (the Oceanside Route). Head north a short distance to Miracle Beach Drive, then drive 2km straight into the park. Nearby communities include Campbell River, Comox Valley, and Merville.

facilities.name: Bike park
facilities.detail: A children’s bike park is available for the use and enjoyment of visitors staying in the campground.

facilities.name: Picnic shelters
facilities.detail:
The south parking lot leads to a day-use area on the beach. This area offers a picnic shelter that is covered, semi-enclosed, and has picnic tables, changing facilities, flush toilets, an information shelter, and a parking area.
You can make a reservation online at camping.bcparks.ca or by calling 1-800-689-9025 (1-519-858-6161 internationally). For detailed information, see the picnic shelters page.
Group picnicking fee: $50.00 per group
A $20 fee is added for anyone who is not a B.C. resident. For more information, visit the non-resident fee section of the camping fees page.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: There is an adventure playground at this park, located in the campground next to the shower house.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. Campfire rings are provided at each campsite, as well as communal ring for the group campsite. Be prepared to bring a portable stove for cooking.
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
Gathering firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park damages vegetation and ground cover and is a ticketable offence under the Park Act. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil. You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps are located throughout the campground. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: There is one hot shower building at this park, located in the center of the campground, including one separate wheelchair-accessible shower stall. Showers are for registered campers only.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station is available during the collecting season.
Sani-station use fee: $5.00 per discharge

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit toilets are located throughout the park. A flush toilet and change house is located at the south beach day-use area. Flush toilets are also located in five areas of the campground.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
This park has two day-use and picnic areas. The south parking lot leads to a day-use area on the beach. This offers a covered, semi-enclosed picnic shelter, picnic tables, changing facilities, flush toilets, an information shelter, and a parking area. The north parking lot leads to nature trails, the Black Creek estuary, and beach. Pit toilets and an information shelter are available at this parking lot.
The Miracle Beach trail map [PDF] shows areas you can go with your on-leash dog. To help protect conservation values, dogs are prohibited from the estuary and north beach areas.

parks.name: Misty Lake Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 12km north west of Port McNeill.

parks.name: Mitlenatch Island Nature Park
parks.location:
Mitlenatch Island Nature Park is located east of Black Creek in the Strait of Georgia, off central Vancouver Island. The closest communities are Comox, Courtenay, Lund, Powell River and Campbell River. The park is accessible by boat, only. Boaters can reference marine chart #3513 and #3538 for more information about this area.
The only access to the park is from Northwest Bay or Camp Bay. No boats are to land along the rocky shorelines on either side of both Camp and Northwest Bays or at any point around the island. Oystercatchers and Pigeon Guillemots nest just above the high tideline. Boaters should enter into the middle of either bay to minimize wildlife disturbance and are responsible for their own boat and passengers.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has one pit toilet, located near the host cabin.

parks.name: Moberly Lake Park
parks.location: Located approximately 25 km northwest of Chetwynd on Highway 29. There are 3 km of paved road access.

facilities.name: Picnic shelters
facilities.detail:
Group picnicking is available for a fee at this park. Reservations for the group site picnic shelter are available. You can make a reservation online at camping.bcparks.ca or by calling 1-800-689-9025 (1-519-858-6161 internationally). For detailed information, see the picnic shelters page.
Group picnicking fee: $35 per group
A $20 fee is added for anyone who is not a B.C. resident. For more information, visit the non-resident fee section of the camping fees page.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: An adventure playground with accessible features is available in the day-use area.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a double boat launch complete with a large parking area for vehicles and trailers.

facilities.name: Sani-station

A sani-station and dump is available during the collecting season.

parks.name: Moksgm'ol/Chapple – Cornwall Conservancy
parks.location:
Moksgm’ol/Chapple-Cornwall Conservancy is only accessible by boat, floatplane or helicopter and is located about 35 km south of Hartley Bay and 105 km southwest of Kitimat. It is located along the northwest side of Princess Royal Island.
Reference: Marine Charts #3719 (Chapple Inlet); #3723 (Barnard Harbour); #3724 (Caamano Sound & Approaches); #3742 (Otter Passage to McKay Reach).
Reference: 1:50,000 scale Topographic Maps #103 A/14 (Caamano Sound); #103 A/15 (Laredo Inlet); #103 H/2 (Butedale); #103 H/3 (Gil Island).

parks.name: Momich Lakes Park
parks.location:
Three routes, all gravel logging roads, can access this area.
From Hwy 5 south of Barriere, via Agate Bay Road and along the west side and northern end of Adams Lake (80 km).
From TransCanada Hwy 1 at Squilax to Adams Lake roads (95 km).
From Hwy 5 at Vavenby, via logging roads (60 km).
Nearest towns include Chase, Scotch Creek, Kamloops, Vavenby, Clearwater.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are only user-maintained pit toilets available in this park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: No firewood is provided. Some fire rings are available. The gathering of firewood in a park is illegal, so fires should only be used for emergency drying and warming. If a fire is used for an emergency, please keep it small, and ensure it is completely out before you leave. Use a camp stove for cooking. Campfires are not permitted on the beach below the high water mark.

parks.name: Monashee Park
parks.location:
Located 111 km north of Vernon. Take Highway 97 to Vernon, then go east on Highway 6 from Vernon for 47 km, through Lumby to Cherryville. Turn north onto Sugar Lake Road and proceed 46 km until you reach the turnoff (km marker #22) to the park. Proceed on Spectrum Creek Road for 16 km to the park.
An alternative access to the park is from the Arrow Lakes side. Follow highway 23 south from Revelstoke to Shelter Bay Forest Service Road (FSR) and turn right. This active logging road is steep and narrow in sections. Follow the Sol Mountain Lodge signs. At kilometre 35 turn right onto North Fosthall Creek FSR, keeping right, for approximately 17 km. The North Fosthall Creek trail starts at the end of the road. The trail may not be well defined and is not regularly maintained. This access should be attempted by experienced backcountry travelers only. The majority of this road access is maintained by Sol Mountain Lodge.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
This park has a day-use and picnic area at Rainbow Falls. There is a 15 car gravel parking lot with one pit toilet and an information shelter beside the trail to Spectrum Lake.
The other trail leaving the parking lot is a steep, well defined trail that leads down to the falls. Wet areas are covered with boardwalk and footbridges. There are no picnic tables at the falls or in the parking lot. There are two wooden viewing platforms below the falls offering a spectacular view.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are three pit toilets at Spectrum Lake campground, one at the Spectrum Lake group site, and one pit toilet each at Little Peters, Big Peters and Margie Lake campgrounds. There is also one at the Spectrum Creek trailhead.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are permitted within fire rings at Spectrum Lake campground only.
Bring a portable stove for cooking. You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Monck Park
parks.location: On the western shore of Nicola Lake, 22 km north of Merritt, 12 km off Hwy 5A via narrow paved road.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
The day-use is located next to the lake on a large grassy area. There are 40 picnic tables and 15 of the tables have a roof shelter. A few trees provide some shade.
There is a large parking area adjacent to the day-use. No campfires are allowed in the day-use area. Please ensure that all barbeques or campstoves are used on the ground and not set on picnic tables.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are three flush toilet buildings, five single flush toilets (four with sinks) and seven pit toilets.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: There is an adventure playground and horseshoe pitch near the day-use area.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a concrete boat launch located next to the day-use area. Waterskiing is popular on the lake.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
There is a user pay sani-station near the entrance of the park.
Sani-station use fee: $5 per discharge

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Monckton Nii Łuutiksm Conservancy
parks.location:
Monckton Nii Luutiksm Conservancy is only accessible by boat, floatplane or helicopter and is located about 30 km SW of Hartley Bay and 105 km SW of Kitimat. It is located along the southwest end of Pitt Island, along the east side of Principe Channel.
Reference: Marine Charts #3721 (Plans Pitt Island); #3741 (Otter Passage to Bonilla Island); #3742 (Otter Passage to McKay Reach); #3945 (Approaches to Douglas Channel).
Reference: 1:50,000 scale Topographic Maps #103 H/4 (Trutch Island) and #103 H/5 (Port Stephens).
Visitor Information Centre:
Kitimat Visitor Information Centre
PO Box 214
2109 Forest Avenue
Kitimat, BC, Canada V8C 2G7
http://www.tourismkitimat.ca/
e-mail: info@tourismkitimat.ca
phone: 250-632-6294 or 1-800-664-6554

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood and campfire rings are not provided. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of campfires and using campstoves instead.
If you must have a fire, please burn only dead and down wood, and be sure to fully extinguish the fire when done and spread out the ashes and rocks. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil so please use it conservatively, if at all.

parks.name: Monkman Park
parks.location:
Monkman Park is located on the Kinuseo Falls Road, 60km south of Tumbler Ridge. Several roads provide access to this community. Turn south off highway 97 at Chetwynd onto highway 29, or turn south off of highway 97 onto highway 52 approximately 17km west of Dawson Creek. Visitors travelling on highway 2 to or from Dawson Creek can also turn south on highway 52, near the BC/Alberta border.
National Topographic Series Maps 93I/11 and 93I/14 at a scale of 1:50,000 cover the Monkman Lake Trail. These maps are available from most map retailers in British Columbia.
GPS Navigation
Monkman Provincial Park Trails and Camps [KMZ]
Ground-Level Views
Eastern shore of Monkman Lake
Near the north end of Monkman Lake
Near Paxton Peak
Kinuseo Falls

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: The picnic area is located two kilometres from the the campsite. At this location, there are picnic tables and pit toilets.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has only pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: A cold water hand pump is located in this park. Boil water advisory in effect. The hand pump is shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Kinuseo
Monkman
Stone Corral

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Fire rings are available. Firewood is is not for sale at this park, so you must bring your own.

gate.note: Frontcountry campground open spring and summer. All other areas accessible year-round as weather allows.

parks.operating_note: Frontcountry campground open spring and summer. All other areas accessible year-round as weather allows.

parks.name: Montague Harbour Marine Park
parks.location:
Montague Harbour Marine Park is located on the southwest side of Galiano Island approximately 10 km northwest of Sturdies Bay. BC Ferries provides vehicle and passenger service to Sturdies Bay from Swartz Bay on Vancouver Island and from Tsawwassen, south of Vancouver. The park is located on Montague Park Road. Follow signs to the park from the ferry terminal. Boaters can reference marine chart #3442, #3462, #3463 and #3473 for more information on this area.
Nearby communities include: Galiano Island, Saltspring Island, Victoria, Nanaimo, Duncan, Vancouver.

facilities.name: Dock
facilities.detail:
Docking fee: $2 per metre
11 m (36 ft) length limit
For more information, see the mooring buoy and boat launch facilities.
A $20 fee is added for anyone who is not a B.C. resident. For more information, visit the non-resident fee section of the camping fees page.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area. As you enter the park, head straight past the drive-in campsites to an open grassy field beside the boat launch. Picnic tables and pit toilets can be found in the day-use area.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are five sets of male and female pit toilets located throughout the campsite.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
Cold water taps are located throughout the park. Water is available from March 15 to October 31. This water is treated and safe to drink.
Annual Drinking Water System Report 2025: Montague Harbour [PDF]

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail:
Montague Harbour Marine Park has a boat launch near the beach and day-use area. To get to the boat launch, follow the main road past the vehicle-accessible campsites.
Montague Harbour has dock facilities and mooring buoys. Boats can also anchor in Montague Harbour.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
This park has campfire time restrictions.
Cooking fires are allowed from:
7 am to 9 am
11 am to 1 pm
5 pm to 7 pm
Small campfires are permitted after 7 pm.
These restrictions will improve air quality and firewood conservation while still permitting fires. Visitors must use campfire rings, which are provided at each campsite. During the camping season, firewood can be purchased from the park operator. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Mooring buoy
facilities.detail:
Mooring buoy fee: $14 per night
39 mooring buoys available
For more information, see the dock and boat launch facilities.
A $20 fee is added for anyone who is not a B.C. resident. For more information, visit the non-resident fee section of the camping fees page.

parks.name: Monte Creek Park
parks.location: Located 26 km east of Kamloops, on the South Thompson River.

parks.name: Monte Lake Park
parks.location: Located 32km southeast of Kamloops on Hwy #97. The closest communities to this park are Monte Lake, Kamloops and Falkland.

parks.name: Moore/McKenny/Whitmore Islands Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Off Aristazabal Island, on the east side of Hecate Strait, 100km north west of Bella Bella.

parks.name: Moose Valley Park
parks.location: The park is located approximately 31 km west of 100 Mile House, and can be accessed by driving west on the Exeter Station Road. This road leaves Hwy 97 just north of downtown 100 Mile House, and should be followed to the junction with the 1100 Road. Continue west on the 1100 Road to the 1117 marker. Here, turn right onto the one-lane road and continue in a northwest direction to the main access point of the canoe route at Marks Lake (approximately 9 km). This road is best suited to four-wheel drive, high clearance vehicles. For additional map information, please refer to topographical map numbers: 1:50,000 Gustafsen Lake 92P/12 or 1:250,000 Bonaparte River 92P.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, located at Maitland and Marks Lake. There are no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood is not provided. Firewood may be purchased outside the park, or you can bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
While campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Morden Colliery Historic Park
parks.location: Morden Colliery Historic Park is located 7 km south of Nanaimo on southern Vancouver Island. Access to the park is off Highway 1 on Morden Road. The parking lot for Morden Colliery is also used as the trailhead for the regional district.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: There is a day-use and picnicking area at this park.

parks.name: Morice Lake Park
parks.location:
Morice Lake Park is located approximately 84 km from the town of Houston. Access to the park follows a radio controlled logging road. Public vehicles are permitted, but please proceed with caution and be aware that loaded logging trucks have the right of way.
Travel the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) to the town of Houston.
Turn south 2 km west of Houston onto the Morice River Forest Service Road (also known as the Huckleberry Mine road). This Forest Service Road (FSR) is marked in kilometres starting at the Canfor Mill site near the Yellowhead Highway.
Driving 27 km will bring you to the junction of the Huckleberry and Morice Lake Roads. Turn right onto the Morice Lake Road and continue to kilometre marker 75.
Take a right at the intersection just past the 75 km mark. Follow this road for 7 km to arrive at Morice Lake Park.
Blue directional blades are posted at intersections along the route to the Park.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Although there is no formalized day-use area, park visitors can use vacant lakeshore campsites for day visits.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail:
A gravel boat launch is situated at the North end of the Morice Lake campsite. The boat launch is not steep. In fall when the water is low, it is often difficult to get boat trailers into deep enough water to launch.
Waterskiing and windsurfing are not popular activities on Morice Lake due to its very cold temperature.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are permitted.
Cutting or otherwise damaging any standing or fallen trees within the park is not allowed. Please collect firewood from outside the park.

parks.name: Morice River Ecological Reserve
parks.location: On the west side of Morice River, 24km south west of Houston.

parks.name: Morton Lake Park
parks.location: Morton Lake Park is located 27 km northwest of Campbell River in the Sayward Forest. The easiest way to reach Morton Lake is via Highway 19. Turn off at the Menzies Main logging road, approximately 10 minutes past the pulp mill. Follow the gravel Menzies Main for 12 km, then take Morton Lake Road for another 7 km to the park.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park is a very popular summertime destination, with a sandy beach and warm lake. Facilities include picnic tables, a parking area and pit toilets.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has pit toilets located at the day-use area and campground.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
There is one cold water hand pump, located at the intersection of the campground and day-use area.
Annual Drinking Water System Report: Morton Lake Handpump [PDF]

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is no boat launch at Morton Lake but launching of small car-top boats and canoes can be done at Mohun Lake. A natural ramp is available for trailered boats on Mohun.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. Campfire rings are provided at each campsite, as well as communal rings in the day-use area. Be prepared to bring a portable stove for cooking.
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Mount Assiniboine Park
parks.location:
Mount Assiniboine Park is west of the British Columbia-Alberta border, 48 km southwest of Banff. Banff National Park forms the eastern boundary and Kootenay National Park marks the western boundary.
You can access the park by hiking in or by using the Mount Assiniboine Lodge helicopter service. Flights operate on Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday, and may change on summer long weekends.
To fly into the core area, you must have a valid camping reservation. For information on making a booking, see the Mount Assiniboine Park reservations page. To book a helicopter flight, visit the Mount Assiniboine Lodge website.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are pit toilets at each of Mount Assiniboine’s designated campgrounds. There are no flush toilets anywhere in the park.

parks.name: Mount Blanchet Park
parks.location: This mountainous park is located between the northwest arm and the main body of Takla Lake at Takla Narrows. There is no road access or facilities provided. (Map reference 93N/4 and 93N/5.)

parks.name: Mount Derby Ecological Reserve
parks.location: At the Tsitika drainage, south of Port McNeill, on northeastern Vancouver Island.

parks.name: Mount Edziza Park
parks.location:
National Topographic Series Map Sheets 104G/7/8W/9W/1014E/15E/15W and 16W, all at a scale of 1:50,000, cover the Mount Edziza area. These maps are available from most map retailers in British Columbia.
Access to Mount Edziza Park comes via several overland hiking routes or through one of the air charter companies that service the area. Overland routes are not regularly maintained, and knowledge of the area is required to safely use these routes. Contact the Stikine Area BC Parks office at 250-771-4591 for up-to-date information.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Always carry a cooking stove, use fire rings, and only build a fire when necessary. Keep fires limited to locations where they will not cause environmental damage.
To maintain a healthy ecosystem community, please don’t gather firewood from the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and contributes to healthy and fertile soils. For more information on campfires in the backcountry.

parks.name: Mount Elliott Ecological Reserve
parks.location: At the Tsitika drainage, south of Port McNeill, on northeastern Vancouver Island.

parks.name: Mount Elphinstone Park
parks.location: Located north of Gibsons, off of Highway 101. To access the park turn right up Crow Road or the B&K Forest Service Road. The closest communities are Gibsons, Roberts Creek and Sechelt.

parks.name: Mount Erskine Park
parks.location:
Mount Erskine Park is located on Salt Spring Island, in the southern Gulf Islands. BC Ferries offers service to Salt Spring Island from Victoria (Swartz Bay) and Crofton on Vancouver Island, and Vancouver (Tsawwassen).
This park is relatively isolated, and due to its rugged terrain, lack of road access and the surrounding private lands, the park is relatively pristine in nature.

parks.name: Mount Fernie Park
parks.location: Located 3 km South of Fernie on Highway 3.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: This park has showers.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Mount Geoffery Escarpment Park
parks.location: Located on Hornby Island, two short ferry rides from Vancouver Island. To reach Hornby Island take the Denman Island Ferry from Buckley Bay, off Hwy 19a or take Buckley Bay exit 101 from Hwy 19. Once on the island, follow Denman Road to the Hornby Island Ferry terminal. Another 10 minute ferry ride will put you on Hornby Island. As you ride the ferry from Denman Island you will get your first views of Mount Geoffrey Escarpment Park. You can access the park at several points including a trail that traverses the park from the Hornby Island Ferry Terminal to Fords Cove Marina.

parks.name: Mount Griffin Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 26km sout west of Revelstoke.

parks.name: Mount Griffin Park
parks.location:
The west side of Mount Griffin can be accessed via the Yard Creek Forest Service Road, beginning at Yard Creek Park. The Caribou Lake trailhead is about 20 km from Yard Creek Park. The road is rough and seldom used. Four-wheel drive vehicles with good clearance are recommended. Caribou Lake is about 3 km from the end of the road on a narrow trail.
The Wap Creek wetlands and Wap Lake can be reached using the Wap Creek Forest Service Road, which starts at the Trans-Canada Highway just west of Three Valley Gap. While road conditions vary with weather, two-wheel drive vehicles can usually use this road in summer. Wap Lake is about 11 km from the Trans-Canada.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Mount Maxwell Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Facing Sansum Narrows, central west coast of Salt Spring Island.

parks.name: Mount Maxwell Park
parks.location: Mount Maxwell Park is located on Salt Spring Island, in the southern Gulf Islands. BC Ferries offers service to Salt Spring Island from Victoria (Swartz Bay) and Crofton on Vancouver Island, and Vancouver (Tsawwassen). From the Salt Spring ferry terminal, head south on the Fulford Ganges Road to Cranberry Road. Turn left at the junction with Mount Maxwell Road and continue slowly on the rough road to the park. This gravel road is steep and narrow and bumpy. Caution should be taken when traveling this road.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area at the summit of Mount Maxwell. Facilities include a parking lot, pit toilet, picnic tables and a viewing area with spectacular vistas of Burgoyne Bay and Samsun Narrows. The gravel road to Mount Maxwell Park is steep, narrow and bumpy. Drive slowly and use caution when traveling this route.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: A pit toilet is located at the day-use area.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Mount Pope Park
parks.location: Mount Pope is located about 7 km northwest of Fort St. James on the northeast side of Stuart Lake. Proceed through Fort St. James on Stuart Drive W and turn left (west) on Stones Bay Road. The trailhead parking lot is 4 km down Stones Bay Road on the right. Map reference: 93K/8 & 93K/9

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: For more information on the drinking water system, read the 2025 annual report [PDF].

parks.name: Mount Richardson Park
parks.location:
From Sechelt, take Wharf Road. Then, turn right onto East Porpoise Bay Road (turns into Sechelt Inlet Road) for 8.6 km. Turn right onto the Sechelt-Dakota Forest Service Road (across from Peddles & Paddles). After 1.1 km, turn left onto Sechelt-Gray Forest Service Road Branch 9. Follow this for 5.2 km, then turn left on Branch 300 (near the 7 km marker). Using four-wheel drive, follow this very rough road staying left for 7 km to the park boundary. The last portion of the road has a very steep, difficult section.
Please read all signs, watch for logging trucks and drive with extreme caution.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are permitted. Fires must be kept to campfire rings if provided, or below the high tide line on the beach. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Mount Robson Park
parks.location:
Mount Robson Park is in east-central British Columbia, just west of the Alberta border and Jasper National Park. The park is approximately:
Four hours north of Kamloops on Highway 5
Three-and-a-half hours east of Prince George on Highway 16
Five hours west of Edmonton on Highway 16
The closest communities are Jasper, Valemount, and McBride. There are commercial airports in Prince George, Kamloops, and Edmonton. Rental vehicles are available at the airports.

facilities.name: EV Charging
facilities.detail:
Robson River
Six EV chargers are available at Mount Robson Welcome Centre. Two are 25 kW Delta chargers, and four are J-1772 compatible with a 7.3 kW output. To learn more information about the chargers available, visit PlugShare.com.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
There are picnic tables on the Berg Lake Trail and in the Corridor area. Picnic tables are available on a first come, first served basis. There are no fees for picnicking, and tables cannot be reserved.
Berg Lake Trail
Picnic tables are available at the south end of Kinney Lake. This area is approximately 5 km from the parking lot and trailhead. The tables are available for day-hikers as well as for campers who are hiking the entire trail.
Corridor
There are various picnic sites along the highway corridor. These span East Portal, at the park’s eastern entrance, to the Mount Robson Park viewpoint at the western boundary.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail:
Berg Lake Trail
There are pit toilets at all campgrounds on the Berg Lake Trail. Toilet paper is not provided at any sites along trail, so come prepared.
Corridor
All day-use picnic areas along the highway corridor have pit toilets. There are no flush toilets in the Corridor area.
Robson Meadows, Robson Rivers, Lucerne
Pit toilets are available at the Robson Meadows, Robson River, and Lucerne campgrounds. Robson Meadows and Robson River also have flush toilets.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: Hot showers are available at Robson Meadows and Robson River campgrounds.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
Berg Lake Trail
Boil, filter, or otherwise treat water from all sources on the Berg Lake Trail before drinking or using it for anything.
Corridor
Safe drinking water is available at the Welcome Centre in the Mount Robson Corridor area.
Robson Meadows and Robson River
There are cold-water taps throughout the campgrounds. Taps are shut off during the off season.
Lucerne
Well water is available via two hand pumps. Boil, filter, or otherwise treat water before drinking or using it for anything else.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Berg Lake Trail
East Portal
Lucerne Campground
Moose Lake day-use area
Robson Meadows Campground
Robson River Campground

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail:
Robson Meadows
The Robson Meadows Campground includes a children’s playground.
Welcome Centre
A playground and climbing frame are at the west end of the Welcome Centre.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station is available on Kinney Lake Road next to the Welcome Centre.
Sani-station fee$5 per discharge

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Berg Lake Trail, Corridor
Campfires are not allowed on the Berg Lake Trail or in the Corridor area. Use a camping stove for cooking. Anyone found starting or maintaining an open fire may be ticketed or, in some cases, evicted from the park.
Robson Meadows, Robson River, Lucerne
Campfires are allowed in these areas. We provide campfire rings at each campsite in Robson Meadows, Robson River, and Lucerne campgrounds. You can buy firewood from the park operator or campground host.
Campfire etiquette
To preserve plants and ground cover, do not gather firewood in the park. Gathering firewood is an offence under the Park Act.
If you bring firewood, buy it locally. Wood from other areas can spread invasive species. To learn more, visit Buy Local, Burn Local.
Please keep you’re your campfire small, to help maintain air quality. Bring a camping stove for cooking.

facilities.name: Electrical hook-ups
facilities.detail:
Robson River
Robson River Campground offers 15-amp, 30-amp, and 50-amp electrical hook-ups at 22 campsites (sites 20 to 41). There is an additional charge of $8 per night for these sites, whether you use power or not. For more information on this campground, see the frontcountry camping section.
Fees (per night)
Electrified sites
(15, 30, or 50-amp service)$8 (in addition to regular camping fee, whether power is used or not)

facilities.name: Information
facilities.detail: The Mount Robson Welcome Centre is at the park’s western entrance. It is within easy walking distance of campgrounds, a restaurant, a gift store, and a gas station. The Welcome Centre provides information on Mount Robson Park and BC Parks. The centre also features natural history displays.

parks.name: Mount Sabine Ecological Reserve
parks.location: On Mount Sabine, 3km north by north east of Canal Flats.

parks.name: Mount Savona Park
parks.location: The park is located off Highway 1 approximately 35 km west of Kamloops. Access is by Tunkwa Lake Road from the town of Savona.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: No firewood is available and no fire rings are installed. The gathering of firewood in a park is illegal, so fires should only be used for emergency drying and warming. If a fire is used for an emergency, please keep it small, and ensure it is completely out before you leave. Use a camp stove for cooking.

parks.name: Mount Seymour Park
parks.location:
The entrance to Mount Seymour Park is on Mount Seymour Road, just north of Mount Seymour Parkway in North Vancouver. It is 15 km northeast of downtown Vancouver via the Second Narrows Bridge and Mount Seymour Parkway. The closest communities are Deep Cove, North Vancouver, and Lynn Valley.
Year-round the gate just above parking lot 2 is closed nightly from 10 pm to 6 am.
During the winter, a BC Parks gatehouse operates at the base of Mount Seymour Road. From November to mid-April, the gate there is closed nightly from 10 pm to 7 am to allow snowplows to clear the road.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
Free day-use vehicle passes may be required to visit in the winter. Visit the day-use passes page for details.
Check the trail conditions report before heading out.
Baden Powell trailhead
This area provides parking for about seven vehicles. There are two picnic tables under the forest canopy on the east side of the road. Access includes a steep incline. There is one pit toilet and an information kiosk with a park map.
Vancouver picnic area
There are three tables available, as well as a pit toilet and park information shelter. Expect this area to be very busy throughout the year.
Deep Cove lookout
Deep Cove lookout is a popular destination for great views west toward the Fraser Valley and Mount Baker. Facilities include a pit toilet, park information shelter, and parking for approximately 15 vehicles. There are no picnic tables at this site.
Mount Seymour trailhead
This area at the end of Mount Seymour Road includes information kiosks at the base of Mt Seymour Resort controlled recreation area. Flush toilets are available, as well as a cafeteria, telephone, and change rooms. In the summer, picnic tables are set in a grassy area just north of the parking lot.
For maps, see maps and location.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.detail: Pit and flush toilets are located throughout the park.

gate.note: The park is open year-round. The gate just past parking lot 2 is closed 10 pm to 6 am. Mid-November to mid-April, the gate at the base of Mount Seymour Road is closed from 10 pm to 7 am.

parks.operating_note: Mid-November to mid-April the Mount Seymour Road gate is closed 10 pm to 7 am.

parks.name: Mount Terry Fox Park
parks.location: Located adjacent to the west boundary of Mt. Robson Provincial Park, three hours from Prince George. Communities close by include Tete Jaune Cache, Valemount and McBride.

parks.name: Mount Tinsdale Ecological Reserve
parks.location: In the Palmer Range, 18km east by south east of Barkerville.

parks.name: Mount Tuam Ecological Reserve
parks.location: At the southeastern end of Saltspring Island, 4km south of Fulford Harbour.

parks.name: Mount Tzuhalem Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 4km east by north east of Duncan, Vancouver Island.

parks.name: Moyie Lake Park
parks.location: Approximately a 20 km (15 minute drive) south of Cranbrook on Highway 3/95. The small community of Moyie is located 5 km south of Moyie Lake Park.

facilities.name: Bike park
facilities.detail: A children’s bike park is available for the use and enjoyment of visitors staying in the campground.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station and dump is located adjacent to the gatehouse on the main access road in the park, which is available during the operating season.
Sani-station use fee: $5 per discharge

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator or you can bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small. Bring a portable stove for cooking.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please do not gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a large day-use and picnic area and beach backed by a grassy play area. A change house and flush toilets are provided. The buoyed swimming area is shallow so is suitable for children’s waterplay. Roofed picnic tables allow for a shady lunch spot.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: The playground in this park is located near the shower building at the north end of the campground.

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: Hot showers are available in the campground in this park. There is no additional fee for their use. The four unit (two men, two women) shower building is located at the north end of the campground near campsite number 56. Shower facilities are for campground visitors only.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Ten cold water taps are located throughout the campground and operational during the operating season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail:
The boat launch is a concrete double ramp launch located at the end of the campground. Milfoil plants must be removed from your boat prior to travelling through the park.
Park visitors should be aware of fluctuating water levels and the presence of underwater gravel deposits at the boat launch. Use caution while loading and unloading. Please look before you launch.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Two flush toilet buildings are located centrally at the north and south loops of the campground. Pit toilets are located throughout the campground. A flush toilet building and one pit toilet are located at the day-use area.

parks.operating_note: Opening dates depend on snow.

parks.name: Mud Lake Delta Park
parks.location: On the east end of Mud Lake, due east of Blue River and 230 km north of Kamloops on Highway 5. The park is accessible by boat via the North Thompson and Mud Rivers. There is an active logging road that can be used to access portions of the Park.

parks.name: Mudzenchoot Park
parks.location: The park is located about 90 km northwest of Fort St. James. The nearest road access is the Witch Forest Service Road off the Germansen Landing North road. (Map reference: 93N/1)

parks.name: Muncho Lake Park
parks.location: Muncho Lake Park can be accessed via the Alaska Highway at kilometre 681. The highway runs through the park and provides access to the two BC Parks campgrounds: Strawberry Flats and MacDonald.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Macdonald
Strawberry Flats

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Hand pumps provide drinking water throughout Muncho Lake Park. These pumps are only available during peak season.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: A boat launch is available at MacDonald Campground. For a map with the boat launch location, see maps and location.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed at vehicle-accessible campgrounds in Muncho Lake Park. Fire rings are provided at each campsite. Campfires are allowed in fire rings only. Campfires are not allowed in the backcountry.
Do not gather firewood in the park. This is an offence under the Park Act. Dead wood is important habitat for plants and animals, and it adds valuable organic material to the soil.
If you bring your own firewood, buy it locally. Wood from other areas can spread invasive species. To learn more, visit Buy Local, Burn Local. You can buy firewood in the park. For firewood prices, contact the park operator.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Muncho Lake Park has a small day-use and picnic area next to the boat launch at MacDonald Campground. This area has one picnic table and parking spots for two vehicles.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Muncho Lake Park has pit toilets only. There are no flush toilets in the park. For a map with pit toilet locations, see maps and location.

parks.name: Murrin Park
parks.location: Murrin Park is located 2 km north of Britannia Beach and 9 km south of Squamish alongside Highway 99.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
This park has a day-use and picnic area with picnic tables, three pit toilets, a grassy area, and a sandy beach. Some of the picnic tables have barbeque attachments. There are no shelters or change houses available.
The day-use area is very popular and busy during the summer months.

parks.name: Muscovite Lakes Park
parks.location: Located on the western edge of Williston Lake, approximately 135 km north of Mackenzie on the Finlay Forest Service Road. The Finlay Forest Service Road can be accessed at approximately 10 km north of McLeod Lake on Hwy 97.

parks.name: Myra-Bellevue Park
parks.location:
The protected area is southeast of Kelowna. It roughly encompasses KLO Creek to Bellevue Creek and up to Saucier Creek and Canyon Lake with a large exclusion in the centre that locals refer to as the “donut.” The upper portions of Pooley Creek are also excluded. There are two accesses off of McCulloch Road.
Myra (the main access)
Follow McCulloch Road past the golf course to the Myra Forest Service Road. Use caution since this section of paved road is narrow with blind corners. Once on the forest service road, follow it for 8 km to the large parking area. The road is gravel and can be rough. The gravel parking area is divided into two lots with a total of roughly 75 spots and lots of room to turn around. There are two pit toilets here, one of which is wheelchair-accessible. There is no parking beyond this point. Motorized vehicles are prohibited past this access to Myra Canyon.
June Springs
The other access is via the paved June Springs Road. Follow it for 6 km to the Little White Forest Service Road. Follow the unpaved forest service road for 4.5 km to the parking area. This road is also rough and passes through private property. There is a gravel parking area for roughly 33 vehicles and one pit toilet above the parking lot. Further along the rail bed there is more parking. At kilometre 1 there are two narrow pullouts, with 11 spots and 21 spots, and two pit toilets. There is no parking beyond this point. Motorized vehicles are prohibited past this access to Myra Canyon. Use extreme caution when driving around hikers and bikers on the road in.
Stewart Road East
This road accesses the lower elevation portion of the protected area popular with mountain bikers. It is unique in that it is so close to the urban area of Kelowna. In Kelowna, follow Benvoulin Road to Casorso Road to Bedford Road to Stewart Road East and the parking lot where there are two pit toilets.

facilities.name: Accessibility information

Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Myra Station
Ruth Station

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are two pit toilets located at the Myra trailhead, one located just beyond Trestle 8, one just beyond Trestle 1, three at the Ruth trailhead, and two at the Stewart Road East trailhead. Please do not put garbage in the pit toilets.

parks.name: Mᑫuqʷin/Brooks Peninsula Park
parks.location: The park is located approximately 20 km southwest of Port Alice on northwest Vancouver Island and is accessible primarily by boat, north from Quatsino Sound and south from Kyuquot Sound. Boaters can reference marine chart #3683 (Checleset Bay) and #3680 (Brooks Bay) for more information on this area. The use of water taxis and air charters is becoming more and more popular as a method of quickly reaching the park. These can be found in Kyuquot and Zeballos.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: While small fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you do have a fire, please utilize previously constructed fire rings and use small pieces of wood that will burn completely. If you can’t find a previously used site, try to construct your fire rings below the high tide mark. Never leave your fire unattended and practice “Leave No Trace” camping ethics.

parks.name: Nadina Mountain Park
parks.location:
Nadina Mountain Park is located in west-central British Columbia, approximately 42 km southwest of Houston. Access to the Park follows a radio controlled logging road. Public vehicles are permitted, but please proceed with caution and be aware that loaded logging trucks have the right of way.
Travel the Yellowhead Highway (Hwy 16) to the town of Houston.
Turn south 2 kilometres west of Houston onto the Morice River Forest Service Road (also known as the Huckleberry road). This Forest Service Road (FSR) is marked in kilometres starting at the Canfor Mill site near the Yellowhead Highway.
Driving 27 kilometres will bring you to the junction of the Huckleberry and Morice Lake Roads. Continue straight (south) on the Huckleberry Road to the Owen Lake Recreation Site just after the 39 kilometre marker.
Turn right into the rec site onto Klate Road, drive across a bridge, up a short hill and turn right at a Y in the road at 1 km.
Continue for 6 km to the end of this logging road. Park at the bottom of a clear-cut where the road becomes impassable to access the Nadina Mountain Trail.
Please note: A vehicle with generous clearance is required to travel the road after Owen Lake.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: There are no designated campsites or campfire rings on Nadina Mountain and there is no wood available on the summit plateau. It is highly recommended that hikers bring along a light cook stove.

parks.name: Nahatlatch Park
parks.location:

Turn right on Chaumox Road and cross the bridge to the west side of the Fraser River, and stay on Chaumox Road. Chaumox Road turns into Nahatlatch Forest Service Road about 10.5 km out of North Bend.
The park entrance is located on Nahatlatch Road approximately 26.5 km northwest of Boston Bar. It is identified with a park information shelter.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Each designated campground has one pit toilet. Swakum has two pit toilets.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a small rustic boat launch next to the Salmon Beach campground. The launch has a dirt surface and can accommodate a small motor boat or car top boat. Power boats are rarely used on these lakes.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small. Be prepared by bringing a portable stove for cooking. Due to high winds funneling through this valley, visitors are requested to keep their campfires small.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, it is prohibited to gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Naikoon Park
parks.location: Haida Gwaii is served by scheduled air transportation from Vancouver and Prince Rupert and by BC Ferries between Prince Rupert and Skidegate. Highway 16 that connects the island communities passes close to the south and west boundaries of the park providing access at Tlell, Mayer Lake, and north east of Masset. There is no developed access to the interior of the park. Park headquarters are on the highway just south of the Tlell River bridge, 45 km north of the Village of Queen Charlotte.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Potable water is available in park campgrounds and at the parks headquarters in Tlell. Hikers are advised to carry plenty of drinking water and must treat surface water due to risk of water-borne illness.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
An accessible beach mat (mobi-mat) is available in the summer months to support beach access.
Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Agate Beach
Mayer Lake
Misty Meadows
Tlell River
Tow Hill

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a rustic boat launch at the Mayer Lake day-use area. It is suitable for launching canoes, kayaks, and small boats.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead. Always ensure that fires are completely extinguished when they will be untended.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
Naikoon Park has wheelchair-accessible picnic facilities in the day-use areas at:
Agate Beach Campground
Mayer Lake
Misty Meadows Campground
Tow Hill

parks.name: Nairn Falls Park
parks.location: This park is off Highway 99, approximately 92km north of Squamish, 32km north of Whistler and within the boundaries of the Village of Pemberton, just five minutes from Pemberton town center.
