facilities.detail: There are accessible pit toilets throughout Tyhee Lake Park. Tyhee Lake Campground and the day-use area both have accessible flush toilets.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: The day-use area in Tylee Lake Park has an adventure playground. Tyhee Lake Campground has a children’s bike track.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
Tyhee Lake Park has a coin-operated sani-station at the park entrance.
Fees (per use)
Sani-station$5

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: Tyhee Lake Campground and the day-use area both have shower buildings.

parks.name: Tā Ch'ilā Park [a.k.a. Boya Lake Park]
parks.location: There is a 2 km access road east of Highway 37 that leads into the park. It is located about 150 km north of the town of Dease Lake, and about 285 km north of Kinaskan Lake Park.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: One cold water pump is located in the park, near the information shelter at the entrance to the campground. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a boat launch southeast of the campground. 9.9 hp boat engines or electric motors only please.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: There is a day use picnic area adjacent to Boya Lake with picnic tables, fire rings, and a large picnic shelter.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: There is a small playground in the day-use area.

parks.name: Tŝi ʔEẑɨsh Ecological Reserve
parks.location: This ecological reserve is located 70km south west of Hanceville, Chilcotin District.

parks.name: Ugʷiwa'/Cape Caution Conservancy
parks.location: The Ugʷiwa’/Cape Caution Conservancy is located just South of Smith Inlet on British Columbia’s Central Coast. It is 56 km of Port Hardy, 196 km northwest of Campbell River and 400 km northwest of Vancouver.

parks.name: Ugʷiwa'/Cape Caution – Blunden Bay Conservancy
parks.location: The Ugʷiwa’/Cape Caution – Blunden Bay Conservancy is located just on British Columbia’s Central Coast and found 60 km north of Port Hardy, 217 km northwest of Campbell River, and 407 km northwest of Vancouver.

parks.name: Uncha Mountain Red Hills Park
parks.location: Uncha Mountain Red Hills Park is located on Francois Lake, approximately 30 km south of Burns Lake. The Red Hills portion of the park is reached by road from Burns Lake via Highway 35 to the community of Francois Lake, then east along Francois Lake East Road. Uncha Mountain is reached by taking the public ferry at the community of Francois Lake south across the lake, then following Uncha Lake Road east to Uncha Mountain Forest Service Road.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

parks.name: Union Passage Marine Park
parks.location: Union Passage Marine Park is located at the southern end of Grenville Channel, between Pitt and Farrant Islands. The closest communities are Hartley Bay (12 km), Kitimat (90 km), Port Edward (105 km) and Prince Rupert (120 km). Only accessible by boat or floatplane. For reference, use marine charts #3945 (Approaches to Douglas Channel), #3946 (Grenville Channel) or #3742 (Otter Passage to McKay Reach).

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: No firewood or fire rings are available. If you must make a fire, please keep it minimal. Before you leave, make sure the campfire is extinguished and spread the ashes and rocks about.

parks.name: Upper Adams River Park
parks.location:
The park is a very long, narrow strip that roughly follows the Upper Adams River and protects the riparian area on both sides of the river, from the north end of Adams Lake to a point north of Tum Tum Lake.
Three routes, all gravel logging roads, access this area:
from Highway 5 south of Barriere, via Agate Bay Road and along the west side and northern end of Adams Lake (80 km).
from Trans Canada Highway 1 at Squilax to Adams Lake roads (95 km).
from Highway 5 at Vavenby, via logging roads (30 km).
Use caution when traveling on logging roads. This is an active logging area.
The nearest communities are Kamloops, Clearwater, Barriere, Vavenby and Little Fort. The closest public telephone is at Vavenby Store, approximately 30 km away.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has user maintained pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is no boat launch, but there is opportunity to launch small car top boats.

parks.name: Upper Elaho Valley Conservancy
parks.location: The conservancy is located approximately 60 kilometres southwest of Pemberton and approximately 100 kilometres northwest of Squamish.

parks.name: Upper Kimsquit River Conservancy
parks.location: The conservancy is located approximately 55 kilometres northwest of Bella Coola and 75 kilometres northeast of Bella Bella.

parks.name: Upper Klinaklini Protected Area
parks.location: Upper Klinaklini Protected Area is approximately 60 kilometres southeast of Bella Coola and 150 kilometres northeast of Port Hardy.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Campfires are permitted, but rings are not provided. Be fire safe, and check the BC Wildfire website during high-risk times.

parks.name: Upper Lillooet Park
parks.location:
The park is located approximately 150 km northwest of Vancouver or 60 km northwest of Pemberton at the headwaters of the Lillooet River.
To reach Upper Lillooet Park, visitors drive to Pemberton and then along the Upper Lillooet forest service road on the north side of the Lillooet River, approximately 70 km to the boundary of the park. The road ends just outside the park boundary. Rough logging roads extend up Meager Creek towards the south end, but not into, the park. Helicopter access, with a valid permit, has been moderately popular mostly for accessing base camp areas in the alpine portions of the park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Campfires are permitted. Fires must be attended at all times, and fully extinguished prior to leaving. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.

parks.name: Upper Raush Protected Area
parks.location: Located on the south west side of the Fraser River, just south of McBride, these protected areas have no road access or facilities of any kind. There is an old road on the east side of the Raush River, on private land, and permission from the owner must be obtained.

parks.name: Upper Seymour River Park
parks.location: The park is accessed by 40 kilometres of generally good two-wheel drive gravel roads from the community of Seymour Arm, which in turn is a 40 kilometre drive on gravel surface from the end of the paved road on the north shore of Shuswap Lake.

parks.name: Upper Shuswap River Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Upper Shuswap River valley, 50km north by north east of Cherryville.

parks.name: Upper Soo Conservancy
parks.location: The conservancy is located approximately 25 kilometres northwest of Whistler and 22 kilometres southwest of Pemberton.

parks.name: Valhalla Park
parks.location: The park is located on the west shore of Slocan Lake, north of both Slocan and Castlegar. It encompasses most of the Valhalla Range of the Selkirk Mountains. The park can be accessed by water, forest industrial roads or by trail. The nearest community to the park is Slocan and Highway 6 provides access to the town as well as other population centres in the vicinity. Public boat launches exist in a number of towns, including Slocan, Silverton and New Denver, by which trailheads can be easily reached.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: Boat accessible beach areas provide day-use and picnic opportunities.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfire pits are provided at established Slocan Lakeshore sites.
Drinnon, Wicca and Gwillim lakes campgrounds have cooking areas but campfires are not allowed there.
Where campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Vance Creek Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 6km north of Lumby.

parks.name: Vargas Island Park
parks.location: Vargas Island Park is located immediately northwest of Tofino and west of Meares Island on the west coast of Vancouver Island. The park is accessible by boat from Tofino. Small planes can land on the beach of Ahous Bay. Nearby communities include: Tofino, Ucluelet, Ahousat, Flores Island.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There are six pit toilets located at Vargas Island’s most popular camping beaches.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: While small fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you do have a fire please use small pieces of wood that will burn completely and keep the fire below the high tide mark. Never build your fire near the beach log piles as the fire could ignite the logs and get out of control. Also do not leave your fire unattended and practice “Leave No Trace”.

parks.name: Vaseux Lake Park
parks.location: About 25 km south of Penticton on Highway 97. The closest communities are Okanagan Falls and Oliver.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area located off the Canadian Wildlife Service, Environment Canada Waterfowl Sanctuary parking lot. There are two pit toilets visible from the gravel parking lot. The two picnic tables are down a short path to the lake in a small grassy area surrounded by thick shrubs. There is an information kiosk here with facts about the wildlife in the area.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: A hand pump is available in the park. Interior Health has issued a permanent boil-water advisory on this source.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park, as well as the park's Wildlife Centre.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has four pit toilets, no flush toilets.

parks.name: Victor Lake Park
parks.location: Located 14 km west of Revelstoke. There is no public access into the park. The closest communities to this park are Revelstoke, Three Valley Gap and Sicamous.

parks.name: Vladimir J. Krajina (Port Chanal) Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Middle west coast of Graham Island, Haida Gwaii, 35km west of Justatla.

parks.name: Wakes Cove Park
parks.location: Wakes Cove is located on the northeast corner of Valdes Island, south of Gabriola Island and southeast of Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. Access to the park is by boat only and is situated next to Gabriola Passage. Boaters can reference marine chart #3475 for more information on this area. Nearby communities include: Gabriola Island and Nanaimo.

parks.name: Wales Harbour Conservancy
parks.location:
The conservancy is located approximately 40 kilometres north of Prince Rupert.
Wales Harbour Conservancy: Overview [PDF]
Wales Harbour Conservancy: Context [PDF]

parks.name: Walhachin Oxbows Park
parks.location: On the Thompson River west of Kamloops, approximately 30 km east of the town of Cache Creek, situated just downstream from the mouth of the Deadman River. There is no road access. Access is by boat from the west end of Kamloops Lake.

parks.name: Wallace Island Marine Park
parks.location: Wallace Island Marine Park is only accessible by boat. This park lies in Trincomali Channel between Galiano Island and the northern tip of Saltspring Island, off southern Vancouver Island. Boats can enter the sheltered anchorages at Princess Bay and Conover Cove from Houston Channel. Boaters can reference marine chart #3442 and #3463 for more information on this area. Nearby communities include: Galiano Island, Saltspring Island, Victoria, Nanaimo, Duncan.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit toilets are located at Conover Cove and Chivers Point.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
A picnic shelter and open grass fields offer day-use opportunities at Conover Cove. Dock facilities use fee: $2 per metre per night
A $20 fee is added for anyone who is not a B.C. resident. For more information, visit the non-resident fee section of the camping fees page.
Docking facilities are located at Conover Cove, as well as stern tie rings at both Conover Cove and Princess Cove. Anchorage is available in Conover Cove and Princess Cove. When anchoring, please ensure you are not blocking stern tie rings or access to and from the docks. The entrance to Conover Cove is shallow at low tide and care must be exercised to avoid grounding. Boaters should not tie up at the portion of the dock reserved for BC Parks staff.

parks.name: Walloper Lake Park
parks.location: This park is located just off the Coquihalla Highway #5, 37 km south of Kamloops. Watch for highway signs for Lac Le Jeune Park.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: An undeveloped area provides launching for small boats, only.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

parks.name: Walsh Cove Park
parks.location: Located on the east side of West Redonda Island on the Waddington Channel, north of Desolation Sound.

parks.name: Wapiti Lake Park
parks.location:
Wapiti Lake Park is located about 60 km south of Tumbler Ridge in the upper portions of the Wapiti River drainage. It is accessed via the Ojay Main Road. Follow this road to kilometre 29 and turn right onto the 2500 road (at approximately 25 km) a road that leads to an old well site. The trail starts at the southwest corner of this site.
The trail is approximately 18 km and follows the north side of the Wapiti River and the shores of a few smaller lakes. A view of Wapiti Falls can be achieved by following a short 200 metre trail off the main trail at kilometre 7. Be sure to bring your camera, as the scenic views are plentiful.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has pit toilets, no flush toilets. A pit toilet is provided at the 19.2 km camping area.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Campfires are permitted. Firewood and a fire ring are provided at the designated camping area and backcountry cabin located on the northwest side of Wapiti Lake. While campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves, instead.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: There is a day-use area.

parks.name: Wasa Lake Park
parks.location: This park is located in south eastern British Columbia, 40 km north of Cranbrook or 102 km south of Radium Hot Springs and 1 km east of Highway 93/95. The closest communities are Kimberley located 35 km north west and Cranbrook located 40 km south of Wasa Lake.

facilities.name: Bike park
facilities.detail: A children’s bike park is located within the campground at the south end, near site 89, for the use and enjoyment of families staying in the campground.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
This park has four day-use and picnic areas, including 45 picnic sites.
Camper’s Beach
Camper’s Beach is located across from the campground and has a pit toilet, change house, picnic tables, sandy beach and a grassed area.
Horseshoe Beach
Horseshoe Beach is located 2 km north of the campground and has picnic tables, sandy beach, grassed area and a flush toilet building.
Grey Change Beach
Adjacent to Horseshoe Beach, Grey Change Beach has a day-use area, picnic tables, grassed area, a pebbly beach and one pit toilet. At the very north end of the lake is another day-use area. The Grey Change day-use area is open year-round.
Main Beach
Main Beach has a large sandy beach, grassed area, picnic tables, paved parking, and two pit toilets.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: There is an adventure playground located within Camper’s Beach day-use area. A children’s bike park is located within the campground at the south end, near site 89, for the use and enjoyment of families staying in the campground.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit and flush toilets are located throughout the park. Change houses are located at each day-use area.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: A boat launch is located on the east shore across from the campground at Camper’s Beach. It consists of a concrete pad capable of launching a large boat.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Accessibility information is available for this park, as well as these areas of the park:
Campers beach
Grey change house
Horseshoe Beach
Main Beach

facilities.name: Showers
facilities.detail: Hot showers are available at Wasa Lake, located near the front entrance of campground.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Ten cold water taps are located randomly throughout the campground. Each day-use area of the park also has a cold water tap. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station is located at the north end of the lake on Wasa Lake Park Drive and is available during the operating season.
Sani-station use fee: $5 per discharge

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator in some parks or you can bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please do not gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.
You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small. Bring a portable stove for cooking.

gate.note: Dates may change depending on snow. Trails accessible year-round as snow allows.

parks.operating_note: Gate opening dates depend on snow. Trails accessible year-round as snow allows.

parks.name: Weewanie Hot Springs Park
parks.location:
Weewanie Hot Springs Park is located on the east side of Devastation Channel, approximately 38 km south of Kitimat. Access is by boat only. Use Marine Chart #3743 (Douglas Channel) and NTS Map Sheet # 103 H/10 (Devastation Channel). The closest communities to this park are Kitimat and Kitamaat Village.
Visitor Information Centre:
Kitimat Visitor Information Centre
PO Box 214
2109 Forest Avenue
Kitimat, BC, Canada V8C 2G7
http://www.tourismkitimat.ca/
Email: info@tourismkitimat.ca
Phone: 250 632-6294 or 1-800-664-6554

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
This park has a day use and picnic area. Facilities include a 8 ft by 15 ft cement bathhouse for soaking in hot springs water, one pit toilet, one picnic table, one fire ring, and one campsite.
The UTM coordinates for the bath house are: Zone 9U 5949861 m North; 0513888 m East.
The UTM coordinates for the campsite are: Zone 9U 5949793 m North; 0513945 m East.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park only has one pit toilet (no flush toilets) which is located about 50 metres uphill from the hot springs bath house.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: Please conserve firewood. Campfires are permitted, but firewood is not provided. We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of campfires and using campstoves instead.

facilities.name: Hot spring
facilities.detail:
Location: East side of Devastation Channel, in small bay 700 m north of Weewanie Creek, about 40 km south of Kitimat.
GPS: Lat. 53° 41’ 49” North; Long. 128° 47’ 21” West
Pool Water Temperature: 39°C
Facilities: Wood frame and concrete block bathhouse (8 ft by 15 ft) just above high tide line. The concrete block soaking pool inside is about 8 ft by 8 ft by 3 ft deep. It has a pit toilet and campsite with a picnic table and fire ring.
Comments: The waters are odorless. Short 300 m trail from the bathhouse SE to the campsite.

parks.name: Wells Gray Park
parks.location:
Core area
Wells Gray Park’s core area includes many popular campgrounds, day-use sites, and backcountry trails. The Wells Gray core includes the Corridor, Clearwater/Azure Marine, Clearwater River, Spahats Creek, and Trophy Mountain areas. You can access these areas off Highway 5 at Clearwater.
The road to Helmcken Falls, a popular spot in the lower Corridor, is open year-round. But, in winter, some parking areas in the lower Corridor may be unusable. Find a plowed parking area and hike to your destination from there. The road to Clearwater Lake and the upper Corridor is closed mid-December to mid-May.
Murtle Lake area
You can access Murtle Lake off Highway 5 at Blue River. Drive 27 km west on a narrow, winding gravel road to find the Murtle Lake parking lot. From the parking lot, you can hike a 2.5 km level trail, which leads to a canoe launch. This trail is suitable for canoe carts.
Mahood Lake area
The Mahood Lake area is at the south-western tip of Wells Gray Park. Access to this area is a considerable distance from the park’s other popular areas. You can access the Mahood Lake area via Highway 24, either from Highway 97 near 100 Mile House or from Highway 5 at Little Fort.
For more details, see the page for the area you are visiting:
Backcountry areas
Clearwater/Azure Marine
Clearwater River
Corridor area
Mahood Lake
Murtle Lake
Spahats Creek
Trophy Mountain

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Clearwater Corridor
Clearwater Lake
Falls Creek
Mahood Lake
Pyramid
Spahats Creek
Visitor Centre

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail:
A boat launch is available for visitors to the Clearwater/Azure Marine area. It is at the end of Wells Gray Park Road, near the southern end of Clearwater Lake.
A second boat launch is available in the Mahood Lake area, next to the frontcountry campground.
If you are parking overnight at this boat launch, please let the park operator know when you plan to return.
For park operator details, see the contact section. For a map of boat launch locations, see maps and location.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed only in the fire rings provided at frontcountry campsites. We encourage you to protect the environment by minimizing campfires and bringing a camping stove for cooking.
Do not gather firewood from anywhere in the park. This is an offence under the Park Act. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals. It also adds valuable organic matter to the soil.
If you bring your own firewood, buy it locally or in the park. Wood from other areas can spread invasive species. Please contact the park operator for information about buying firewood.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
Cold-water taps are available in some areas of Wells Gray Park. Specifically, taps are available at Spahats Creek day-use area and the Clearwater Lake/Falls Creek and Pyramid campgrounds.
Taps are not provided in the Corridor and Mahood Lake day-use areas. Drinking water is not provided anywhere in the Clearwater/Azure Marine, Mahood Lake, and Murtle Lake Marine areas.
Mahood Lake Campground has a permanent boil water advisory. Also, always boil or otherwise purify lake or creek water from anywhere in the park before using it for anything.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail:
There are picnic areas throughout Wells Gray Park. Day-use visitors can use picnic areas in the Clearwater/Azure Marine, Corridor, and Mahood Lake, and Spahats Creek areas.
Clearwater/Azure Marine
Day-use picnickers can use the marine campsites closest to the boat launch when these are not occupied by campers.
Corridor
There are 10 day-use areas in the Corridor area, with several picnic tables at each. Campfires are not allowed in these picnic areas.
Mahood Lake
There is parking for approximately 40 vehicles in the Mahood Lake day-use area. Campfires are not allowed in the day-use area, and water is not provided.
Spahats Creek
There is parking for approximately 40 vehicles in the day-use area at the Clearwater Valley viewpoint.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Spahats day-use area has flush toilets. The rest of the park has pit toilets only.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: Mahood Lake has an excellent adventure playground ideal for small children. This area also has a horseshoe pit next to the campground and a large, grassy playing field for ball games.

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station is available when campgrounds are operating. The sani-station is in the Corridor area, between Falls Creek and Clearwater Lake campgrounds.
Fees (per use)
Sani-station$5

gate.note:
The park is open year round.
The road to Helmcken Falls is open year-round, but the road to Clearwater Lake and the upper corridor is closed mid-December to mid-May. In winter, parking areas in the lower corridor may not be plowed but, where there is safe parking, visitors can access trails on foot.

parks.name: West Arm Park
parks.location: This park is situated east of Nelson and south of the West Arm of Kootenay Lake.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: There are beach picnicking areas in the park. Beach areas are boat access only and user maintained.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
We encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: West Lake Park
parks.location: West Lake Park is located 22km southwest of Prince George on the Blackwater Road on the north shore of West Lake.

facilities.name: Picnic shelters
facilities.detail:
For groups, two picnic shelters are available. A wood stove, horseshoe pitches, and a playfield make year-round fun available for groups of up to 100. One of the shelters is enclosed for optimum use during cooler weather and is available on a first come, first served basis. The other shelter can be reserved for group use.
You can make a reservation online at camping.bcparks.ca or by calling 1-800-689-9025 (1-519-858-6161 internationally). For detailed information, see the picnic shelters page.
Group picnicking fee: $50 per group
A $20 fee is added for anyone who is not a B.C. resident. For more information, visit the non-resident fee section of the camping fees page.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: West Lake’s day-use area has all the ingredients for an ideal family outing. Sunbathers will find a perfect spot to spread a blanket on the expansive sandy beach or under the shady cottonwood trees. Nearby change houses and picnic tables make it easy to spend an entire day enjoying this beautiful setting near the water. For energetic visitors looking for a little light-hearted competition, a play field, volleyball net and horseshoe pitches are provided.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit and flush toilets are located throughout the park.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There is a double concrete boat launch, complete with parking lots. The boat launch area is closed daily from dusk to 8am during the summer months. The boat launch opens May 1 and closes October 30.

parks.name: West Shawnigan Lake Park
parks.location: West Shawnigan Lake Park is located north of Victoria on southern Vancouver Island. Turn west off Highway 1 at Shawnigan/Mill Bay Road in Mill Bay. Follow the road approximately 15km to Shawnigan Lake, then turn right onto Shawnigan Lake Road. Follow this road until you reach the park. Nearby communities include Shawnigan Lake, Cobble Hill, Mill Bay, Cowichan.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area on the sandy northwest shores of Shawnigan Lake. Facilities included picnic tables, pit toilets, a grassy area and a change house.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit toilets are located near the parking lot and at the beach day-use area.

parks.name: West Twin Park
parks.location:
To access Boulder Mountain Hike, drive 166 km from Prince George on Highway 16 toward McBride and at the Goat River Forestry Road, turn in and drive another 1 km. Where a side road turns left park your vehicle. This is where the hike begins.
There is a popular hiking trail off the West Dore River Road (just northwest of McBride). This hike is 7 km to the cabin and then the hike can extend to various areas of the park.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area.

parks.name: Westwick Lakes Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 15km south of Williams Lake.

parks.name: Weymer Creek Park
parks.location: Weymer Creek Park is located 5 km southeast of the village of Tahsis on northwestern Vancouver Island. Access to the park is via a series of old and active logging roads off the road to Tahsis. Visitors should use caution when traveling these roads; logging vehicles have the right of way. Nearby communities include Tahsis, Gold River and Nootka Sound.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you must use a campfire, please practice “
Leave No Trace” camping ethics.

parks.name: Whaleboat Island Marine Park
parks.location: Whaleboat Island is located northeast of Ladysmith off the east coast of south Vancouver Island. This tiny island sits between Ruxton and Valdez Islands in Pylades Channel and is access is by boat only. Boaters can reference marine chart #3443 for more information on this area. Nearby communities include Ladysmith, Nanaimo, Yellow Point

parks.name: Whipsaw Creek Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 10km south west of Princeton.

parks.name: Whiskers Point Park
parks.location: Located 130 km north of Prince George on Highway 97. Communities close to this park include Mackenzie, Mcleod Lake, Bear Lake and Prince George.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: For swimmers and sunbathers, the sheltered sandy beach is perfect for tranquil outdoor relaxation. Nearby change houses, picnic tables and firepits makeit easy to spend a full day enjoying this natural playground. A picnic shelter near the day use area is ideal for covered activities. A playing field, horseshoe pitches, adventure playground and volleyball net provide something for every member of the family.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit and flush toilets are located throughout the park.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Cold water taps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Playground
facilities.detail: There is an adventure playground with accessible features in the picnic and day-use area.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: Boaters will find a convenient concrete boat launch, complete with parking area.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: White Lake Grasslands Protected Area
parks.location:
White Lake Protected Area encompasses the height of land west of Okanagan Falls from Mt. McLellan and Mount Hawthorne, wrapping around the vineyard, Green Lake and the community of Willowbrook as it continues down the west side of Vaseux Lake from Mt. Keogan to McIntyre Bluff and over to Myers Flats. The eastern face of Mt. Parker, overlooking St. Andrews Golf Course is also protected. The protected area does not include White Lake itself or the lower elevations of the basin; these are managed by the Nature Trust of British Columbia. Access to the protected area is via Green Lake Road and Fairview-White Lake Road.
The nearest communities are Twin Lakes, Willowbrook, Oliver, Penticton, Okanagan Falls.

parks.name: White Lake Park
parks.location: The park is located approximately 10 km northeast of the Trans-Canada Highway from Balmoral (west of Salmon Arm), the last 2 km is on a logging road. Balmoral, White lake, Tappen, Sorrento and Salmon Arm are the communities that are close to the park.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: An undeveloped boat launch area is suitable for small car-top type boats only. The lakeshore is suffering from extensive damage, so boaters are requested to please launch their boats in the main launching area only.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While campfires are allowed we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

gate.note: Dates may change depending on snow and lake freeze.

parks.operating_note: Gate opening dates depend on snow and lake freeze.

parks.name: White Pelican Park
parks.location: White Pelican Park is located approximately 60 km northwest of Williams Lake on the Chilcotin Plateau.

parks.name: White Ridge Park
parks.location: White Ridge Park extends from the boundary of Strathcona Park northwest to the Gold River Highway corridor. The park is located 4 km west of Gold River and is accessed off Gold River Highway 28 via Ucona Rd.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you must use a campfire, please practice “Leave No Trace” camping ethics.

parks.name: White River Park
parks.location: The park is located on the White River, approximately 25 km south of Sayward on northern Vancouver Island. The park is accessed by a gravel logging road off Hwy 19 from Sayward Junction.

parks.name: Whiteswan Lake Park
parks.location: Whiteswan Lake Park is located within the Kootenay Ranges of the Rocky Mountains, 22km southeast of the Village of Canal Flats, the nearest community. Access is from Highway 93/95, turn east 4.5 kilometres south of Canal Flats onto the gravel Whiteswan Forest Service Road. Whiteswan Lake is about 25km from the highway, the hot springs are located near the west boundary of the park at 17.5km.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: Pit toilets are located centrally in each campground; Home Basin (6), Inlet Creek (2), Packrat Point (2), Alces (4), Cave Creek (2), and White River (2).

facilities.name: Sani-station
facilities.detail:
A sani-station is available during the operating season at the entrance to Alces Campground. A water hose is available for rinsing, however, water is non-potable.
Sani-station use fee: $5.00 per discharge

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: There are four boat launches. Home Basin and Packrat Point which are concrete, Alces and Inlet Creek which are gravel. To ensure a quiet and relaxing experience, no towing is allowed on Alces or Whiteswan Lakes. Electric motors only are allowed on Alces Lake.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
Firewood can be purchased from the park operator in some parks or you can bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please do not gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park. Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.
You can conserve firewood and air quality by keeping your campfire small. Bring a portable stove for cooking.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has 3 day-use and picnic areas located at Packrat, Home Basin, and White River campgrounds. A day-use area at Lussier Hot Springs has a parking lot and pit toilet.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail:
Each of the campgrounds in the park have water provided by groundwater hand pumps.
A permanent boil water advisory is in effect. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail:
Accessibility information is available for these areas of the park:
Alces Lake
Home Basin
Inlet Creek
Lussier River Hotsprings
Pack Rat Point
White River

facilities.name: Hot spring
facilities.detail:
Lussier Hot Springs is located near the park entrance at 17.5km on the Whiteswan forest service road (FSR). The springs, long a favourite of campers and wilderness enthusiasts, can be accessed from the Whiteswan FSR by a short hike down to the Lussier River. Two pit toilets are located at the parking lot. Liquor, dogs, and smoking are not permitted at the hot springs. Garbage receptacles are located up at the parking area. Nudity is prohibited. Park Rangers make regular patrols to Lussier Hot Springs. Please help keep this wildland hot springs clean. Please be aware, Lussier Hot Springs are natural, and subject to climactic conditions, may sometimes run cool.
Attention winter users: The trail leading down to the hot pools can become very slippery during the winter, please use caution during your visit.

parks.name: Wilkinson-Wright Bay Conservancy
parks.location: The conservancy is located 75 kilometres west of Smithers and is accessible by boat 10 kilometres across Babine Lake, southeast of the Village of Granisle.

parks.name: Williams Creek Ecological Reserve
parks.location: South side of Williams Creek, 20km south east of Terrace.

parks.name: Willison Creek – Nelson Lake/Sít' Héeni Conservancy
Windermere Lake Park
parks.location: 10km South of Invermere on Westside Road

parks.name: Winter Inlet Conservancy
parks.location: The conservancy is located approximately 40 kilometres north of Prince Rupert.

parks.name: Wire Cache Park
parks.location: Located 90 km northeast of Clearwater, on the south side of the North Thompson River. Road access is poor. There is potential for a river pullout area. The closest communities are Clearwater, Vavenby, Avola, Blue River and Kamloops.

parks.name: Wistaria Park
parks.location: From Burns Lake, take Hwy 35 and cross Francois Lake on the ferry. Follow the main road from the ferry for 17.5 km and turn right onto Keefe’s Landing Road (Ootsa-Nadina Road). Follow this for 36.7 km to the signed road for Wistaria Park (on your left). If you reach Carroll Road you have gone too far. It is 700 m from the Keefe’s Landing (Ootsa-Nadina) Road to the lake.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: This park has pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Boat launch
facilities.detail: This park has a single-wide concrete boat launch with a gentle grade. Boaters must use caution on Oosta Lake due to weather conditions and underwater hazards such as submerged stumps and trees.

parks.name: Woodley Range Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 2km north of Ladysmith.

parks.name: Woodworth Lake Conservancy
parks.location: The conservancy is located approximately seven kilometres northeast of Prince Rupert.

parks.name: Woss Lake Park
parks.location: The park is south of the community of Woss on northern Vancouver Island. Access to the park is generally by boat from a launch at the north end of Woss Lake. Walk-in access to the northern portion of the park is possible from logging roads on either side of Woss Lake. Access to Rugged Mountain is through a steep and strenuous hike from logging roads outside the park in the vicinity of Zeballos Lake to the west.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: There is a composting toilet in this park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail: While fires are allowed, we encourage visitors to conserve the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using stoves instead. If you must use a campfire, please practice “Leave No Trace” camping ethics.

parks.name: Wrinkly Face Park
parks.location: The approach trail is located just north-east of Winfield, at the south-west end of Long Mountain, south of Vernon. The park is accessed via the Beaver Main Forest Service Road. From Highway 97 follow Beaver Lake Road for about 12 km to the High Rim trail head. Hike north about one hour to the park.

parks.name: Yaaguun Gandlaay Conservancy
parks.location: Yaaguun G̱andlaay Conservancy is located on the north end of Yakoun River, on Graham Island, Haida Gwaii, immediately southeast of the community of Port Clements.

parks.name: Yaaguun Suu Conservancy
parks.location:
Yaaguun Suu Heritage Site/Conservancy is located in the southwest corner of Graham Island approximately 2 kilometres from the western coast of Haida Gwaii/Queen Charlotte Islands at Shields Bay and 25 kilometres northwest of the community of Queen Charlotte. It is part of an archipelago-wide system of protected areas that includes Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve and Haida heritage Site, several provincial parks and ecological reserves, and ten other heritage site/conservancies. In total, half of the land base of Haida Gwaii is now in protected status.
It includes all of Yakoun Lake and its tributaries, with the exception of the eastern half of Etheline Bay and the outlet of Yakoun River. The eastern portion of Etheline Bay is encompassed by private property owned by Island Timberlands LP.

parks.name: Yahk Park
parks.location: Yahk Park is located along Highway 3/95, 70km south of Cranbrook, 14.5km north of the U.S. and Canadian borders at Kingsgate. This park is found on the south edge of the small community of Yahk.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use and picnic area with tables near the river.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: The park has four pit toilets, no flush toilets.

facilities.name: Drinking water
facilities.detail: Three cold water taps are located throughout the park. Taps are shut off during the off-season.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

facilities.name: Campfires
facilities.detail:
While campfires are allowed and campfire rings are provided at each campsite, we encourage visitors to conserve wood and protect the environment by minimizing the use of fire and using campstoves instead.
Firewood can be purchased in the park or you may bring your own wood. Fees for firewood are set locally and may vary from park to park.
To preserve vegetation and ground cover, please don’t gather firewood from the area around your campsite or elsewhere in the park (this is a ticketable offence under the Park Act). Dead wood is an important habitat element for many plants and animals and it adds organic matter to the soil.

parks.name: Yalakom Park
parks.location: This park is located approximately 60 kilometres northwest of Lillooet.

parks.name: Yale Garry Oak Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 2km north east of Yale.

parks.name: Yard Creek Park
parks.location: This park is located approximately 15 kilometres east of Sicamous, along the Trans Canada Highway.

parks.name: Yellow Point Bog Ecological Reserve
parks.location: Located 10km south of Nanaimo.

parks.name: Zumtela Bay Conservancy
parks.location:
The conservancy is located approximately 25 kilometres north of Prince Rupert.
Zumtela Bay Conservancy: overview [PDF]
Zumtela Bay Conservancy: context [PDF]

parks.name: ȽÁU,WELṈEW̱/John Dean Park
parks.location: ȽÁU,WELṈEW̱/John Dean Park is located near Sidney on southern Vancouver Island. The park can be accessed off Hwy #17. Turn west onto McTavish Road, south onto East Saanich Road, then west onto John Dean Road. Follow John Dean Road until you reach the park. Nearby communities include: Sidney, Saanichton, Brentwood Bay, Victoria.

facilities.name: Picnic areas
facilities.detail: This park has a day-use area with a parking lot, information shelter and a pit toilet. The park is blocked off by a gate, which is locked from dusk until 8am. This park is closed to vehicle traffic from November to March.

facilities.name: Pit or flush toilets
facilities.detail: A pit toilet is located near the parking lot.

facilities.name: Accessibility information
facilities.detail: Accessibility information is available for this park.

advisories.title: Myra Falls Mine access
advisories.description: To ensure public safety and maintain continued access through the active mine, the public is reminded to be respectful of the mine entrance "Checkpoint", obey all No Entry signs and follow directional signage to park trailheads/parking. Mine site conditions can change rapidly and industrial mine traffic is constantly active. While visitors are safe travelling through the mine along the main road corridor, there is a safety risk if deviating into No Entry areas. Thank you for your cooperation.

advisories.title: Public access to the column features is not permitted
advisories.description: Keremeos Columns Park does not contain the geological features that were intended to be protected at the time of establishment in the early 1930s. The column features are fully contained on private land. At this time, public access to the column features is not permitted. Viewing of the column features must be done so by using valley bottom vantage points that do not involve encroachment or access onto private land.

advisories.title: Klappan Rail Grade is impassible
advisories.description: The Klappan Rail grade has suffered a wash out at km 30. Eaglenest Creek Trail and Didene Portage trail are no longer accessible via the Klappan Rail Grade. Access to Spatsizi Plateau Wilderness Provincial Park is possible through air charter or via the McEwan Creek Trail.

advisories.title: Drinking water at Mahood Lake campground on permanent boil water order
advisories.description:
Park Visitors are advised to either bring their own potable water or boil water prior to consumption. Interior Health advises the following:
Boiling water is the most effective way to disinfect water, particularly if you think your water has parasites such as Giardia or Cryptosporidium, or if you have a weakened immune system.
Boil water for at least 1 minute. At elevations over 2,000 meters (6,500 feet) boil water for at least 2 minutes.
Store disinfected water in clean, covered, food grade containers
BC Parks is working with Interior Health and our Capital program and hopes to develop a new drinking water source at the Park in the near future. Unfortunately this will take some time. Please consult this web page for future updates.

advisories.title: Access to Lake Lovely Water trailhead
advisories.description: Access is from the west side of the Squamish River. The east side of the river is First Nations land and BC Parks does not recommend using the dirt road to access the trailhead due to land use issues. Use of the cable car is also prohibited. Helicopter and boat services are available, see the Location section below for further details.

advisories.title: Bear-proof canisters are mandatory
advisories.description: Due to the current popularity of the area, food storage is limited and only available at the main campground. Visitors must store their food in a bear proof canister away from their tent.

advisories.title: Campground capacity
advisories.description: Most sites previously closed for hazard trees resulting from a spruce beetle infestation have been made safe again and are re-opened. A few sites remain closed, please respect signage and stay out of closed areas.

advisories.title: Campfires are not permitted in this park
Fording the Athabasca River is not recommended
advisories.description: There is no estimated time for repair or replacement of this bridge.

advisories.title: Athabasca River suspension bridge failure
advisories.description: On October 1, 2014, the suspension bridge which crosses the Athabasca River in Jasper National Park, along the land access route to Hamber Park, failed.

advisories.title: The Washout Creek and Fortress Creek Campgrounds have been decommissioned due to dangerous trees
advisories.description: Please use at your own risk.

advisories.title: Boiling water advisory at Hicks Lake
advisories.description: Visitors are advised to boil water for at least two minute before drinking.

advisories.title: Porcupines chew brake and fuel lines. Wrap your parked vehicle with chicken wire.
advisories.description: If leaving your vehicle at the trail head, we suggest that you surround your vehicle with chicken wire. Porcupines may chew rubber and cause damage.

advisories.title: No parking on Alice Lake Road
advisories.description: In order to maintain park safety and public security, all vehicles parked illegally and on road edges will be subject to towing at the owner’s expense.

advisories.title: Illegally parked vehicles will be towed
advisories.description:
Vehicles parked illegally at Porteau Cove Park will be subject to towing at the owner’s expense. Visitors must park in designated parking lots and observe the “no parking” signs posted.
Illegal parking has become a safety issue at Porteau Cove Park, with vehicles blocking access for emergency response and people parking along the highway. Thank you for making a visit to Porteau Cove safe for everyone.

advisories.title: Kennedy Lake Park is a day-use park
advisories.description:
Camping and overnight parking is strictly prohibited.
Anyone found in the park between 11pm and 7am will be evicted and will receive violation tickets.

advisories.title: The Nels Bight and Cape Sutil Ranger Station Cabins will be closed to public access until further notice
advisories.description: Campers must be self-sufficient and prepared to camp at all locations within the park. Thank you for your cooperation.

advisories.title: Caution: Due to historic military training exercises in the Cosens Bay area, Unexploded Ordinance (UXOs) may be present
advisories.description: Please stay on designated trails at all times. If a UXO is encountered, do not touch it and call 911.

advisories.title: Hazardous conditions
advisories.description: The conditions on the Gitnadoiks River are known to change quickly due to fluctuating water levels, both seasonally and in response to weather events. Rapidly fluctuating flow conditions (within hours) can occasionally result in unpredictable hazards, including submerged woody debris, complete channel obstructions (such as log jams, landslides, rock falls), and river channel changes. Travel cautiously and anticipate the chance that you may suddenly encounter other jetboat traffic.

advisories.title: No camping or campfires are permitted in this park at any time
Off-road vehicle registration is mandatory
advisories.description: Starting in 2015, off-road vehicle registration is mandatory on crown land, including on forest service roads. Find out more at: Off-Road Vehicle Management Framework.

advisories.title: Vehicle use in Chemainus River Park is restricted to Hillcrest Road (Forest Service Road)
advisories.description: Driving on park trails disrupts and damages natural areas. Operators of vehicles found off-road may be fined under the Park, Conservancy and Recreation Area Regulation (minimum $575, maximum $200,000).

advisories.title: Parking lot closed for winter months
advisories.description: The parking lot will be closed during winter months and will reopen in the spring. The park remains open and can still be accessed on foot.

advisories.title: Snowmobile use is not permitted in any area of Elk Lakes Park
advisories.description: The previous special exemption to use snowmobiles to access Abruzzi Lake along the seismic corridor is no longer in effect. The entire park is closed to all motorized activities. Non-compliance of the motorized closure will result in enforcement actions.

advisories.title: Trail condition in poor shape - Travel not recommended
advisories.description: Please be advised the trail up to the Holliday Creek Arch is in very bad shape with windfall, washouts and several areas where detours are required. Travel is not recommended unless you are prepared for these conditions.

advisories.title: Off-Road Vehicles prohibited
advisories.description: Off-Road Vehicles (ORVs) are prohibited in this ecological reserve. ORVs include ATVs, off-road motorcycles, snowmobiles and side-by-sides.

advisories.title: Park closure reassessed and amended
advisories.description:
In May 2019, BC Parks closed the Nlháxten/Cerise Creek Conservancy after two landslides from Joffre Peak heavily impacted the Cerise Creek watershed within the Conservancy.
BC Parks has reassessed the closure and the closure area has been amended. Public access is not permitted within the immediate slide path as outlined in red on the map posted on the Nlháxten/Cerise Creek Conservancy website. There is one temporary route located at the midpoint of the landslide track. This route is unmaintained and is not a designated trail. The time crossing the path must be minimized. The remaining areas of the Conservancy are now open to public access.
The Keith Flavelle Hut (Keith’s Hut) is outside the closure area.
Signage has been posted at the trailheads and on the conservancy website.
BC Parks will be conducting a further assessment of the closure area in 2021.

advisories.title: Pets must be on leash at all times
advisories.description:
Kokanee Creek estuary area is important habitat for migratory and resident waterfowl and shorebirds. Thanks for doing your part to help sensitive wildlife by keeping your dog on a leash.
Pets/domestic animals must be on a leash at all times and are not allowed in beach areas. This applies year-round. A dog beach is beside the boat launch at the north-east end of the park. Park visitors are responsible for their behaviour and must dispose of their excrement.

advisories.title: Strathcona Park offers a Backcountry Host volunteer opportunity
advisories.description: Applications for the 2026 season are now closed.

advisories.title: Spill response complete
advisories.description:
Notice to Park Visitors
The spill response at Zuciarte Channel in Bligh Island Park is complete. A Canadian Coast Guard Marine Notice for the site remains in effect:
http://www.spillresponsebc.ca/marinenotice/

advisories.title: Cave and surrounding area is closed to public access
advisories.description:
Until risks to public safety have been assessed and engagement with First Nations has been concluded, the newly discovered cave and surrounding area is closed to public access as per the Directors Order [PDF].
Any member of the public in contravention of Order is subject to the following:
Under Section 17 of the Park Act, Section 28:
28 (1) A person who contravenes any provision of this Act commits an offence and is liable to a fine of up to $1,000,000 or a term of imprisonment of not more than one year or both.
(3) When a contravention of the Act or regulations continues for more than one day, the person is guilty of a separate offence for each day on which the contravention continues.

advisories.title: Access to this protected area is from the Copper River Forest Service Road
advisories.description: Drive with caution. There may be rocks or wildlife on the road and other industrial traffic such as logging trucks, heavy machinery, or other vehicles.

advisories.title: Pets not permitted in Ripple Ridge or Lightning Strike cabin
advisories.description:
Pets are not permitted in Ripple Ridge or Lightning Strike cabin. For additional information:
Ripple Cabin – Recreation Sites and Trails BC
rippleridge.ca

advisories.title: Rock climbing, slacklining, hang-gliding not permitted
advisories.description: Rock climbing, slacklining, and hang gliding are unauthorized activities and are not permitted in the park.

advisories.title: Lakeside walking trail between campgrounds permanently closed
advisories.description:
Lakeside walking trail between campgrounds is permanently closed for public safety. The upper trail connecting the north and south portions of this park remains open.
A major landslide (Dec. 30, 2020) sent mature trees and massive amounts of debris across the trail and into the lake. The silt bluffs above the trail were studied by geotechnical engineers and found to be both unstable, and unpredictable. The next landslide event could happen anytime and without warning, and may injure, bury, or kill persons travelling through the area.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory in effect
advisories.description: The South Okanagan/Penticton Region Health Department has issued a year-round boil water advisory. Water must be boiled for a minimum of 5 minutes, filtered, or treated, prior to consumption.

advisories.title: Road to Paradise Bay Campground is single lane only but does not affect access to caves
advisories.description: A small section of the Horne Lake Road, located approximately 200m past the Horne Lake Caves Visitor Centre (approximate km marker 9.5), has been changed to single lane traffic only due to poor road condition. No vehicles more than 30 tonnes are allowed on this part of the road. Access to the Visitor Centre parking lot from Highway 19 is not affected by this traffic pattern change.

advisories.title: Be aware of thieves
advisories.description:
Lock up securely. Do not leave any valuables or personal information in vehicle while visiting the park.
Report any suspicious activity, theft, or damage to the police.

advisories.title: Be aware of thieves
advisories.description: Thieves have been known to operate in the Juan de Fuca area. Secure/remove all valuables if leaving your vehicle unattended. Any information regarding incidents of theft should be reported to the Sooke RCMP at 250-264-5241 or Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-8477

advisories.title: Volunteer host opportunities
advisories.description: Kootenay Lake Provincial Park offers volunteer host opportunities.

links.title: Contact the park operator for more information

advisories.title: Electric wildlife fence
advisories.description: Liard River Hot Springs Park is the first provincial park to have an electric fence installed. We will be keeping visitors and wildlife safe by reducing the amount of human-wildlife interactions at the park.

links.title: Learn more about the electric wildlife fence [PDF]

advisories.title: Road closures
advisories.description: The Clearwater River Road (the gravel road along the west side of the Clearwater River, used primarily by fishers and kayakers) is closed beyond the Kettle at 11 km, due to water damage. Updates will be provided as conditions change.

advisories.title: Wear clean caving gear to protect bats from White-Nose Syndrome
advisories.description:
White-nose Syndrome is a fungal disease that has been linked to the mass die-off of hibernating bats in Eastern North America – it poses a significant threat to bats of the west and British Columbia. There is evidence that humans have accelerated the spread through entering caves with contaminated clothing, gear or equipment. To help prevent WNS from taking hold in B.C., the Province is making investments in bat conservation projects.
To ensure the protection of bats and their habitat in this park, BC Parks strongly advises that personal caving gear that has been used anywhere east of the Rockies not be used in B.C. Also, before entering caves in B.C, cavers and visitors should consult the provincial WNS website, which includes a link to a Decontamination Protocol for Mines and Caves.
Learn more about white-nose syndrome

advisories.title: Guided Tours are now available in Cody Cave
advisories.description: Please check codycavetours.com for full details!

advisories.title: Protect bears by securing all food and garbage when away from your camp and at night
advisories.description: Bears are destroyed every year due to campers neglecting to properly manage their attractants. It is illegal to leave food and/or garbage unsecured and unattended. Store all food and scented items in a vehicle, hard-sided trailer, or bear-proof locker. Campers failing to ensure their camp is secure of attractants may be evicted from the park and issued a violation ticket under the BC Wildlife Act. Please do your part to ensure the safety of your family, fellow campers, and the local bears, by keeping a clean camp!

advisories.title: Amphitheatre closure
advisories.description: The climbing area known as the Amphitheatre is closed annually from May 1 to August 30, for the protection of the Peregrine falcon nest. The nesting season is a very sensitive time for these birds. Please respect this closure.

advisories.title: Silvertip Campground reconstruction
advisories.description: We are pleased to share that the Silvertip Campground reconstruction project is nearing completion. We are excited to welcome our guests to the newly rebuilt campground in the Spring of 2027.

advisories.title: Volunteer Host Opportunity
advisories.description: Mount Fernie Provincial Park offers volunteer host opportunities

links.title: Contact the park operator for more information

advisories.title: Illegally parked vehicles
advisories.description: Vehicles parked illegally at Stawamus Chief including the Apron parking lot will be subject to towing at the owner’s expense. Visitors must park in designated parking lots and observe the "no parking" signs posted. Vehicles parked illegally in closed day-use areas will be charged a fee for gate unlocking. Thank you for your compliance.

advisories.title: Momich Lake East Campground closed
advisories.description: Momich Lake East Campground and its access is closed due to slope instability caused by wildfire damage.

advisories.title: Help protect Bank Swallow habitat
advisories.description:
BC Parks has recently installed barriers along one of the boat accessible pocket beaches near the north end of Windermere Lake Park. These barriers have been installed to protect a sensitive Bank Swallow nesting colony area. Bank Swallows are classified as a threatened species federally and have suffered a 98% population decline in Canada over the last 40 years. Please help BC Parks protect this very important habitat and ensure you do not enter or disturb this area and keep all pets on a leash.
For more information please call 250 420-6285

advisories.title: Removing plants from the park is prohibitted
advisories.description: Removing plants from BC parks is prohibited and is contrary to section 32(1)c of the Park Act

advisories.title: Park access via Chute Lake Road
advisories.description: The road access from Chute Lake Road to the south parking lot very is rough, washed-out and overgrown. This road is not suitable for most vehicles.

advisories.title: Thieves are targeting vehicles in parking lots
advisories.description: Please protect yourself by not leaving any valuables in your vehicle. Report any suspicious activity to the RCMP.

advisories.title: Buttle Lake boat launch
advisories.description: Due to safety of vehicles and ramp material, only 4x4 vehicles are allowed to access the gravel area beyond the toe/bottom of the concrete ramp when the water is at or below this level.

advisories.title: Fires are not permitted anywhere or at any time
advisories.description: Fires are not permitted anywhere or at any time (all seasons) within Strathcona Park, except in authorized and provided BC Parks steel fire rings. This regulation is in effect at all times of the year. No open fires are allowed in any backcountry areas.

advisories.title: No motorized vehicles are permitted in the park
advisories.description:
Vehicle access to the northern boundary of the park via the Stawamus/Indian River Forest Service Road (maintained by the Squamish Forest District Office) from Squamish is “4WD access only; seasonally deactivated – Access may be limited beyond 10km, due to minor washouts.”
Road Conditions in the Sea to Sky District

advisories.title: Dogs prohibited at Joffre Lakes to protect park
advisories.description:
To protect the environment and wildlife at Joffre Lakes Provincial Park, dogs and other domestic pets are prohibited.
Information Bulletin

advisories.title: Joffre Lakes Park Visitor Use Management Strategy: Complete
advisories.description: BC Parks, in partnership with the Lil’wat Nation and N’Quatqua, has developed a Visitor Use Management Strategy (Joffre VUMS) to manage visitor use at Joffre Lakes Park. This strategy builds on the 2019 Visitor Use Management Action Plan for Joffre Lakes Park and provides long-term direction for management of Joffre Lakes Park.

advisories.title: Archaeological site
advisories.description: During the course of a facility improvement project in 2014, BC Parks uncovered an important archaeological site within the campground. With sẁiẁs Park now an archaeological site, the Province and Osoyoos Indian Band (OIB) have agreed that sẁiẁs and sx̌ʷəx̌ʷnitkʷ Parks will be managed by the OIB. Park visitors can expect the same recreational opportunities as before. BC Parks and OIB continue to collaborate on management that will ensure the long term protection of the cultural heritage values in the park and the strengthen their government to government relationship.

advisories.title: Be aware of industrial road conditions required to access this park
advisories.description: Gravel roads outside of the park are only maintained to industrial standards and may be very rough in some areas at any time. Road grading and drainage work was completed on the Morton Lake FSR during the fall of 2020 to alleviate significant pothole concerns.

advisories.title: Hazards due to wildfire damage
advisories.description:
There are significant risks associated with entering areas that have been burnt over by the 2017 wildfires.
Potential risks could include:
danger trees and overhead hazards – the integrity of trees whose trunks, roots or branches have been damaged by wildfire is unreliable
terrain instability resulting in landslides and falling or shifting debris and rock
amplified runoff after rainfall or snowmelt which could result in a rapid increase of water course depth and flow rates or flooding conditions
ash pits – may be deep and difficult to see
respiratory effects caused by breathing soot and charcoal for extended periods of time
Post-wildfire hazards may last for several years or longer after a wildfire and may be triggered at any time with little or no warning.

advisories.title: No parking along access road
advisories.description: As of 2021, vehicles parked along this road will be towed at the owner’s expense. New signage and physical barriers have been installed to make clear where parking is not allowed. [More info]

advisories.title: Dogs must be leashed at all times in the park
advisories.description: This park protects a rare and fragile ecosystem, and experiences increasing visitor numbers each year. Dogs impact park values, posing a threat to wildlife, ecology, and public safety. Keeping dogs leashed reduces their impact.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory
advisories.description: In effect for the north campground and south campgrounds until further notice.

advisories.title: Use extreme caution
advisories.description: High temperatures and rapid snow melt have led to unpredictable water flow and levels. Please use extreme caution at river crossings and while near the water’s edge. Be extra mindful of pets and children while hiking up the Lake Lovely Water trail.

advisories.title: The section of Ram Creek Forest Service Road which previously traversed through Ram Creek Ecological Reserve has been permanently deactivated
advisories.description: Motorized users are advised that the section of the Ram Creek Forest Service Road which previously traversed through Ram Creek Ecological Reserve has been permanently deactivated and reclaimed for public safety, due to significant debris torrent hazard to the geothermal site. All resource roads adjacent to Ram Creek Ecological Reserve remain open.

advisories.title: Whiteswan Park is bear country!
advisories.description: BC Parks is promoting a BARE Campsite program in the park and is asking all park users to help out by not leaving any unattended wildlife attractants in their campsites. Wildlife attractants include, but are not limited to: coolers (empty or full), garbage, BBQs, stoves, food, dishes/pots, fish/fish remains, pet food, gas/oil products, bird feeders, and toiletries. It is a legal requirement to properly store all wildlife attractants and keep a BARE campsite. When you leave your site unattended for any length of time or when you go to sleep at night please keep a BARE campsite. The BARE Campsite program is in place for your safety and to help keep the wildlife in our parks alive and well.

advisories.title: Camping and campfires are not allowed – no day-use facilities
Maitland Lake Cabin is no longer suitable for public use
advisories.description: In keeping with the approved park management plan, the cabin will not be repaired or replaced.

advisories.title: There is no longer a mooring buoy at Drewry Point
advisories.description: Please check this page for updates. Any updates regarding the mooring buoy will be posted here when available.

advisories.title: Access to Earl Grey Pass Trail from the Toby Creek Trailhead
advisories.description: To access the Earl Grey Pass Trail from the Toby Creek Trailhead, it is best to park at the trailhead and walk the 2 km to the park boundary; the road has been permanently deactivated. Follow the road to locate where the trail begins.

advisories.title: Trail Conditions
advisories.description:
For more information about hiking in the Purcell Wilderness Conservancy, read the Purcell Wilderness Conservancy Trail Information page.
The Birchdale Trail continues for 2km beyond the Fry Creek bridge. This trail ends at private property and there is no designated trail access to the community of Birchdale at this time.

links.title: Trail Conditions Report for the east end of the park
Trail Conditions Report for the west side of the park (scroll to the Purcell Wilderness Conservancy entry)

advisories.title: Visitors must be accompanied by a Guardian Watchman or permitted guide
advisories.description:
Khutze Conservancy rules and etiquette
Visiting the Khutze Estuary requires careful management to protect bears, maintain natural behaviors, and support visitor safety.
The following measures apply from August 15 to October 15. Visitors are asked to:
Check in with the Kitasoo Xai'xais Guardians on Marine VHF Channel 6 upon arrival, when Guardians are present.
Access the estuary only when accompanied by a Guardian, an approved guide, or an authorized operator.
Dogs are not allowed on shore in the estuary. This is to prevent disturbance of the bears, and for the protection of dogs and their owners.
Refrain from using drones unless authorized by permit.
Follow all posted rules and etiquette.

advisories.title: Dogs prohibited in estuary
advisories.description: Dogs are not allowed on shore in the estuary. This is to prevent disturbance of the bears, and for the protection of dogs and their owners.

advisories.title: The road to Eneas Lakes has been deactivated as of April 1, 2002
advisories.description: Access to the park is by 4x4 vehicle only. Recommend packing along a chainsaw, for it is common to find trees and debris across the road on your way in. There is no signage on the forestry road to Eneas Lakes; you should have a good forestry map for the area.

advisories.title: High-clearance vehicle is recommended
advisories.description:
The Dore River Forest Road into the Ozakenka Trailhead is narrow, with poor visibility in spots.
For additional information on Ozalenka Trail, please contact the Ozalenka Alpine Club at 250 569-2596 or BC Parks/Mount Robson at 250-566-4325. Thank you for your cooperation and understanding.

advisories.title: River Hazards
advisories.description: Cowichan River is a natural watercourse with natural hazards that may pose significant risks to river users. Please use extreme caution around sweepers and strainers (partially and fully submerged trees). Tubing within the park is not recommended as tubers are especially at risk and fatalities have occurred.

advisories.title: Boil Water Notice
advisories.description: The Vancouver Island Health Authority recommends visitors to Cowichan River Park to boil water collected from the water pumps for at least one minute or otherwise disinfect before drinking, brushing teeth or using water for food preparation that will not be cooked.

advisories.title: A permit is required to access this ecological reserve
advisories.description: Permits are available for research and educational activities only.

advisories.title: Fees at the Shelter Bay site
advisories.description: Burton and Eagle Creek campgrounds are operated by local community groups. While the Park Act fees have been removed from the BC Parks fee schedule for these sites, user fees are still being collected by the operator. BC Parks camping fees are still being collected for the Shelter Bay site.

advisories.title: Flood risk in Vowell Creek Drainage
advisories.description:
In recent years, a proglacial lake adjacent to the Vowell Glacier has been forming during the summer months. This lake has the potential to rapidly fail, as it did in 2017, resulting in a glacial lake outburst flood.
A proglacial lake is formed when meltwater is trapped against a glacier or dammed by a moraine or ice. The outburst flood may be triggered by the failure of the dam, a buildup of water pressure, or an avalanche or rockslide into the lake.
Park visitors are advised to avoid extended travel or overnight camping in the Vowell Creek drainage between August 1 and September 30.

advisories.title: Spires area park access – stay on Brisco Road
advisories.description:
Visitors accessing the Spires area of Bugaboo Park should be aware of ongoing directional signage vandalism occurring on the lower portion of the Bugaboo Park access route from Brisco. Visitors utilizing this access route are cautioned to stay on Brisco Road, about 5 km from the highway turn-off.
Avoid travelling up the "Mine Road." This road is hazardous; it's steep, narrow, and directional guide signage may be missing in this area. The standard access turns up Westside Road, at about 8.5 km from the highway, and proceeds to the junction with the Bugaboo Forest Service Road.
Alternatively, visitors can use the access route from Spillimacheen, which connects with the Brisco access route at the Brisco Road / Westside Road junction.

advisories.title: Winter Helicopter Access to Bugaboo Park
advisories.description: Letters of permission (LOP) are required for winter helicopter access. For further information on visiting the park in winter and early spring, contact the Ministry of Environment and Parks office at 250 489-8540.

advisories.title: Construction noise
