advisories.title: Road and trail Information
advisories.description:
Walker Creek Forest Service Road (FSR) is in good condition up to 50km.
While travelling on the Walker Creek FSR, attention is required to navigate the surface as it is uneven, rutted, slippery and very rough. The road is not recommended for anything other than a 4x4, high clearance vehicle, and drivers familiar with this type of vehicle operation.
The trail between Bastille Creek and Buchanan Creek can result in quite a bit of hiking around sections where the old road surface has washed away, and some travel on muddy sections of the winter snowmobile route due to ATV/UTV traffic and wet conditions up to Buchanan Creek, where ATV/UTV traffic is not permitted within the boundaries of the park. Trail/route surface is a good hard surface from Buchanan Creek to Kakwa Lake.

advisories.title: Pet closures are in place on park beaches
advisories.description:
Seasonal beach closure for pets along the shores of Rathtrevor Beach in effect from February 15 to April 30
Permanent and seasonal beach closures exist for pets along the shores of Rathtrevor Beach Provincial Park to protect migratory birds. The sandy day-use beach along the east shore of the park is closed to pets year-round. Leashed pets are only permitted on the rocky north shore of the park from May 1 – Feb 14. Pets must be physically restrained and under control at all times within the park. Those found in contravention of this notice are liable for fines starting at $115.00.
Please reference the below map to better understand where and when you can take your pet within the park.

advisories.title: Western thatch ants
advisories.description: Rathtrevor Beach Provincial Park is home to Western thatch ants. During the spring and summer months these ants are very active so please respect these natural insects and avoid any unnecessary disruption of their homes, which are in the form of mounds. Please keep all food sealed and stored away when not in use, and use garbage and recycling bins to dispose of waste. These actions will help avoid any unwanted interaction with these tiny creatures.

advisories.title: Prevent raccoons from becoming food-conditioned
advisories.description:
ATTENTION: This park has an abundant raccoon population that thrives on park visitor’s food, garbage and other scented items.
Please follow these important guidelines to prevent raccoons from becoming food conditioned:
Do not feed raccoons. They may become aggressive and potentially dangerous once they are used to getting food from people.
Never leave food unattended. Properly secure food and scented items (sunscreen, toothpaste, etc.) when you are away from your campsite and at night.
Store food and scented items, inside vehicles, boats, or secured food containers provided (bungee cords around coolers and rubbermaid bins do not work!).
Never leave food inside your tent.
Dispose of garbage immediately in the garbage bins provided. Never leave scraps or waste unattended.
Ensure your vessel is secure to prevent raccoons from accessing food from inside vessel hatches.
Park Operators and Park Rangers patrol the area to facilitate public education and monitoring. Penalties may be issued under the Park Act for non-compliance.
Thanks for your cooperation.

advisories.title: Declared Title Area
advisories.description:
In 2014, the Supreme Court of Canada recognized TŜilhqot’in Nation’s Aboriginal title to 1,700 square kilometres of land in the Chilcotin region called the Declared Title Area, along with the right and responsibility to manage and determine how the land is used. The Province of British Columbia, TŜilhqot’in Nation, and Xeni Gwet’in First Nation are working to implement a shared vision of establishing the Declared Title Area as a unique, world-class example of government-to-government and nation-to-nation partnership grounded in Indigenous leadership, vision and self-determination. This includes working collaboratively to manage the impact of human activity on grizzly bears, fish, and other wildlife in the Upper Chilko Corridor.
The map to the right shows the land that is subject to the declaration of Aboriginal title, including Ts’il?os Park, Nuntsi Park, & Cardiff Ecological Reserve. Persons interested in visiting parks within the Declared Title Area for camping and associated recreational activities are encouraged to visit the Tsilhqot’in National Government webpage, to better understand the visitor protocols and procedures. Questions around park access can be directed to parkinfo@gov.bc.ca.

advisories.title: Aggressive harbour seal in the Canoe Islets area
advisories.description:
BC Parks has received a new report (July 23, 2023) of a harbour seal attacking a group of sea kayakers in the vicinity of Canoe Islets (just to the West of Cedar Island). Though harbour seal attacks do occur, this is not seen as typical behaviour, but does happen from time to time.
All visitors to Broughton Archipelago area should be mindful of this event. Larger group sizes may be advantageous. Department of Fisheries and Oceans (DFO) recommends you move away slowly at the first sign of disturbance or agitation. If the animal starts to stare, fidget or dive into the water, you’re too close. For emergencies involving marine animals, please contact DFO at 1 800 465-4336.

advisories.title: Increased grizzly bear activity in area
advisories.description:
BC Conservation Officer Service (COS) has received increased reports of grizzly bear activity and presence within Broughton Archipelago Provincial Park and Broughton Archipelago Provincial Conservancy. Areas of particular reporting have been around Swanson Island, Flower Island, Crease Island, and the Village Channel corridor. Report encounters to COS 1-877-952-RAPP (Cellular Dial: #7277 Telus Network).
Staying Safe in Bear Country

This is a true wilderness area and very little is known at preset about the potential hazards; use caution and be prepared if you’re planning a trip into this area.

The best access road is off of Highway 3 about 6km east of Bridesville. Follow Johnstone Creek Road for 25km to the park. It is a maintained gravel road and takes approximately 40 minutes from the highway turnoff. Other access points off of Highway 33 and from Okanagan Falls are not well marked and are unmaintained forestry roads that are not suitable for vehicle traffic.

advisories.title: Pets prohibited except in San Josef Bay area due to wolf activity - pets must be kept on leash in San Josef Bay
advisories.description:
BC Parks has received ongoing reports of high wolf activity in some areas of Cape Scott Park. Dogs are only permitted in San Josef Bay area and must be leashed at all times. Dogs are prohibited in all other areas of the park, including the North Coast Trail. Dogs are a high level attractant to wolves and other large carnivores. Protect your pet – keep them at home.
All visitors and hikers in Cape Scott must be extremely mindful about how they recreate in coastal wolf habitat to help prevent wolves from becoming habituated to humans and conditioned to attractants.
Avoid attracting wolves
Securely store your food and cooking equipment during the day and night in food caches provided at all designated camping locations.
Avoid camping or recreating in locations where a carcass (ie. sea lion or seal) has washed ashore.
Keep your distance
Never approach wolves and scare them away immediately if they approach you.
Keep children close to you at all times and leave your pets at home.
Do your part when recreating in wolf country and help keep wolves wild. Please click the links for specific information on how to avoid wolf encounters and to practice proper backcountry etiquette.
If you encounter an aggressive wild animal, report it by calling the Conservation Officer Service 24-hour hotline toll free at 1-877-952-7277 (RAPP) or #7277 on the Telus Mobility Network.

The wildfire guard on the west side of the lake is decommissioned to vehicles larger than ATV/UTV near north and south park boundaries. The road between the campground and Munro Lake FSR remains relatively unchanged and accessible to motorized vehicles with high clearance. All motorized vehicles must stay on the already established trails.

advisories.description:
The park and canoe circuit have now been reopened, with limited facilities. Tanikul South Campsite will remain closed due to the severity of the burn. Safety assessment and site rehabilitations were completed in 2018 and replacement of infrastructure are being planned.
Caution – be advised that there are significant risks associated with entering areas that have been burnt over by the 2017 wildfires. Potential risks could include:
danger trees and overhead hazards – the integrity of trees whose trunks, roots or branches have been damaged by wildfire is unreliable
terrain instability resulting in landslides and falling or shifting debris and rock
amplified runoff after rainfall or snowmelt which could result in a rapid increase of water course depth and flow rates or flooding conditions
ash pits – may be deep and difficult to see
respiratory effects caused by breathing soot and charcoal for extended periods of time
Post-wildfire hazards may last for several years or longer after a wildfire and may be triggered at any time with little or no warning.

Of note, the Chilliwack Natural Resource District indicates that the FSR is not vehicle accessible past the 21km mark. As a result, road access to Squakum campground is not currently available. Please visit the Ministry of Forests road conditions page for current information on forest service road conditions.

links.title: Chilliwack Natural Resource District road safety information

advisories.title: Reservations for Skyview RV Campground
advisories.description: Reservations for Skyview Campground can be made through the Manning Park Resort Skyview booking system.

advisories.title: Stolz Pool groupsite relocated
advisories.description: The Stolz Pool groupsite is an inland location with an open area inclusive RV and tent camping. Parking is in a gravel lot beside the 12 tent pads. Campers and RV’s can camp in the parking lot. There are 2 pit toilets and garbage and recycling facilities at the groupsite. The groupsite has an open-air shelter that can fit 4 picnic tables. The firepit is located beside the shelter.

advisories.title: Increased wolf activity
advisories.description:
There has been recent increase in wildlife activity in and around Vargas Island Park and Flores Island Park.
Park visitors are advised to:
Store food securely. Be extremely mindful about how food is stored, always use food caches where possible, and have equipment to hang food if food caches are full. Kayak hatches are not a suitable storage for food as wolves have learned how to get into them. Unlawfully storing food and/or garbage may result in an eviction or violation ticket under section 33.1 of the Wildlife Act.
Do not sleep outside your tent. There is a high frequency of wildlife coming into campsites during the night.
Do not bring pets to Vargas or Flores Islands. Dogs are a high level attractant to wolves and other large carnivores. Protect your pet – keep them at home.
Do not try to get close to wildlife, specifically large carnivores. Do your part to help keep wildlife wild.
If you encounter an aggressive wild animal, report it to the Conservation Officer Service 24-hour hotline toll free at 1-877-952-7277 (RAPP) or #7277 on the Telus Mobility Network.
Learn more about wildlife safety

advisories.title: Road closure
advisories.description: The road into the Clayoquot Arm Recreation Site has been blocked and will remain closed until further notice. There is no longer any vehicle access to the site or Clayoquot Arm bridge; park users wanting to use the boat launch will need to walk 400m down to the lake.

advisories.title: Rough conditions on Barker Access Road
advisories.description: Please be advised that park access via Barker Road for the northern portion of Stamp River Provincial Park is a very rough road. BC Parks strongly suggests that visitors to the park only use high clearance vehicles and drive slowly if they choose to use this access road.

advisories.title: Access to nʕaylintn (McIntyre Bluff) via Covert Farms is permanently closed
advisories.description: Thank you for respecting private lands.

advisories.title: Safety Bulletins
advisories.description:
Do not attempt to cross the highway
There is no pedestrian access between the east and west sides of Goldstream Provincial Park, bisected by the Trans-Canada Highway.
Railway lines/trestles/tunnels are private property
All railway lines and associated structures (trestles and tunnels) are located outside the boundaries of Goldstream Provincial Park. Accessing these are considered trespassing on private property and pose a significant public safety risk.
Mount Finlayson Trail caution
This trail is steep and rugged; dress for the terrain and weather; stay on the marked trail; allow adequate time for return in daylight. The summit can be accessed from Finlayson Arm Road or the day-use area. Use caution when walking on Finlayson Arm Road.

advisories.title: Snowmobile use at Call Lake Park
advisories.description:
Restrictions on snowmobile use in Call Lake Park are in place to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone recreating in the park. Snowmobiling within the park is only allowed under a letter of authorization (LOA) from BC Parks and only for the purpose of accessing ice fishing locations on Call Lake. Individuals wishing to use a snowmobile within the park must complete, sign and carry the LOA for snowmobile access [PDF] with them before entering the park, and must follow all regulations stipulated in the letter while in the park.
These restrictions were put in place to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone recreating in the Park.

advisories.title: Hazards along the Kettle River
advisories.description: Hazards exist along the Kettle River, including Cascade Falls, located approximately 5 kilometres downstream of Gilpin Grasslands Park. Park users intending on river travel are advised to become familiar with river conditions, safe river exit locations, and to plan accordingly.

advisories.title: Wildlife warning
advisories.description: Bears are common in this park.

advisories.title: Park access
advisories.description:
Please be advised that access to Artlish Caves Provincial Park is very difficult as a result of road deactivation activities outside of park boundaries.
Approaching from the west, by way of Atluck Lake, a bridge has been removed on East Artlish Main approximately 50m from the Artlish Main logging Road and visitors must now walk several kilometres on overgrown former logging roads to the park boundary and caves beyond.
Trails receive limited maintenance and are difficult to access; please exercise caution. Deactivated logging roads into the park, approached from the east from the Zebellos Mainline, are also overgrown and difficult to follow.

advisories.title: Drinking water currently unavailable
advisories.description: There is no potable water at any of the campsites within the park. Visitors must be prepared and bring their own drinking water with them to the park, or boil/filter water from nearby creeks and streams.

advisories.title: Caution: Celesta Creek trail at ALBAS campsite contains steep, rough sections with sharp drop-offs
advisories.description: Children should be closely supervised and pets kept on a leash. Serious injury and deaths have occurred in this area due to adjacent waterfalls, changing water levels, fast currents and cold water.

advisories.title: Boating safety
advisories.description: For boating safety tips, information and requirements for pleasure craft, please refer to the Transport Canada Safe Boating Guide.

advisories.title: Portions of Epper Passage Park are designated as a Rock Fish Conservation Area
advisories.description:
Some special fishing restrictions apply. Please click on the links below to view restrictions and a map of area.
Permitted fishing activities in a Rock Fish Conservation Area
Map: Epper Passage Rock Fish Conservation Area

advisories.title: This is a very remote area; any visitors must be self-sufficient and fully prepared
advisories.description: It is recommended that visitors carry a satellite phone or handheld VHF radio in case of emergencies.

advisories.title: Park in designated spots - illegally parked vehicles will be towed
advisories.description: Vehicles parked illegally at Murrin Provincial Park will be subject to towing at the owner's expense. Visitors must park in designated parking lots and observe the "no parking" signs posted. Vehicles parked illegally in closed day-use areas will be charged a fee for gate unlocking. Thank you for your cooperation.

advisories.title: Running water unavailable at Shelter Bay Site
advisories.description: Due to a waterline break, the Shelter Bay Site is currently without running water. Updates will be posted when available.

advisories.title: Driving conditions
advisories.description: Rough driving conditions are present on the steep public road (Mount Maxwell Road) that leads to Mount Maxwell Provincial Park. Drivers should be experienced and prepared for surface erosion issues such as deep potholes, steep ruts and exposed bedrock on sections of the road outside of the park. Only 4X4 vehicles with high clearance are recommended.

advisories.title: Help keep Nicola Lake healthy
advisories.description: We all need to do our part to keep Nicola Lake as healthy as possible. Please keep yourself updated with information on Nicola Lake at http://www.fraserbasin.bc.ca/tr_nicola_lake.html.

links.title: Learn more about Nicola watershed planning

advisories.title: Reminders to park visitors
advisories.description:
No open alcohol on docks or in day-use areas.
No smoking/vaping on docks or in day-use areas.
Pets must be kept on leash at all times.
Quiet time is from 11pm to 7am.
Absolutely no swimming/diving off or around the docks.
Maximum stay is 14 days.
No removal of park resources.
All persons, when requested by a park ranger, must produce identification. Failure to identify oneself to a park ranger is a ticketable offense.
Docks are to remain clear for pedestrians.
We are trying to protect the sensitive ecological values of the sea bed from dragging anchors. For this reason, the use of anchors in Mark Bay is not permitted in order to allow for the recovery of sub tidal and inter-tidal marine life in the bay, and to better prevent boats from washing ashore. Please use the mooring buoys available and make sure your boat is safely secured to them.

advisories.title: Protected area renamed to Hisnit River Watershed Protected Area
advisories.description:
To recognize Indigenous history and culture, the Power River Watershed Protected Area has been renamed the Hisnit River Watershed Protected Area. The protected area is significant to the Ka:’yu:k’t’h’/Che:k’tles7et’h’ (Kie-you-cut and Chek-le-seth) First Nations since the Power River Estuary is the location of a former village site called Hisnit.
News Release

advisories.title: Annual mowing of the former agricultural fields occurs in the late spring/early summer
advisories.description: Please note that the annual mowing of the former agricultural fields occurs in the late spring to early summer. Temporary noise disruptions, as well as access and parking restrictions, can be expected.

advisories.title: The campground gate is locked daily between 11 pm and 7 am
advisories.description: After-hours arrivals and early departures are not permitted within the park after the gate is closed. Please ensure your schedule is compatible with these gate closure times.

advisories.title: Illegally parked vehicles will be towed
advisories.description:
Visitors must park in designated parking lots and observe the “no parking” signs posted.
Provincial parks in the Fraser Valley have experienced exceptional growth in visitor numbers, leading to parking congestion and illegally parked vehicles. Public safety is paramount for BC Parks, and these new parking policies are in place to ensure safe access for all.

advisories.title: Be aware of thieves
advisories.description: Lock up securely. Do not leave valuables in campsites. Report any theft or damage to police, 911 non-emergency.

advisories.title: Glass Sponge Reef protection
advisories.description:
No commercial, recreational or Indigenous bottom-contact fishing activities are allowed in the area of Halkett Point, within Halkett Bay Marine Provincial Park. This includes fishing for:
prawn
shrimp
crab
groundfish (including halibut)
The use of downrigger gear in recreational salmon trolling is also prohibited in these areas due to the potential risk of damage to shallow reefs.
Further information, including maps of the closure area

advisories.title: Maximum stay is 14 nights per year - fines issued for staying longer
advisories.description: Park visitors using the campground, mooring buoy, or dock are limited to 14 nights per calendar year (BC Park Conservancy and Recreation Area Regulation (180/90)(Section 39.1 and 39.2)). Exceeding this limit may result in eviction from the park and potential fines.

advisories.title: Current hiking trail conditions report
advisories.description: Check Activities Available at this Park / Hiking for current trail conditions.

advisories.title: Conover Cove access
advisories.description: Conover Cove is a popular boating destination and very busy throughout the summer. The dock is available on a First Come/First Serve basis and a size restriction for vessels is in place year-round. Vessels greater than 11m in length are not permitted on the dock and are encouraged to anchor in Princess Cove.

advisories.title: Goldpan Campground closed until further notice, day-use area open to walk-in only
advisories.description:
The campground at Goldpan Park will remain closed due to ongoing slope instability caused by recent wildfire impacts. Geo-technical assessments provided by the Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure, combined with frequent slide activity, confirm a heightened risk to public safety for anyone staying overnight within the campground.
While camping remains closed, the park is open for day use, walk-in only. Visitors are welcome to enjoy the day-use areas but are reminded to remain vigilant and respect all posted signage.

advisories.title: Chilko-Newton Road and Gwe Da Ts‘ih Campground closed September 1 to October 31
advisories.description:
To mitigate the risks of members of the public coming into close contact with grizzly bears in the area, the following areas of Tsilos Park will be closed from September 1 to October 31 annually.
Gwe Da Ts‘ih Campground
Chilko-Newton Road, south of Henry’s Crossing
The Tŝilhqot’in Nation and the Province are jointly restricting public access to the upper Chilko corridor while a management plan is being written for the area. The closure of Chilko-Newton Road will be monitored and enforced under the BC Wildlife Act. Penalties and fines for violators will be issued.
Learn More:
For updates, visit DriveBC and BC Gov News - Chilko-Newton Road closure
Call FrontCounter BC 250 398-4574 for more information

advisories.title: Attention fisherman - New fishing regulation
advisories.description: No Fishing from Sept 1-Oct 31 between fishing boundary signs in the vicinity of the public salmon viewing platforms in Tsu’tswecw Provincial Park.

advisories.title: Road Closure of the Bonanza River Bridge - Rennell Sound
advisories.description:
Effective August 26, 2022, the Bonanza River Bridge located at the beginning of the Hangover Forest Service Road will be closed for safety issues. This closure prevents vehicular access to Bonanza Beach, Bill Brown FSR and the Hangover Forest Service Road. At this time, there is no estimated time of repair.
Bonanza Bridge Closure [PDF, 744KB]
Road users a can watch for updates by visiting the Haida Gwaii Natural Resource District Road Safety Information web page.

advisories.title: Bring your own toilet paper
advisories.description:
As of July 1, 2021, BC Parks will no longer supply toilet paper to the Joffre Lakes backcountry outhouse facilities at Middle Joffre Lake and Upper Joffre Lake Toilet paper will continue to be provided for the main parking lot and overflow parking lot outhouse facilities.
Information is included in the Garibaldi backcountry education module.
For more backcountry ethics, check out AdventureSmart.ca and our Backcountry Visitor Guide.

advisories.title: Unauthorized off-road vehicle use on trails prohibited
advisories.description: Unauthorized off-road vehicle (ORV) use on trails in this park is strictly prohibited. Driving on park trails disrupts and damages natural areas and poses a safety risk to other park visitors. Operators of unauthorized motorized vehicles found off-road in the park could face fines under the Park, Conservancy and Recreation Areas Regulations.

advisories.title: Firewood collection
advisories.description: Firewood is not provided for campers or cabin users from October to May. Collecting firewood within and around campgrounds and trails is prohibited. Collect firewood from fallen dead trees only. Standing trees, dead or alive, are not to be cut.

advisories.title: 2026 Camping Reservations
advisories.description: Some campsites at this park will be available to reserve for the 2026 camping season. Check back here or at camping.bcparks.ca in early 2026 for more booking details including reservable dates and available campsites.

advisories.title: Winter Closure Area for protection of wolverine in Goat Range Park
advisories.description:
BC Parks has been working with local wolverine researchers over the last several years supporting research in various West Kootenay Provincial Parks. As a result, two maternal wolverine denning areas have been confirmed in Goat Range Park. Wolverine (Gulo gulo) is a species of provincial and national conservation concern and are exceptionally vulnerable to human disturbance. As such, BC Parks has implemented two closure areas in Goat Range Park to help ensure the protection of this important species. These closures are put in place by a “Directors Order”.
The winter closure is in effect from January 11 to May 17. The closure will be supported by compliance and enforcement action from BC Parks ranger staff. A copy of the order and KMZ files showing the closure can be found here:
Order of the Regional Director [PDF]
Upper Poplar Creek - Area 1 [KMZ]
Upper Poplar Creek - Area 2 [KMZ]
Closure Map [PDF]
Seen a wolverine or found tracks in the backcountry? Help support wolverine conservation by sharing your observation with Wolverine Watch. Every report contributes valuable information for monitoring and protecting wolverine populations.
We appreciate everyone's support in respecting the closure of these areas. The assessment of these closures is an ongoing process.

advisories.title: Lands proposed for Te’mexw treaties
advisories.description:
Negotiations between Canada, B.C. and the Te’mexw Treaty Association (TTA) are coming to a close. If concluded, treaties will be implemented on Southern Vancouver Island for Beecher Bay (SC’IA/NEW), Malahat, Songhees, Snaw-Naw-As (Nanoose) and T’Sou-ke Nations.
Sooke Mountain Provincial Park is being considered to become public Treaty Lands as part of the T’Sou-ke Treaty, subject to successful conclusion of the treaty negotiations, and ratification by all parties.
TTA and B.C. have a shared interest in maintaining public access and continued recreational opportunities to the park, while protecting the ecological and conservation values. These interests will be detailed in the treaties’ terms and conditions.
Find out more and sign up for updates: engage.gov.bc.ca/temexw-treaty-negotiations

advisories.title: Lands proposed for Te’mexw treaties
advisories.description:
Negotiations between Canada, B.C. and the Te’mexw Treaty Association (TTA) are coming to a close. If concluded, treaties will be implemented on Southern Vancouver Island for Beecher Bay (SC’IA/NEW), Malahat, Songhees, Snaw-Naw-As (Nanoose) and T’Sou-ke Nations.
Discovery Island Marine Provincial Park is being considered to become public Treaty Lands as part of the Songhees Treaty, subject to successful conclusion of the treaty negotiations, and ratification by all parties.
TTA and B.C. have a shared interest in maintaining public access and continued recreational opportunities to the park, while protecting the ecological and conservation values. These interests will be detailed in the treaties’ terms and conditions.
Find out more and sign up for updates: engage.gov.bc.ca/temexw-treaty-negotiations

advisories.title: Kakwa Park offers a Backcountry Host volunteer opportunity
advisories.description: Applications for the 2026 season are now closed.

advisories.title: Halkett Bay dock closure
advisories.description: The BC Parks dock in Halkett Bay has sustained significant damage. For public safety, portions of the dock have been removed. Please refrain from using the dock and please respect the closure signs and measures currently in place. The campsite and its facilities remain open to the public. Another dock is available for use nearby at Plumper Cove Marine Park. Thank you for your patience and understanding as BC Parks works to make the necessary improvements in the park.

advisories.title: Visitors to this protected area are expected to follow these guidelines:
advisories.description:
Respect Site Integrity
Leave no physical trace of your visit. Leave sites as you found them.
Do not tag locations on social media. Allow others to discover these sites.
Leave Sites Intact
Do not dig holes, or move or damage rocks, plants, trees, or driftwood on the land, beach or intertidal zone.
Stay in designated campsites and on established trails to protect sensitive ecosystems.
Best practice is to not have campfires. Fires below high tide line only. Do not forage for firewood. Leave no evidence of fires.
Adhere to fire bans.
Respect the Cultural History of the First Nation whose Territory You are Visiting
Do not touch or otherwise disturb any First Nation cultural material. Treat land and cultural sites with respect. Disturb nothing, take nothing.
Respect any First Nation protocols identified in signage.
Consult websites before trips.
First Nation stories are the property of the Nation – do not share that history without permission.
Respect Provincial and Federal Government Regulations and Legislation.
The law protects archaeological and cultural sites. Do not disturb them.

advisories.title: Cellular service unavailable
advisories.description: There is no cell service at this park, please plan accordingly. The park operators can take both cash and cards for payment.

advisories.title: Safety information regarding fluctuating water levels
advisories.description: Please be vigilant when near Kleanza Creek due to fluctuating water levels and respect any posted trail closures or advisories.

advisories.title: The Kettle Valley Rail (KVR) trail at the site of the May 2023 landslide (approximately 2 km west of the Little White Forest Service Road (FSR) junction) is now OPEN to most traffic, with the exception of side by side and road vehicles
advisories.description:
This section of trail is now open for bike, foot, quad and dirt bike traffic only. The site will remain closed to road vehicles and side-by-side traffic until further notice. Throughout the season, the site may be subject to wet weather shutdown guidelines and may be closed during periods of inclement weather or if signs of instability are observed.
The 18 KVR historic trestles through Myra Canyon are accessible from both Ruth Station (Little White FSR) and Myra Station (Myra FSR). The Bellevue Trestle can be accessed from the west, off Gilliard Forest Service Rd.
For more information, please visit the Recreation Sites and Trails BC website.

advisories.title: Road closures in effect on approach to Loveland Bay Park — July 2023 to July 2029
advisories.description:
Visitors to Loveland Bay Park are advised that access to the park is subject to road closures at the Brewster Lake Road where it crosses the John Hart Dam.
Please check majorprojects.ca for up-to-date information on closures.
Alternative vehicle access to Loveland Bay Provincial Park can be made from Duncan Bay Road via Highway 19 north of Campbell River. Follow the blue and white directional signs along Gordon Road, from Duncan Bay Road, to reconnect with the Brewster Lake / Loveland Bay Forest Service Road (FSR).
See map below with the detour route shown as bold green near the north side of the dam going to Loveland Bay.

advisories.title: Wildfire damage, lake access affected
advisories.description: Access to Willowgrouse and Tuwut Lakes will remain closed due to wildfire related hazards. BC Parks is working on a plan for reopening this area.

advisories.title: Fishing is restricted in the Rockfish Conservation Area
advisories.description: This ecological reserve is within a federal Rockfish Conservation Area. Some fishing activities are restricted. Check the Fisheries and Oceans Canada website for details.

links.title: Fishing restrictions in Rockfish Conservation Areas

advisories.title: Ongoing research at Kikomun Creek Park
advisories.description:
Researchers have installed 8 research sites throughout Kikomun Creek Park supporting a project to monitor the impact and interactions of prescribed burning and herbicide application on invasive species in the park. These research sites will be in place for several years and will include minimal research infrastructure (metal pegs and pins) that may be visible to park visitors. The intent of the project is to determine the best possible management of invasive species while supporting ecosystem restoration actions. There will be signage indicating the location of the research sites. Please DO NOT DISTURB these sites.
For more information please contact the BC Parks Conservation Specialist at (250) 420-6285.

advisories.title: No road access
advisories.description: The vehicle access road has been closed and gated since 2015 due to rock fall hazards and bridge failure.

advisories.title: Road access changes as of June 9, 2023
advisories.description: Resource Road access to Pennask Lake has changed as of June 9, 2023. Please see maps below for more details.

links.title: New Pennask Lake Park access - detailed map
New Pennask Lake Park access - simple view

advisories.title: Communication alert for the Bowron Canoe Circuit
advisories.description:
Visitors are highly encouraged to bring a personal emergency communication device (such as a satellite phone, inReach, Spot), while traveling on the canoe circuit.
While the circuit is equipped with emergency radios, coverage can be inconsistent, and there is no cellular reception or WiFi anywhere in the park.

advisories.title: Parking lot temporary closure
advisories.description: The small parking lot in the east end of park, just off the Hat Creek Road, is temporarily closed.

advisories.title: Use caution and stay on the existing trail
advisories.description:
Thorsen Creek flows through a canyon feature which contains steep embankments and cliff edges. People wishing to access the petroglyph site should be aware of these features as they may be dangerous, unstable, and some are overhanging.
Please ensure you stay on the existing trail and do not wonder over to the edges to gain a better view of the river. The boardwalk and stairs accessing the petroglyph site may be slippery when wet. Please take extra caution when travelling along the boardwalk and stairs especially during rain events.

advisories.title: Otter Lake Campground, trailered boat launch is closed
advisories.description: The Otter Lake Campground trailered boat launch is closed until further notice.

advisories.title: Hand pump is closed for repairs
advisories.description: The drinking water hand pump at Inkaneep Campground has been closed for repairs and will be not available for the remainder of the camping season.

advisories.title: Grassy Glades outhouse closed
advisories.description: The Grassy Glades outhouse is closed until further notice.

advisories.title: Park-use permit required for any commercial operations
advisories.description:
A park-use permit is required for any commercial operations within provincial parks and protected areas in the province of British Columbia, including operations such as bus tours and guiding. Operating without a park-use permit is a violation of the Park Act and could result in fines and/or further administrative enforcement. Any reference to commercial operations occurring within provincial parks and protected areas must also be removed from websites, advertisements, and social media sites until a valid park-use permit has been issued.
For futher information on obtaining a Commercial Recreation – Park Use Permit, please visit the portal below.

links.title: Commercial Recreation – Park Use Permit Portal

advisories.title: No camping permitted, remainder of conservancy day-use only, section of conservancy completely closed
advisories.description:
The Burdwood Group Conservancy will be closed to overnight camping effective 8:00 am, September 5, 2023 to December 31, 2026. The island identified in red on the attached map is closed to all public use from 8:00 am, September 5, 2023 to December 31, 2026.
This closure is intended to provide BC Parks and Kwikwasut'inuxw Haxwa'mis First Nation an opportunity to develop a plan to manage recreation to better protect ecological and cultural values in the Conservancy. Any changes to the closure will be posted on the BC Parks website.

advisories.title: Kokanee Creek Spawning Channel Area restrictions
advisories.description:
Kokanee Creek Spawning Channel restrictions are in place from August 15 to September 30, to improve public safety and provide viewing opportunities of Kokanee spawning in the channel. Thank you for observing all signs.
Kokanee Creek Spawning Channel Area restrictions include:
Dogs will not be permitted on the channel boardwalk or trails adjacent to the spawning channel.
Bicycles must be walked across the boardwalk and along the trails adjacent to the spawning channel.
The portion of the spawning channel downstream of the viewing platform will be closed to the public during the period when bears are utilizing it for feeding. This closure will include the trails behind the Nature Centre.

advisories.title: Seasonal low water levels affecting boat launch use
advisories.description: Seasonal low water levels may have an impact on the ability to launch or retrieve boats. Please plan your use accordingly.

advisories.title: Canyon Trail access restricted
advisories.description: The Canyon Trail network west of the Westside Road is closed until further notice.

advisories.title: Follow 'no anchoring' buoys and signs to protect eelgrass beds
advisories.description:
Desolation Sound Marine Park is home to eelgrass habitats that play a crucial role in supporting marine biodiversity. To further our understanding of biodiversity recovery in the region, we are monitoring eelgrass beds with valuable support from the Tla'amin, Klahoose, and Hamalco Nations, and the University of British Columbia.
To study these vital habitats, small area closures are in place, marked by ‘no anchoring’ buoys. Around Williams Island, boaters must not anchor in the areas delineated by the ‘no anchoring’ buoys. At Copplestone Island, anchoring is not permitted between the buoys.
Our study also includes annual eelgrass monitoring to assess the potential recovery of the eelgrass beds, and evaluate the effectiveness of the closures.

advisories.title: Multiple trail bridges damaged by flood events
advisories.description:
Multiple trail bridges within the park have been damaged by flood events in recent years. This concerns the bridge over Spahats Creek on the Clearwater River Trail. This creek is impassable.
The bridges over Hemp Creek and Trout Creek on the Flatiron trail were also washed out. The creeks are impassable at high water levels.
Lastly, the bridges over the Second Canyon creek and Third Canyon creek were also washed out. The trail from Third Canyon to First Canyon is closed until further noticed due to the bridges that are not present anymore.

advisories.title: Access restricted
advisories.description: Tatuk East Campground remains closed until further notice. Access to Tatuk East is restricted while the bridge into the park is being replaced. Tatuk West remains open at this time.

advisories.title: Grizzly bears frequent area - exercise caution
advisories.description:
Grizzly bears are known to regularly travel through this area and may be present at any time, including sows with cubs.
**Please travel in groups, have bear spray, and make noise**

advisories.title: Smith River Falls viewpoint is not accessible by vehicle in winter months
The building located by the bay and its surrounding area are closed to the public
advisories.description:
This is an active construction zone.
This area is licensed for the exclusive use by the Cowichan Tribes and sublicensee Stqeeye' Learning Society. This area is designated for the purpose of supporting Cowichan Tribes and other Quw'utsun Nation member communities in cultural and traditional teachings and for land-based cultural and educational programs.
The public kayak launch near this area is not closed to the public. Please access the launch safely and only park vehicles in the designated upper parking areas.

advisories.title: Winter conditions - use caution
advisories.description: Winter conditions exist at Nlhaxten/Cerise Creek Conservancy. Park visitors will encounter deep snow, ice and slippery conditions. Micro spikes, snowshoes or backcountry skiing equipment are strongly recommended. Use at your own risk. Those visiting Nlhaxten/Cerise Creek during the fall, winter and spring months will be exposed to avalanche terrain. Visitors should bring and know how to use an avalanche transceiver, probe, and shovel. It is recommended that visitors consider taking a formal avalanche training course prior to visiting the Park during winter months.

advisories.title: Wolves active in beach and campground area, off-leash dogs are prohibited
advisories.description:
Wolves are active in the beach and campground area of Raft Cove Park, exercise caution. Visitors must secure and control all wildlife attractants such as food, food waste, and domestic animals.
Please consider leaving domestic animals at home. If you choose to bring a domestic animal to the park, you must keep it on a leash less than two meters in length or within a container for the duration of its time in the park.
The Park, Conservancy and Recreation Area Regulation prohibits off-leash dogs within provincial parks (B.C. Reg. 180/90, 10[1]).

advisories.title: Hotsprings tub and facilities closed due to landslide
advisories.description: The Hotsprings tub and facilities are closed due to a landslide which affected the upper water piping.

advisories.title: Peregrine Falcon monitoring and reporting
advisories.description:
Peregrine Falcon monitoring program in Stawamus Chief Park, to help protect nesting areas from recreational rock climbing routes, is in effect. Monitoring takes place from March until July, but the most important months for monitoring is between March and April.
The Peregrine Falcon's anatum subspecies is currently in a recovery stage with a low population size. Habitat loss due to urban and agricultural development, as well as contamination from organochlorines, has significantly impacted its range, which has contracted from historical levels. The population remains small, with ongoing threats from human disturbance and environmental contaminants, but there is a slow recovery underway in certain regions, particularly with recent reintroductions in southern British Columbia.
Help BC Parks track presence and survivorship, and evaluate nest productivity and success by reporting.
Please report falcon sightings to BC Parks ParkInfo@gov.bc.ca.

advisories.title: Old Cronin Creek and Higgins Creek Trails no longer maintained
advisories.description: Due to slope stability issues, multiple maintenance challenges, and the availability of new access opportunities, BC Parks has chosen to no longer maintain the original Cronin Creek Trail and the lower Higgins Creek Trail. Higgins Basin is still accessible to hikers via the Little Joe Creek and Eagle Pass Trails. Anyone wishing to use the original Cronin Creek Trail or the lower end of the Higgins Creek Trail will find their condition quite poor with un-bridged stream crossings, thick brush, and significant amounts of standing and running water on the trail surfaces.

advisories.title: Camping reminders and regulations
advisories.description:
Attention Campers! BC Parks is reminding vehicle and tent campers at Stawamus Chief Park to adhere to BC Parks camping regulations:
Each tent site and drive-in site are available on a first come, first served, basis.
Campers are required to submit their payment at the self-registration info kiosk and display their registration tags at their campsite for their entire stay.
Maximum length of stay is limited to 14 days. This is to ensure that all visitors to the park have equal and fair access to the campground.
Park operators will be checking camping registration daily.
Designated bear caches will be inspected and cleaned regularly by park operator staff.
Please do not store food items in caches beyond the 14-day stay limit.
To ensure there is room in the bear caches, place all belongings in a self-contained bag. To assist the park operator staff, please label your bag with your campsite number.
Thank you for helping keep the Stawamus Chief campground clean, safe, and accessible for all park visitors.

advisories.title: Watercraft and fishing equipment banned to combat transmission of invasive species
advisories.description:
To help combat and mitigate the transmission of aquatic invasive species, effective immediately, the following fishing equipment and watercraft is banned in lakes, rivers, and creeks in Mount Assiniboine Park:
Watercraft
Belly boats
Stand up paddleboards
Dinghies
Boats
Fishing Equipment
Wading bibs/pants - all types (neoprene, breathable, rubber)
Wading boots - all types (felt sole, rubber sole)
Park visitors failing to comply with these measures are subject to violations and fines under the Park Act.
Park visitors are reminded to clean, drain, and dry all immersible water equipment prior to entering the park.
To learn more about aquatic invasive species and provincial measures being taken to mitigate transmission, read Aquatic invasive species (gov.bc.ca).

advisories.title: Clean all equipment to help prevent the spread of aquatic invasive species
advisories.description:
BC Parks is seeking your help to prevent the introduction of aquatic invasive species into this park.
Please adhere to the following measures.
Clean plants, animals, mud from any watercraft and equipment before storing it or moving it into this park.
Drain all water from any watercraft and equipment before storing it or moving it into this park.
Dry all parts of your watercraft and equipment completely before storing it or moving it into this park.
Recreational fishing gear should always be cleaned before and after entering this park. This includes waders, boots, fishing rods and lines, and other angling equipment.
Never move species, organisms, or water from one body of water to another. This includes all fish species and fish parts.
Bathe pets before allowing them to enter water bodies in this park.
Learn about aquatic invasive species and how to identify them.
Thank you for your help in protecting native plant and animal life in this park.

advisories.title: Possible road closures due to slide potential
advisories.description:
All individuals planning to visit Adams Lake (Bush Creek) should be aware of the possibility of flood or slide events that may affect the Adams Lake forest access road to the park. Post wildfire slide events are a distinct possibility and may follow a significant rain event in the area.
Visitors should be prepared to spend an extra day or two in the park should this happen, as it may take some time for road maintenance crews to clear an access route.

advisories.title: Cash only - no cell service or wifi available
advisories.description:
There is no cell phone service or wifi available along Highway 37 from Kitwanga to the Yukon border.
Be prepared for remote conditions and plan ahead for potential delays or emergencies.
Carry multiple forms of payment as many businesses in the area accept cash only.

advisories.title: Bring your own water or boil water before use
advisories.description:
Interior Health has issued a boil water notice for Skihist Provincial Park. Boiling is the most effective way to disinfect water and protect yourself from parasites like Giardia or Cryptosporidium. Boil water for at least two minutes and store it in clean, covered, food-grade containers.
We are working to resolve this issue and hope that we can provide safe drinking water in the near future. Thank you for your patience

advisories.title: Clean all boats and equipment to prevent the spread of aquatic invasive species
advisories.description:
Thank you for your helping prevent invasive species from spreading into this park.
Before you arrive:
Make sure your boat and all your equipment and clothing are completely clean and completely dry
This includes waders, boots, fishing rods and lines
Before storage or moving to another body of water:
Drain all water from your boat, and remove all plants, animals, and mud
Clean and dry your boat and all equipment and clothing
Wash your pets if they have been swimming
Report sightings of invasive species
Never move plants, animals, mud, or water between water bodies. This includes all fish and fish parts.
Learn more about invasive aquatic species and how to spot them

advisories.title: Boat launch at day-use area temporarily closed
advisories.description: Due to very low water levels, the boat launch at Allison Lake day-use area is temporarily closed. The boat launch will remain closed until the lake level returns to normal.

advisories.title: Beach areas affected by hazard trees
advisories.description:
Some beach areas and public lawn areas within Bear Creek campground are closed due to hazard trees. Thank you for obeying closure signs and staying out of these areas.
The closed-off area is indicated in red on the map below.

advisories.title: Park-use permit required for any commercial operations
advisories.description: A park-use permit is required for any commercial operations within provincial parks and protected areas in the province of British Columbia, including operations such as bus tours and guiding. Operating without a park-use permit is a violation of the Park Act and could result in fines and/or further administrative enforcement. Any reference to commercial operations occurring within provincial parks and protected areas must also be removed from websites, advertisements, and social media sites until a valid park-use permit has been issued.

advisories.title: It is illegal to transport watercraft with the drain plug still in place
advisories.description:
Before transporting a boat or other watercraft, owners/operators must remove the drain plug and drain all water on dry land including all internal compartments such as ballasts, bilges, and live wells.
Why is this important? Whirling disease has been detected in Yoho National Park in B.C. and containment and prevention is critical.
Read more information on the gov.bc.ca whirling disease webpage.

advisories.title: Notice of marine usage monitoring
advisories.description: To track marine usage trends, please be aware that automatic still-image cameras have been installed in Halkett Bay Marine Park. These cameras are installed and programmed in such a way to count the number of vessels in the park at a given time without collecting personal information from park users. All information is collected under the authority of s.26(c) and (e) of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act. If you have any questions about this program, please email parkinfo@gov.bc.ca.

advisories.title: Potential blue-green algae blooms on Nicola Lake
advisories.description:
A number of algae blooms have been reported on Nicola Lake. Use caution and avoid direct contact with the bloom if you see one. Water activities like swimming are discouraged near blooms. If you make contact, rinse your body with clean water.
Keep pets out of the water, and don’t allow pets to drink the water if algae blooms are suspected. If you, or your pet, have become unwell after contact with water that you think may be contaminated with cyanobacteria (blue-green algae), we strongly recommend that you seek immediate medical or veterinary advice.
Additional information is available at Algae Watch - Province of British Columbia or Recreational water and health: Cyanobacteria and their toxins - Canada.ca.
BC Parks and Interior Health will continue to monitor the situation and update information as required.

advisories.title: Portable campfire apparatus restriction
advisories.description:
During campfire prohibitions, the use of portable campfire apparatuses within Ruckle Park campground is prohibited, due to the flammable nature of the dry, coastal bluff ecosystem.
Designated communal fire rings
RV campsites 1 to 8
Please note: only a CSA-approved or ULC-approved portable campfire apparatus may be used in these areas and the flame length must not exceed 15 centimeters.

advisories.title: Management planning for Klinse-za / Twin Sisters Park
advisories.description: In 2026, a park management planning process for Klinse-za / Twin Sisters Park will begin. Management planning is a public process. Interested parties and the public will have the opportunity to provide input about how they want the park to be managed into the future. To learn more about park management planning and how it works, visit the management plans page.

advisories.title: New Cronin Creek Trail open
advisories.description: BC Parks is excited to announce a new Cronin Creek Trail experience for summer 2024. Trail information, driving directions, user safety, and more can be found in the hiking section. Pay special attention to information about Forest Service Road Safety, as trail users must access the new Cronin Trail by driving 12 kilometers on an active Forest Service Road.

advisories.title: Park is partially closed due to post 2024 wildfire hazards: Clint Creek drainage, Hamill Creek drainage, and the western portion of the Earl Grey Pass Trail impacted
advisories.description:
The trail and surrounding area are expected to reopen in 2028.
In the interest of public safety, BC Parks has partially closed this park until further notice.
Get up-to-date information from other official sources, such as the BC Wildfire Service (BCWS), the local regional district, and Drive BC.
You can still visit other BC Parks that remain unaffected by wildfire. Find other places to visit on the find a park page.

advisories.title: Rock slide hazard
advisories.description: A recent rock slide at Kleanza Creek Canyon has occurred within the park canyon. Stay clear of the canyon and pools until BC Parks has determined the area to be safe. Updates will be posted on the park page as they become available.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory in effect
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: Change to park hours
advisories.description: Effective August 1 to November 30 of each year, the portion of Babine River Corridor Park from the Southern Park boundary to the outflow of the Nilkitkwa River will only be open from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, except for those engaged in rafting or floating activities. Due to public safety and conservation concerns, access outside the posted hours is prohibited unless authorized by a Park Officer. The park area downstream of the Nilkitkwa River outflow remains open. Hours have been limited to help ensure public safety by having BC Parks staff on site and available to monitor wildlife activity during those hours. Given the history of dangerous human-bear interactions on site, further restrictions related to access may occur. Please review the FAQ document for further information.

advisories.title: No fencing storage
advisories.description: Visitors are required to bring their own vehicle fencing if they wish to use it and remove it after use. Storage of fencing in Bugaboo Park is not permitted.

advisories.title: Road conditions
advisories.description: Access to Birkenhead Lake is via Blackwater Lake Road which is a backcountry dirt road that can be pitted and rough on older low-riding vehicles.

advisories.title: Ecological Reserve is closed due to the ongoing residual risk of unstable riverbanks and reactivating landslides
advisories.description:
In the interest of public safety, BC Parks has closed this ER until further notice.
Get up-to-date information from other official sources, such as the local regional district, and Drive BC.
You can still visit other BC Parks that remain unaffected. Find other places to visit on the find a park page.

advisories.title: Water is by manual hand pump only, not designed for RV filling
advisories.description:
The water pump at Prudhomme Lake Campground is a manual pump not designed for RV filling. Consider bringing a personal supply of water during your stay.
The nearest sani-stations are:
The Port Edward Municipal Sani-Dump station
Located in Port Edward BC just a few kilometers off highway 16 on the right side of the road
The Prince Rupert Sani-Dump Station
Located off highway 16 in the Industrial Park at Grassy Bay Petro Canada gas station

advisories.title: Boil water advisory in effect
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: Grizzly bears frequent the campground area - securing all food is essential
advisories.description:
Grizzly bears frequent the campground area. Securing all bear attractants is essential.
Wildlife attractants include: Food and drinks, food waste, food packaging, toothpaste, beverage containers, food coolers, dishes and pots, pet food and bowls, BBQs and camp stoves, petroleum products, any scented toiletries, any item that has been used for food preparation.
Secure all attractants in a locked vehicle, hard-sided trailer or bear-proof canister.
Never store food and packs in your tent.
Ensure that your children and pets are always close by.
Pets must be leashed throughout your stay at the park.
Report bear sightings and aggressive wildlife to the Conservation Officer Service RAPP line toll-free at 1-877-952-7277.
What to do if you see a bear
Learn more about bear safety and backcountry etiquette
Stay safe in bear country and help keep bears wild.

advisories.title: Low water levels, be cautious of underwater hazards
advisories.description: Lower water levels may cause underwater hazards to be closer to the surface of Swan Lake. Use caution when launching and operating boats, particularly around the boat launch and beach day-use area.

advisories.title: Day-use gates closed on October 15, walk-in access only
advisories.description: The day-use gates at Jimsmith Lake Park will be closed on October 15 for the winter season. During the winter, visitors are welcome to walk into the park. Please refer back to this website for spring opening dates.

advisories.title: Picnic tables not available in day-use area
advisories.description: Picnic tables will not be available in the day-use areas as they have been removed for maintenance and refinishing. They will be replaced before the gates open in the Spring.

advisories.title: Be aware of post-wildfire hazards
advisories.description:
There are significant risks in areas burned by wildfire. These include:
Unstable trees and branches that could fall
Unstable terrain causing landslides or falling rocks and debris
Increased water runoff causing waterways to rise rapidly, flood, or change course
Ash pits that may be deep and difficult to see
Respiratory damage from soot and charcoal
Hazards may last several years and may be triggered at any time with little or no warning. Be prepared and check post-wildfire hazard reports, if a report is available, for the area before visiting.

advisories.title: Attention climbers, help us learn more about bats!
advisories.description: BC Parks, the Ministry of Water, Land and Resources Stewardship, has partnered with Squamish Access Society to help collect baseline data on bats using cliffs. Bat reports can be made with your phone using the iNaturalist Canada app. BC is home to 15 bat species; half of the species are listed as species at risk. Reports collected will not result in trail closures; these will help us learn more about these species to help with future management and conservation efforts. Learn about bats and other bat programs at bcbats.ca

advisories.title: Trails are impacted due to 2024 storm event
advisories.description:
Trails continue to be assessed for damage and signed for hazards where present. Some trails have been closed.
Check the latest trail conditions report for more information. Please use extra caution during this time.
While assessments are ongoing, unmarked hazards may exist in the park. Please avoid streams, stream banks and steep slopes that may be particularly unstable due to the November 2024 storm event.

advisories.title: Online backcountry registration opening July 1, 2026
advisories.description: Online registration for all backcountry campsites will open on July 1 for arrivals between July 1 and July 15. After this period, permitting will return to the standard two-week rolling booking window.

advisories.title: Increased risk of landslide and flooding in wildfire impacted areas
advisories.description:
While not directly impacted by recent wildfire events, much of the area around Nahatlach Park has recently burned.
Due to severe wildfires in the region, some areas have decreased tree-cover resulting in greater amounts of surface runoff during increased precipitation (rain and snow). This may be exacerbated by hydrophobic soils leading to additional runoff which could overwhelm natural and man-made drainage features. Landslides, debris flows, and debris floods can result, threatening public safety and damaging infrastructure.
All resource road users are advised to check local weather and safety advisories. Drive to the condition of the road and watch for hazards if heading into the backcountry.
For more information on post-wildfire natural hazard risks:

links.title: Landslide and Flooding Risks Due to Wildfires sign (PDF, 3MB)
Landslide and Flooding Risks Due to Wildfires pamphlet (PDF, 5.7MB)

advisories.title: Bridge removed at Joseph Creek Crossing, no passage past this point
Wakes Cove Park is closed to hunting, and the use of motor vehicles - bikes are permitted only on designated roads
Drinking water unavailable due to presence of lead
advisories.description: Due to the presence of lead, drinking water is currently unavailable at Porteau Cove. We request that visitors bring their own potable water when they visit the park. Outhouses and washrooms are still open. Showers are closed for the winter season, and will reopen March 1. We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate your understanding.

advisories.title: Swimming prohibited in the Thompson River
advisories.description: Thompson River waters are dangerously swift, especially in the high water of June and July.

advisories.title: New electric service campsites and new campground amenities
advisories.description: 30 new campsites with power hook-ups have been built at Fintry Park. Reservations for the new electric campsites are available to book starting January 15 at camping.bcparks.ca. Additional campground upgrades include new flush toilet facilities, potable water taps, and service centers with a dishwashing station.

advisories.title: Low water levels may render boat launch unusable
Garibaldi Wilderness Area reservations must be made by phone
advisories.description:
As of January 16, 2025, Garibaldi Wilderness Area reservations must be made by phone.
You can make your reservation by calling 1-800-689-9025 (1-519-858-6161 internationally). For further details, please visit Garibaldi Park Wilderness Camping Area.

advisories.title: There is a year-round fire ban within the park
advisories.description: Fires are not permitted above the high-tide line.

advisories.title: Closure of White Creek trail due to sinkholes
advisories.description: White Creek trail is closed due to seasonal flooding. Sinkholes have been discovered which pose a hazard to visitor safety. The trail is closed until the danger is assessed and resolved.

advisories.title: Cable car out of service
advisories.description: Access to Close-To-The-Edge Cave is currently unavailable as the cable car is out of service.

advisories.title: Trail to Niagara River Falls closed for public safety
advisories.description: The trail to Niagara Falls is closed due to a trail washout. There is no access or alternate route via Gold Mine Trail or the Island Highway parking lot.

advisories.title: Park boundary expanded
advisories.description:
In 2021, BC Parks acquired two properties (including Tribune Bay Campground) to expand Tribune Bay Park on Hornby Island. In the fall of 2024, they were officially added to Tribune Bay Park.
Trail accessibility, along with the water and septic systems, have been improved and more enhancements are being planned. For more information, read about Tribune Bay Park recreation enhancements on the Help Shape BC website.

advisories.title: The Fry Creek Canyon route is no longer classified as a designated route
advisories.description: The Fry Creek and Carney Creek drainages are deemed wilderness areas. Travel to these areas is not recommended. Use at your own risk and route-finding skills are required.

advisories.title: Boil water prior to use
advisories.description:
A hand pump for water is located near the information shelter.
A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory in effect
advisories.description: A permanent boil water advisory is in effect. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory in effect
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: No campfires permitted
advisories.description: Due to dry windy conditions and the risk of soil erosion, campfires are not permitted anywhere within Roscoe Bay Park.

advisories.title: No campfires permitted
advisories.description: Due to dry windy conditions and the risk of soil erosion, campfires are not permitted anywhere within Desolation Sound Marine Park.

advisories.title: Partial trail closures within Prideaux Haven Anchorage
advisories.description: Portions of established trails within Prideaux Haven Anchorage including the Viewpoint Trail and Melanie Cove Beach Trail are now closed off for recreational use due to ecological restoration. Please respect all signs and fencing identifying closure areas.

advisories.title: Drinking water unavailable at Muncho Lake Park due to diesel spill
advisories.description:
On April 7, a diesel spill occurred along Highway 97 North within Muncho Lake Park following a motor vehicle accident involving a transport truck. The extent of contamination is still being assessed, with remediation efforts and water quality monitoring ongoing.
Until further notice, do not drink or treat water from any sources within or around the park. Boiling or filtering water does not remove petrochemical contaminants. Visitors should bring bottled or treated water from outside the park.
For the latest updates, visit the Motor Vehicle Incident Toad River page.

advisories.title: Kinuseo Falls viewing platform closure
advisories.description:
The Kinuseo Falls viewing platform will be closed for the 2026 season. An engineering assessment has determined the structure is no longer safe for public use due to significant structural concerns.
Please refer to the FAQ linked below for more details about the closure.
The trail to the upper viewpoints remains open. However, please note that this trail is considered challenging and features steep drop-offs. Caution is strongly advised.

advisories.title: Dogs must always remain on leash
advisories.description:
BC Parks would like to remind all park visitors that dogs must always remain on leash while visiting Alice Lake Park..
Keeping your dog in control protects your pet, other visitors and their pets, and local wildlife.

advisories.title: Ancient Forest/Chun T’oh Whudujut interpretive centre construction ongoing
advisories.description:
Construction of the Ancient Forest/Chun T’oh Whudujut Interpretive Centre is ongoing. Please expect limited parking and follow all posted signage.
Trail access will remain open; however, some areas may experience temporary closures. Please check back here regularly for updates.
The interpretive centre is part of the Ancient Forest Enhancement Project. For more information, please visit Ancient Forest Enhancement Project on the Lheidli T'enneh website.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory in effect
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water from all hand pumps before use.

advisories.title: Limited tent camping now permitted on a first come, first served basis
advisories.description:
Standalone or ground-based tents are permitted on a first come, first served basis, within the electric fence, in sites 2-8. Cartop tent structures, pop-up trailers, trailers, and van/campers are permitted in the rest of the campground..
Bears are active in the campground and area. The park operator and BC Parks staff are working to maintain safe distances from visitors, and we may limit sites again as needed..
Those with reservations who are planning to use tents, may only maintain their reservation if they are equipped with a hard sided camping structure.

advisories.title: Border access at Hozomeen closed until further notice
advisories.description:
The US National Park Service has indicated that until further notice, the gate located along the Canada/US border at Hozomeen will remain closed; vehicle and foot traffic across the Canada/US border is prohibited and visitors must enter through a designated port of entry.
For backcountry permit questions in North Cascade National Park or the Ross Lake National Recreation Area (USA) please email noca_wilderness@nps.gov. For further information about border crossing, please contact the relevant authority of jurisdiction.

advisories.title: Giovando Lookout closed
advisories.description: Giovando Lookout is closed until further notice.

advisories.title: Be aware of thieves
advisories.description: BC Parks has been made aware of some recent bike thefts in Alice Lake Park. While visiting the park, please ensure to lock up securely and do not leave any valuables unattended or in your vehicle. Report any suspicious activity, theft, or damage to the police.

advisories.title: Contact border services for all border-related matters
advisories.description: BC Parks is unable to advise on any border-related activities taking place in Peace Arch Park. For border-related inquiries, please contact the respective border services agency in either Canada or the United States.

advisories.title: Hummingbird Campground and Spruce Lake South Campground are closed due to hazardous trees
advisories.description: The nearest open campgrounds are at Trigger Lake, Spruce Lake North, and Gun Creek Grassland-Cowboy Camp.

advisories.title: Cathedral Park reopens
advisories.description:
Cathedral Park reopens – June 2026 update
All trails impacted by the fire have now been assessed, cleared, and are open. Please be aware that there will likely be significantly more windfall than normal on the trails for a number of years to come, and it will take longer for BC Parks to have them cleared.
Backcountry camping is available at Quiniscoe Lake campground only. Reservations are required from June 27 to September 12, and can be booked at camping.bcparks.ca. Backcountry camping registration is required outside of these dates.
Frontcountry camping is available at Buckhorn on a first come, first served basis. Ashnola Valley also has recreation sites, as well as the Lower Similkameen Band’s Ashnola Campground.
Lakeview Road, which provides vehicle access to the core area of the park, is open, allowing Cathedral Lakes Lodge to resume lodge and shuttle service operations. Campers at Quiniscoe Lake using the shuttle service must have campsite reservations.
Thank you for your patience as we complete maintenance, repairs, and replacements related to the 2023 Crater Creek wildfire. Lake of the Woods and Pyramid Lake campgrounds are closed while undergoing reconstruction.

advisories.title: Recreation on Tranquille River allowed upstream of the water diversion (dam) only
advisories.description:
Recreational activities in the water are allowed only upstream of the water diversion (dam), which is approximately 2 km north of the trailhead. This recreational closure from the trailhead to the water diversion supports protection of salmon habitat and prevents further degradation of the stream bank.
Various salmon species spawn in the Tranquille River, including threatened interior Fraser Coho (see COSEWIC status report). Coho have been in this river system for many years, but just recently has made a re-emergence in significant numbers within Lac du Bois.
The water diversion enhancement project is ongoing. BC Parks is working with partner agencies to collect data and determine which areas need long-term protection. This includes determining which recreational activities are appropriate amidst climate change.
Salmon are an integral part of a healthy ecosystem and an important cultural and recreational resource. Please do your part by appreciating them from a distance.
The public celebration of the pink salmon, titled 'Pink Palooza at Pine Park,' a multi-agency celebration, was held on September 27, 2025. A fun and interactive event led by many organizations who work to protect the year-round use of the Tranquille River by many species. Expect another event in the fall of 2027!
For further information:
Learn more about the Stream to Sea Program
Check back on this page for updates
Connect with BC Parks and supporting agencies while visiting the park.
Connect with BC Parks at parkinfo@gov.bc.ca.

advisories.title: Wolves frequent the McMicking Beach area and may approach
advisories.description:
Wolves are known to frequent McMicking Beach and the surrounding area. Wolves may be food conditioned, may approach people and camping areas, and may take or damage personal items.
Please follow these important guidelines:
Never feed wolves. Never leave food or scented items inside your tent, stored in your kayak, or unattended. Store food and scented items in secure containers. Pack out what you pack in.
Dogs attract wolves. Leave dogs at home for the safety of the dogs and the wolves.
Maintain a minimum distance of 100 m where possible. Carry bear spray as a deterrent.
Report all wolf encounters to the RAPP Line: 1-877-952-RAPP (7277)
Read the wolf safety guidelines for more information.
Thank you for your cooperation.

advisories.title: Butterfly habitat garden
advisories.description:
BC Parks is creating a butterfly habitat garden at one end of the parking area. This garden will provide habitat and food for many native pollinators, including butterflies, bees, and beetles. The garden will be planted with a wide range of native plant species – including shrubs, a wildflower meadow, grasslands and a milkweed area for Monarch butterflies.
The garden is developing in stages. In spring 2025, the newly created berms were sheet mulched, using layers of cardboard, shredded paper, and leaves. They were covered in plastic for the summer to help break down those composting layers and prevent weeds from establishing. Other areas were covered in plastic to control unwanted grasses and other plants. A couple of areas were planted with some native shrubs.
In the spring of 2026, the remainder of the garden will be planted. With help from local volunteers and staff from the Christina Lake Stewardship Society, the garden will be watered and weeded for the first few years to help it get established. It will take a few years for the garden to fully develop, but with the accessible trail and bench, it will be a great place to explore the variety of native plants and insects that occur here.
BC Parks appreciates the support of the Christina Lake Stewardship Society with this project. We also appreciate the assistance from the Christina Lake Fire Dept for help with the water supply for watering the plantings.

advisories.title: Ross Lake boat launch open for visitor use May 1 to October 15 when water levels permit
advisories.description:
The boat launch at Ross Lake is open for visitor use when Ross Reservoir water levels are sufficiently high to accommodate the safe launching of vessels. During periods of low water, the boat launch will be closed. Full pool for the reservoir is generally considered to be 1,602.5 feet ASL. The boat launch may be difficult to use below 1,595 feet above sea level. Usability of the boat launch will depend on the draught depth of the vessel.
Visitors are advised to check current Ross Reservoir water levels before planning their trip. Visit the U.S. Geological Survey website to view the real‑time Ross Reservoir water level information.
The U.S. National Park Service has indicated the gate located along the Canada–U.S. border at Hozomeen will remain closed until further notice. Vehicle, foot, and boat traffic across the Canada–U.S. border is prohibited, and visitors must enter the United States through a designated port of entry. Ross Reservoir is not a designated port of crossing, and access into the USA via Ross Reservoir is not permitted.
Visitors must observe the clearly demarcated international boundary lines on both sides of Ross Reservoir and must not cross from Canada into the United States at any point during their visit to Skagit Valley Park.
