advisories.title: Alice Lake water quality and aeration project
advisories.description:
BC Parks is working with partners to support the long-term health of Alice Lake and help reduce the risk of cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) blooms.
What's happening?
Cyanobacteria occur naturally in lakes and can sometimes grow quickly and form blooms. Some blooms may produce toxins that can be harmful to people, pets, and wildlife.
After a bloom at Alice Lake in 2024, BC Parks, the Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship, and Vancouver Coastal Health began monitoring lake conditions to better understand what contributes to blooms and how to manage water quality.
New aeration system
BC Parks has installed an aeration system that circulates and mixes lake water. This may help reduce conditions that support cyanobacteria growth.
While the system may help lower the risk of blooms, it will not prevent them entirely. Water-quality monitoring will continue, and the system will be adjusted as needed based on lake conditions and scientific advice.
Working together
The project is a partnership between:
BC Parks, which manages the park and installed the aeration system
The Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship, which provides water-quality monitoring and scientific expertise
Vancouver Coastal Health, which provides public-health guidance
The aeration system was funded through the BC Parks Licence Plate Program.
Visiting Alice Lake
Visitors should continue to follow posted water-quality advisories and closures. BC Parks and its partners will continue monitoring the lake to help guide future management decisions.

Lussier Hot Springs closed
advisories.description:
Lussier Hot Springs is temporarily closed to protect public safety. Earlier this year, staff identified large, dislodged rocks in the upper pool and a compromised retaining wall, increasing the risk of further rockfall. Visitor safety is our top priority, and the site will remain closed until it is assessed and confirmed safe to reopen.
Following the initial closure, BC Parks engaged a professional geotechnical engineer (P.Eng.), whose review confirmed unstable rock features and recommended the area remain closed while mitigation options were evaluated and implemented. Based on those recommendations, material from the damaged retaining wall was repositioned within the upper pool area as a temporary measure to help stabilize the site and support public safety while the pool is closed.
BC Parks is developing a phased reopening plan to support limited access to the hot springs once priority safety measures are in place, consistent with geotechnical recommendations. In parallel, work is underway on longer-term mitigation and rehabilitation options to address slope stability and support safe, sustainable access. Timelines and next steps are still being determined and will be shared as more information becomes available.
This advisory will be updated if any information changes. Until then, the closure remains in place, and the public is asked to respect all signage and safety hazards.

advisories.title: Be prepared for heavier snow conditions in 2026 than typically seen early in the season
advisories.description:
Trail report, June 11, 2026
The hiking trail from Mount Shark looks to be clear of snow until about the warden cabin (Banff National Park), where snow patches begin along with many wet sections. The trail is fully covered in snow by the time you start climbing Assiniboine Pass. Wonder Pass has higher than average snowpack this year, and hikers can expect isothermic conditions. Snow depth at Mount Assiniboine Lodge averaged at 50 cm in addition to Magog Campground.
Special note
Sunshine Village is opening for skiing June 20 to July 5 due to high snowpack levels this year. Visitors accessing Mount Assiniboine Park from Sunshine Meadows should note that gondola/lift access will only be available to skiers during this period. Visitors can expect significant levels of snow at Citadel Pass/Sunshine Meadows Trailhead elevations. Webcams are available at skibanff.com to acquire further information on snowpack conditions.
What visitors need to know
Expect deep snow: Subalpine and alpine terrain may hold 1–2 metres of snow, with soft, unconsolidated layers common during warm periods.
Winter travel equipment is essential: Snowshoes or skis, avalanche‑appropriate gear, and waterproof, insulated clothing are strongly recommended.
Navigation will be challenging: Trail markers, junctions, and bridges may be buried. GPS navigation, maps, and the ability to travel safely in winter terrain are required.
Travel times will be significantly longer: Deep snow and difficult terrain can double or triple normal travel times.
Cabins, campsites, and tent pads may be inaccessible: Snow depth may prevent access to facilities or require digging out tent platforms.
Avalanche hazards may be present: Visitors should check the latest avalanche forecasts and be prepared for changing conditions throughout the day. Please check avalanche.ca for the latest information.
Mount Assiniboine is a remote, high‑elevation wilderness area. Rescue response may be delayed due to weather, snowpack, or aircraft access limitations. Visitors should plan conservatively, travel with partners, and be prepared to turn back if conditions deteriorate. Please continue to check back for seasonal travel updates as conditions improve.

advisories.title: Bears are active in campgrounds at Golden Ears Park
advisories.description:
Wild animals may be attracted to campgrounds by the smell of food, garbage, and other scented items. Minimizing odours and securing all attractants will help you prevent wild animals from looking for food in your campsite.
Watch the Golden Ears bear safety video
All visitors are expected to follow the bear safety code of conduct.
To maintain a safe campsite:
Secure all attractants in a locked vehicle, hard-sided trailer, bear-proof cannister, or bear-resistant locker. Flexible truck bed covers are not secure.
In the backcountry, you can also secure your food in a properly constructed food hang or food cache.
Never leave any food, garbage or other potential attractants in your tent, hammock, backpack, or soft-sided trailer.
Below is a list of common attractants that must be securely stored whenever you’re sleeping or away from your campsite. Ensure attractants are securely stored, even if you’re only gone for one minute.
What are wildlife attractants?
Food (open or sealed)
Garbage, recycling, and food scraps
Coolers (full or empty)
Dishes and pots (clean or dirty)
Pet food and bowls
Bottles and cans (full or empty)
Barbecues and camp stoves (clean or dirty)
Any item used in preparing food
Any item with a smell, such as toiletries, sunscreen, and bug spray
Petroleum products, including motor oil bottles and gasoline or diesel cans
Clothes worn during cooking
Remember the saying: “A fed bear is a dead bear”. This applies to all wild animals, not just bears.
Report bear sightings and aggressive wildlife to the Conservation Officer Service RAPP line toll-free at 1-877-952-7277.
What to do if you see a bear
Learn more about bear safety and backcountry etiquette
Stay safe in bear country and help keep bears wild.

advisories.title: Nuchatlaht Title Area
advisories.description:
The B.C. Government has filed an appeal with the Supreme Court of Canada regarding the April 2026 Court of Appeal Nuchatlaht First Nation Aboriginal title ruling.
For now, the declared title lands are no longer open for public access. Anyone seeking information about access permissions, cultural protocols, or restrictions within the Nuchatlaht declared Aboriginal title area should contact the Nuchatlaht First Nation directly at communications@nuchatlaht.com.
For general park information and updates, including questions about public park access, contact BC Parks at parkinfo@gov.bc.ca.

advisories.title: Large sections of the Stein Valley trail remain impassable and closed due to the impacts of the 2023 wildfire
advisories.description:
In the Lower Valley, beyond Earls Camp, it is impossible to travel further into the park from the west due to many landslides, rockfall events, and hazardous trees. The suspension bridge 12 km from the Lytton trailhead is damaged and closed. The cottonwood cable car has been removed. Due to this, thru-hiking is not possible or advised.
There is some access to the park from the Lizzie Lake and Blowdown Pass areas. However, this is only recommended for experienced backcountry users who are aware of all risks and hazards. Hazards in the park may include danger trees (unstable trees that can fall over without warning) and increased tree obstructions on trails, irregular trail surfaces and increased potential for landslides and/or rockfalls.

advisories.title: Grizzly and black bears live here! Avoid bear encounters
advisories.description:
Report bear sightings and aggressive wildlife to the Conservation Officer Service RAPP line toll-free at 1-877-952-7277.
What to do if you see a bear
Learn more about bear safety and backcountry etiquette
Stay safe in bear country and help keep bears wild.

advisories.title: Limited parking available
advisories.description: Callaghan Lake receives high numbers of visitors on weekends and holidays. Parking in the day-use and camping area is limited, and the site may become congested during peak times.

advisories.title: Road closure, Highway 742 (Canmore Hill to Kananaskis)
advisories.description: Park visitors looking to access Mount Assiniboine Park via Mount Shark Trailhead and/or Heli Pad should note that Highway 742 is closed at Canmore Hill and not expected to reopen until Mid-July. If park visitors are planning to fly from Mount Shark, it is recommended to give an additional 2 hours of travel time from Canmore to the Mount Shark Helipad via Highway 40 (south through Kananaskis). Please check Alberta 511 detour information and closure updates.

advisories.title: Clean all boats and equipment to prevent the spread of aquatic invasive species
advisories.description:
Thank you for your helping prevent invasive species from spreading into this park.
Before you arrive:
Make sure your boat and all your equipment and clothing are completely clean and completely dry
This includes waders, boots, fishing rods and lines
Before storage or moving to another body of water:
Drain all water from your boat, and remove all plants, animals, and mud
Clean and dry your boat and all equipment and clothing
Wash your pets if they have been swimming
Report sightings of invasive species
Never move plants, animals, mud, or water between water bodies. This includes all fish and fish parts.
Learn more about invasive aquatic species and how to spot them

advisories.title: Trail advisory notice for Lindeman/Greendrop Lake Trail
advisories.description:
The Lindeman/Greendrop Lake Trail is now open and available for access.
Portions of Sxótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Park experienced impacts from severe winter winds, resulting in extensive tree damage. The trail has been cleared up to Lindeman Lake, including the backcountry campsite at this location. Four tent pads are currently available; however, one pad was damaged and requires replacement.
Beyond Lindeman Lake, sections of trail still contain fallen trees. While these do not pose a significant safety risk, hikers should expect to navigate over, under, or around obstacles. Travel beyond Lindeman Lake may be slower and more challenging.
Clearing of remaining wind-felled trees will continue throughout the 2026 season.

advisories.title: Fang Trail temporarily closed
advisories.description: Due to a rock slide and debris, the Fang Trail is temporarily closed until further investigations can be conducted.

advisories.title: Adams River Gorge Trail is now open
advisories.description:
The Adams River Gorge Trail is now open and safely accessible to both pedestrians and cyclists.
Please be aware that the Ancient Pictograph protection fence and interpretive signage are currently under reconstruction following damage from the 2023 Bush Creek East wildfire. For your safety and to help protect these irreplaceable cultural sites, do not enter the fenced area and avoid disturbing the pictographs.
Thank you for respecting the land, its history, and the ongoing restoration work.

advisories.title: Bear safe food storage lockers available
advisories.description: Available for use by cyclists, motorcyclists, and anyone without bear-proof storage for wildlife attractants. Located in the campground between sites 1 and 2. Users are asked to tidy their locker as needed.

advisories.title: Bear safe food storage lockers available
advisories.description: Available for use by cyclists, motorcyclists, and anyone without bear-proof storage for wildlife attractants. Located in the campground beside the central information board, and water tap. Users are asked to tidy their locker as needed.

advisories.title: Trailhead access
advisories.description:
Vehicle requirement: Only 4WD, high-clearance vehicles are recommended for the South Thunderbird Forest Service Road at this time. It is not suitable for 2WD or low-clearance vehicles.
Active hazard: Approximately 500 meters from the start of the road, a section is actively sloughing away. This area is marked with traffic cones and flagging tape.
The overall road is in rough condition, and other unmarked hazards may be present. Drive with extreme caution.

advisories.title: Alberta road closures affecting park access
advisories.description: Access to Elk Lakes Park from the north through Peter Lougheed Provincial Park is currently being impacted by road closures in Alberta. Visitors planning a trip into Elk Lakes Park should check 511.alberta.ca for the most up to date road information.

advisories.title: Dogs only permitted in day-use and camping area
advisories.description:
Dogs and other domestic animals are only permitted in the day-use and camping area.
Dogs are not permitted in the Cirque Lake Basin. This helps to protect grizzly habitat, prevent bear encounters, and maintain park values.
Dogs in boats or other floatation devices are allowed.

advisories.title: Canyon Loop Trail reconstruction being underway
advisories.description:
Canyon Loop Trail remains closed with reconstruction of bridges, staircases, and a pit toilet underway.
For your safety, please respect trail closure signage and directions from construction crews. Keep a safe distance away from construction zones. This project is expected to wrap up mid-November 2026.

advisories.title: Cash is the only form of payment accepted onsite
advisories.description: For first come, first served camping, you must pay park staff in cash, at the campground. Staff will come around to collect fees.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: High water and bridge damage at stream crossings
advisories.description: Use caution at alpine and sub alpine streams where high water flow and bridges damaged in 2025 may make crossing difficult. Find safe places to cross even if they are off the trail.

advisories.title: No water available at Westside Groupsite
advisories.description: Water is unavailable at the Westside Groupsite, the hand pump is out of service. Water can be obtained in Entrance Bay Campground, or other campgrounds, within the park.

advisories.title: Early season conditions persist (high stream flow at crossings)
advisories.description: Early season conditions persist in sub-alpine and alpine areas of the park. Some bridges impacted by natural events in 2025 have yet to be replaced on creek crossings and visitors need to seek areas, off trail at times, for safe crossings.

advisories.title: Summalo Grove closure
advisories.description: Sumallo Grove day-use area is currently closed while contractors work to replace the foot bridge over the Skagit river. This work is anticipated to be completed by the end of October.

advisories.title: Treat water before use along North Coast Trail
advisories.description:
BC Parks is advising all visitors to the North Coast Trail of a potential risk of waterborne illness in natural water sources along the route.
Backcountry water sources, including streams, rivers, and lakes, may contain harmful bacteria, parasites, or other pathogens that can cause illness if consumed untreated. Environmental conditions, wildlife activity, and seasonal factors can increase this risk.
All water collected from natural sources must be treated before drinking. BC Parks recommends that all hikers plan ahead and carry appropriate, and multiple, water treatment options when traveling on the North Coast Trail.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.title: Chatterbox dock repaired
advisories.description: The previously noted potential navigational hazard on the shoreside of the Chatterbox dock has been repaired and vessel travel is once again safe for park visitors.

advisories.description:

You can still visit other BC Parks that remain unaffected by wildfire. Find other places to visit on the find a park page.

advisories.title: Goldstream Nature House closed
advisories.description: The Goldstream Nature House is currently closed due to a recent power failure. We appreciate your patience and look forward to fully restoring services as soon as possible.

advisories.title: Low water levels, boat launch at West Campground closed
advisories.description: Due to low water level, the boat launch at the Roche Lake West Campground is currently closed. Please use the boat launch at Roche Lake North Campground.

advisories.title: Blue-green algae monitoring
advisories.description:
Visitors to Lac La Hache Park are advised that a suspected blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) bloom has been observed in the lake.
Blue-green algae can produce toxins that may pose health risks to people and animals. As a precaution, park users should avoid swimming or wading where algae is present, keep pets away from the water and shoreline, refrain from drinking lake water and avoid any water activities that may result in contact with the algae. Visitors are encouraged to use caution until further notice.

advisories.title: Log jam in river, be prepared for portage around
advisories.description: There is an impassable log jam at the confluence of the Stikine River and Chukachida River. Users need to be prepared for a portage around.

advisories.title: Bear activity in area
advisories.description:
A grizzly bear has been reported frequenting this area as of August 3, 2026. BC Parks is advising all visitors to exercise caution and remain alert when recreating in the park, as bears are actively foraging at this time of year. For your safety:
Make noise to avoid surprising a bear
Avoid trails with dense vegetation where visibility is limited
Keep children close at all times
Keep dogs leashed and under control
Travel in groups whenever possible
Carry bear spray and know how to use it
Avoid the use of headphones so you can remain aware of your surroundings
Avoid high-speed activities, such as biking or running, that may startle a bear
Never approach or feed a bear
Ensure all attractants (food, garbage and scented products) are managed appropriately
If you encounter a bear, remain calm, give it plenty of space, and leave the area safely.
Report bear sightings and aggressive wildlife to the Conservation Officer Service RAPP line toll-free at 1-877-952-7277.
What to do if you see a bear
Learn more about bear safety and backcountry etiquette
Stay safe in bear country and help keep bears wild.

advisories.title: No running water in day-use area
advisories.description:
Due to a recent power failure, there is currently no running water in the Goldstream day-use area. As a result, flush toilets and water taps are temporarily unavailable. Portable toilets have been placed on site until electrical service is restored.
We appreciate your patience and apologize for the inconvenience as we work to restore these services as quickly as possible.

advisories.title: Prospector's Trail partial closure
advisories.description:
A short section of the Prospector's Trail has been closed due to a bank failure. The closure affects approximately the first 200 m of the trail from the Finlayson Arm Road trailhead. Visitors can now access the Prospector’s Trail by using the Mount Finlayson Trail, which reconnects with the Prospector's Trail approximately 500 m east of the closure.
Please obey all closure signs and remain on designated trails.

advisories.title: Western Road access to park - no stopping
advisories.description: Northern access to Fintry Park is available again, after recent wildfires in the area. While Westside Road is open, there is no stopping between Irish Creek Road and Komasket Road. Visitors can check DriveBC for further information.

advisories.title: Do not consume water
advisories.description: Monck Park visitors are advised not to consume any water at this time. Thank you for your patience and understanding while we work to resolve the issue.

advisories.title: Ecological Reserve re-opened but hazards still exist
advisories.description:
Access not recommended, use caution in wildfire-affected areas.
There are significant risks in areas burned by wildfire. These include:
Unstable trees and branches that could fall
Unstable terrain causing landslides or falling rocks and debris
Increased water runoff causing waterways to rise rapidly, flood, or change course
Ash pits that may be deep and difficult to see
Respiratory damage from soot and charcoal
Hazards may last several years and may be triggered at any time with little or no warning. Be prepared and check post-wildfire hazard reports, if a report is available, for the area before visiting.

advisories.description:

The bridge will be closed while contractors replace the structure. There will be no public access on this section of trail during construction. Park visitors are asked to stay away from construction equipment and respect trail closure signage.

advisories.title: Road closure between Deerpelt and Nazko Lake, Deerpelt Lake parking area closed
advisories.description: The road between Deerpelt Lake and Nazko Lake, as well as the main parking area at Deerpelt Lake, are closed until further notice. Visitors accessing the canoe chain must start at Deerpelt Lake and park at Deerpelt Lake Campsite.

advisories.description: Due to the recent park closure due to wildfire activity in the surrounding area, the Downing Campground watersystem is under a Do Not Consume Order until water sample analysis is completed and assessed.

advisories.title: Wildfire risk reduction activities occurring until March 2027 - trail closures in place
advisories.description:
Wildfire risk reduction (WRR) activities will be taking place in Dragon Mountain Park, starting as early as September 14 and lasting until March 31, 2027.
The goal is to reduce wildfire risk to critical infrastructure and support public safety. These activities also support more resilient landscapes in the Dragon Mountain area and are part of responsible park stewardship in a changing climate.
Visitors can expect the following activities:
Vegetation management and selective thinning - this will be completed by both hand crews and equipment operators
Pruning of lower branches (ladder fuel reduction)
Surface fuel clean-up and removal of woody debris
Piling and controlled burning of debris (pile burning)
Temporary trail closures and area restrictions
Temporary road closures and equipment working on Durrell Road
These activities are carefully planned and implemented to support ecosystem health and increase wildfire resilience.
Trail Closures: Several bike trails overlap with WRR treatments. The following trail closures will be in effect from September 14, 2026 – March 31, 2027: Dwarves, Hewitt and Rockasaurus. These closures are in place for both worker and public safety - please respect all signage.

advisories.title: Buttle Lake Campground Closure from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027
advisories.description:
Capital upgrades of the Buttle Lake Campground are scheduled October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027. Construction activities will be underway during this time to improve campsites and to repair campground roads and shoulders. For worker and public safety, please avoid all construction locations and equipment working on site.
All day-use areas and walking trails are accessible through winter months in the remainder of the park. Park visitors are also reminded that the Ralph River Campground remains open for camping through the month of October.
Thank you for your cooperation.

advisories.title: Park is partially closed, trail access impacted
advisories.description:
Portions of the park are partially closed for public health and safety. The trails below are closed due to proximity to the fire boundary and access:
Tyaughton Creek Trailhead
Tyaughton Creek Trailhead from trailhead to WD junction
Casstle Pass Trail
Relay Creek Trail
Little Paradise Creek Trail
In the interest of public safety, BC Parks has partially closed this park until further notice.
Get up-to-date information from other official sources, such as the BC Wildfire Service (BCWS), the local regional district, and Drive BC.
You can still visit other BC Parks that remain unaffected by wildfire. Find other places to visit on the find a park page.

advisories.title: Blue-green algae advisory issued for Alice Lake
advisories.description:
Vancouver Coastal Health has issued an advisory for Alice Lake due to a suspected bloom of cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) detected in the lake. Lab testing is underway to confirm.
Exposure to toxins produced by cyanobacteria may cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or fever in humans and pets. Other symptoms from contact with contaminated water include skin rashes and irritation of the ears and eyes.
People and pets should not swim in water until further notice.
Anyone who comes into contact with a cyanobacterial bloom should rinse off with a source of clean, uncontaminated water immediately after exposure.
To learn more about cyanobacteria, go to What are cyanobacteria (blue-green algae)?
Alice Lake Park’s drinking water system is serviced by wells which are not impacted by this notice.

advisories.title: Boil water advisory in effect
advisories.description: A boil water advisory is in effect until further notice. Boil, filter, or treat water before use.

advisories.description:

advisories.title: Use caution in wildfire-affected areas
advisories.description:
Over the past couple years there have been multiple fires within Itcha Ilgachuz Park. If you're in a prior burn, watch for hazards.
There are significant risks in areas burned by wildfire. These include:
Unstable trees and branches that could fall

advisories.description:
Visitors are cautioned about recent cougar activity on the Bedwell Trail. Use caution and be vigilant when recreating in this area.

advisories.title: Boat launch temporarily closed due to low water
Sani-station water out of service - dump with care
advisories.description:
The sani-station facility's water is out of service.
Please dump with care and bring your own water for cleanup.
Efforts are underway to replace the generator system.

advisories.title: Juan de Fuca Marine Trail closed from Bear Beach to Chin Beach
advisories.description:
Juan de Fuca partial trail closure:
Juan de Fuca Marine Trail is closed between Bear Beach and Chin Beach due to a slope failure. Both Bear Beach and Chin Beach remain open; however, access between the sites is not permitted. There are no alternate routes available. BC Parks is currently assessing the damage and will work to re-open the trail in its entirety as quickly as possible.

advisories.title: Trail work underway from November 4 to 9
advisories.description:
Trail work will take place in Tribune Bay Park from November 4 to 9.
The trail work includes armouring of the trail edges between the day-use parking lot and the picnic shelter, and improving the connecting trail surface.
During construction, a portion of the parking lot and the trail to the picnic shelter will be closed. Parking and access to the park will remain available. Visitors can access the picnic shelter by walking east along the beach.

advisories.title: Diamond Head area - winter conditions
advisories.description:
This area can be reached via a narrow winding mountain road and visitors should expect snow, ice, and steep grades. Vehicles must be equipped with tire chains beyond the chain-up area, as per posted signage or direction by staff. “Snow socks” or spike belts are not considered chains. Failure to comply may result in a $115 fine and/or eviction from the park.
Road conditions may require visitors to put on chains at or before the park boundary along Ring Creek FSR. Park visitors are urged to drive to the road conditions to keep themselves and other vehicles safe.
Vehicles blocking snow removal equipment on the road will be towed at owners’ expense. Grader requires minimum 20 feet of road width.
No parking on Ring Creek Road. Vehicles will be towed.

advisories.title: Singing Pass/Spearhead area - winter access
advisories.description:
Popular backcountry ski touring areas include the Garibaldi Neve Traverse, Singing Pass, musical bumps and the Spearhead-Fitzsimmons Traverse. These trips require advanced skills, advanced planning and good weather conditions.
Consider parking, access to trailheads and lifts, backcountry access routes, required safety equipment, training and trip planning prior to travel.
Skiers and snowboarders re-entering Whistler Blackcomb ski area boundaries from the backcountry should check in with patrol (604 905-2324) or the Terrain Status Map linked below for up-to-date avalanche conditions and terrain closures.
Trip planning resources:
Whistler Blackcomb backcountry
Whistler Blackcomb Terrain Status Map
Avalanche Canada Trip Planner
Whistler parking
Spearhead Huts
AdventureSmart.ca

advisories.title: Cheakamus Lake trailhead access not plowed in the winter
advisories.description:
Cheakamus Lake Road (7 km gravel road access to Cheakamus Lake trailhead) is not plowed in winter which impacts vehicle access to the trailhead.
Park visitors planning to visit this area in winter should be prepared for a longer approach using snowshoe or ski equipment. Parking is available at the Whistler interpretive forest car park just off Highway 99.

advisories.title: Rubble Creek trailhead access via Daisy Lake Rd - winter conditions
advisories.description: This road is plowed after priority highways – service may be delayed during winter months. Please drive at your own risk and prepare for ice, snow, and narrow sections with oncoming vehicles. Use of a 4x4 vehicle with high clearance, winter tires and tire chains is recommended. Parking is not permitted near the Daisy Lake hydro dam access and anywhere blocking snow plow access.

advisories.title: Winter conditions across Garibaldi Park
advisories.description:
Prepare for snowy winter conditions and avalanche hazards across Garibaldi Park during winter months. Most hiking trails are covered in snow, making route finding difficult. Visitors should have appropriate equipment, experience, and training for winter travel.
Winter road conditions are also present. Ensure your vehicle is properly equipped with winter tires and emergency supplies. Campers should be prepared to winter camp as tent pads may be under snow. It is recommended to travel with micro-spikes and/or snowshoes. We recommend animal-proof storage containers as food hangs and bear caches may be inaccessible due to snow height.

advisories.title: Wedgemount Lake winter conditions and trail work
advisories.description:
A contractor is on site carrying out trail work. Trail surfaces may be uneven.
Winter conditions are now in effect, and visitors should be familiar with backcountry and winter travel and safety requirements.
Operations on site are expected to be active until November 15, 2026.

advisories.title: Gruchy's Trail flooded and closed
advisories.description: Gruchy’s Beach Trail is prone to flooding from Williams Creek. Recent rainfall and downstream debris jams may result in unsafe water levels and hazardous conditions. Use caution and consider an alternate trail nearby, such as Gunsight Lake or Clearwater Lakes.

advisories.title: Wildfire Risk Reduction project
advisories.description:
Wildfire risk reduction (WRR) activities will take place at Green Lake Park - Sunset View, between October 26 and December 18, 2026.
The goal is to reduce wildfire risk to park values and support public safety. These activities also support more resilient landscapes in the Green Lake area and are part of responsible park stewardship in a changing climate.
Visitors can expect the following activities:
Selective thinning of coniferous trees
Pruning of lower branches (ladder fuel reduction)
Surface fuel clean-up and removal of woody debris
Piling and controlled burning of debris (pile burning)
Temporary area restrictions and/or traffic restrictions
These activities will be completed by hand crews. Pile burning will only occur under appropriate venting and weather conditions. Please obey all worksite signage to keep you and crews safe.
This WRR project has been carefully planned and will be implemented to support ecosystem health and increase wildfire resilience.

advisories.title: Trail closed for safety and to prevent erosion
advisories.description:
Due to an unstable bank, the southern lagoon trail, indicated by the red circle on the map, is closed for safety and to prevent further erosion.
The Gray Peninsula loop trail may now only be accessed via the northern route indicated by the green arrows.

advisories.description:

advisories.title: Giovando Lookout repairs underway
advisories.description:
Repairs to the Giovando Lookout are currently underway following a condition assessment of the structure. As part of these improvements, the facility will be modified to enhance safety, durability, and extend the lifespan of the facility.
Visitors are advised that access to the lookout area may be restricted during construction. For your safety, please obey all posted signs, barriers, and directions from work crews.
Thank you for your patience and cooperation as we complete these important upgrades.

advisories.title: Use caution in wildfire-affected areas
advisories.description:
There are significant risks in areas that have been burned by wildfire. These include:
Unstable trees and branches that could fall
Unstable terrain causing landslides or falling rocks and debris
Increased water runoff causing waterways to rise rapidly, flood, or change course
Ash pits that may be difficult to see
Respiratory damage from breathing soot and charcoal
Hazards may last several years and may be triggered at any time with little or no warning.

advisories.title: Infrastructure damage at Dewar Creek Hot Springs
advisories.description:
The valve controls at Dewar Creek Hot Springs have sustained damage and may currently be non-functional. Visitors choosing to use the hot spring pool under current conditions must exercise extra caution, as water temperatures may be unregulated.
Members of the public are strictly prohibited from tampering with, altering, or attempting unauthorized repairs on any park infrastructure. Recent unauthorized attempts have worsened the failure and compounded existing damage.
Authorized procurement and repair work are being planned.

The closure areas are shown in red in the attached map.
Please respect all closure signage and instructions from contractors and BC Parks staff on site.

advisories.title: Singing Creek and Cheakamus campgrounds closed until further notice
advisories.description:
Singing Creek and Cheakamus campgrounds are closed, and reservations are unavailable until further notice.
BC Parks staff assessed these campgrounds following the early November atmospheric river event and identified damage at these sites that prevents reopening the campgrounds at this time. BC Parks will work on reopening these campgrounds when the damage has been repaired or hazards mitigated.
The area remains open for day-use, however, visitors should be prepared for impacted facilities and downed trees.

advisories.title: Trail closure due to Trout Creek Restoration Project
advisories.description:
The trail along Trout Creek, on the west side of Highway 97, will be temporarily closed for construction beginning November 16, 2026. Construction is expected to be completed by the end of January 2027.
This work is part of the Trout Creek Restoration Project, a watershed restoration initiative led by the Penticton Indian Band in partnership with the Okanagan Nation Alliance and the Trout Creek Restoration Initiative Steering Committee. The project will restore floodplain connectivity, improve fish and wildlife habitat, enhance salmon spawning areas, and support long-term ecosystem health in Trout Creek.
BC Parks supports this collaborative effort and appreciates visitors' patience during construction. Please follow all posted closures and signage for your safety.

Unstable trees and branches that could fall
Unstable terrain causing landslides or falling rocks and debris
Increased water runoff causing waterways to rise rapidly, flood, or change course

Respiratory damage from soot and charcoal
Hazards may last several years and may be triggered at any time with little or no warning. Be prepared and check post-wildfire hazard reports, if a report is available, for the area before visiting.

advisories.title: Trail closed due to road closure
advisories.description:
Notice: The Beef Trail Road that provides the only vehicle access to the recreation trail is currently closed to support a Motor Vehicle Hunting Closed Area (MVHCA) under the Wildlife Act. It is anticipated the gate at the start of the Beef Trail Road on the north side of Highway 20 will remain closed throughout hunting season, so there will be no vehicle access to the recreation trail during this time.
For more detailed information on the specific areas where motor vehicles are closed for hunting, individuals can refer to the Wildlife Act Motor Vehicle Prohibition Regulation and the Hunting and Trapping Regulations Synopsis. These resources provide comprehensive details on the regulations and maps outlining the closed areas.

As of May 15, 2025, this site is closed for safety reasons until further notice.
Cedar Lake Recreation Site near Campbell River will be closed from mid-July to mid-August as the Blackwater FSR access will require closure during a Western toadlet migration. The exact dates will depend on the migration start and end. For more information and updates, see Campbell River road safety information.

advisories.title: Site closed due to bridge outage
advisories.description: The Spirit Lake Trail is closed at the Mid-Mission Creek bridge located approximately 700 m from the trailhead due to public safety concerns with the bridge structure at that location. Trail users may still access and enjoy the first 700 m of trail from the trailhead; however, the bridge closure prevents access to the remainder of the trail beyond the bridge.
